meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 8, 2012 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners welcomed Boy Scout Troop 451, received a Golden Leaf Award of Merit for the Southwest Durham Regional Library renovation, and voted unanimously (5-0) to suspend the rules to hear urgent public comment from Lincoln Apartments residents facing an October 31 utility shutoff and displacement. The Board approved the September 24 minutes and non-pulled Consent Items 5A and 5C (5-0), opened and considered a request to continue the East Club at Geer Street plan amendment (A1100007) and rezoning (Z1100019) to December 10 pending City Council annexation evaluation, and acted on three consent items pulled by citizen Victoria Peterson. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved Item 5B (grant administrative sign-off authority for housing rehabilitation paperwork), unanimously (5-0) approved Item 5D (a $400,000 CDBG scattered-site housing grant ordinance #13BCC000029 with an added proviso requiring administrator Wooten Company to conduct outreach to Durham firms and preferred vendors), and approved Item 5E (assigning Section 179D courthouse tax deductions to O'Brien/Atkins Associates) by voice vote with no recorded opposition (transcript ASR misrenders the tally as '4 to 3 were' on the five-member board). Before adjourning, commissioners heard emotional testimony from Lincoln Apartments tenants and directed DSS Director Michael Becketts and Deputy Manager Drew Cummings to provide daily updates.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Scout Welcome, Golden Leaf Award, and Rule Suspension for Lincoln Apartments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page welcomed Boy Scout Troop 451 from Westminster Presbyterian Church. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presented a Golden Leaf Award of Merit for Sustainable Properties won by Durham County for the Southwest Durham Regional Library renovation. The Board also voted to suspend its rules and add an agenda item to hear two Lincoln Apartments residents.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 24, 2012 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the September 24, 2012 regular session minutes as written.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Non-Pulled Items 5A and 5C)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson pulled Items 5B, 5D, and 5E for separate discussion; the Board unanimously approved remaining Items 5A and 5C.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearings: East Club at Geer Street Plan Amendment (A1100007) and Zoning (Z1100019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin and applicant counsel Dan Jewell (representing John Turner) requested continuing both public hearings to December 10, 2012 so the applicant could evaluate City Council's October 15 decision and assemble a potential voluntary annexation petition. Chair Page opened the public hearings to keep them open for continuation.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5B: County Manager Administrative Sign-Off Authority for Housing Rehab Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton explained that the state-recommended resolution lets the County Manager sign off on routine $1,000-$1,500 administrative bills within previously authorized $40,000-$50,000 housing rehab project budgets to speed turnaround.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5D: Grant Project Ordinance #13BCC000029 ($400,000 CDBG Scattered-Site Housing Grant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson urged local contractor participation and questioned CDBG rules on county housing projects. Staff clarified the $400,000 NC Department of Commerce grant breakdown (including $8,000 clearance and $173,000 private dwelling reconstruction) and noted the Wooten Company of Raleigh was the sole bidder across two solicitations. Commissioners adopted the ordinance with an explicit proviso requiring Wooten Company to work with County Purchasing to conduct outreach to Durham firms and preferred vendors.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5E: Assignment of Section 179D Tax Deduction to O'Brien/Atkins Associates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson requested a breakdown list regarding assigning the Section 179D tax deduction for the new Durham County courthouse to O'Brien/Atkins Associates. Following brief comment, the Board approved the item by voice vote without recorded dissent.

agenda_items.title: Special Public Comment: Lincoln Apartments Displacement and Utility Shutoff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lincoln Apartments residents Bernadette Turner and Larry Carter described an impending October 31 water and utility shutoff threatening to displace elderly, disabled, and medically vulnerable tenants as well as children and NCCU students, some of whom had lived there over 30 years. Chair Page noted DSS Director Michael Becketts and Deputy Manager Drew Cummings were actively working on relocation/assistance and asked staff to provide daily updates to the Board.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Board rules to add public comment from two Lincoln Apartments residents to the regular session agenda.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved non-pulled consent items 5A and 5C.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized County Manager sign-off on routine housing rehab grant paperwork within authorized grant caps.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $400,000 2011 CDBG Scattered-Site Housing Grant ordinance with a proviso directing Wooten Company to partner with County Purchasing on outreach to Durham firms and preferred vendors.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided over the October 1, 2012 work session in the excused absence of Chair Michael D. Page, opening by deleting the closed session from the agenda and noting no citizens signed up to speak. Commissioners received a presentation on the Research Triangle Park (RTP) Master Plan outlining plans for denser mixed-use nodes (starting with a northern Durham County transit hub near IBM and RTI, followed by Park Center), an update from the Museum of Life and Science on new interactive nature and wind-water-rock exhibits, and a transportation briefing from Andy Henry on the 2040 Metropolitan Transportation Plan—including express bus service for northern Durham and East End Connector connections ahead of a November 14 public hearing. Planning staff also previewed Text Amendment TC1100015 creating the UC-2 zoning district for North Carolina Central University ahead of the October 22 public hearing, and commissioners reviewed board directives and October 22 county brand launch logistics with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow convened the work session, noted Chair Michael D. Page was excused, and deleted the closed session from the agenda. No citizens signed up for the citizen comments period.

agenda_items.title: Research Triangle Park (RTP) Master Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Research Triangle Foundation representatives Bob and Liz presented the new Master Plan for the 7,000-acre park, emphasizing collaborative public spaces, authentic local retail, and three future higher-intensity hubs—beginning with a mixed-use transit node in northern Durham County near IBM/Syngenta/RTI and Park Center near the Radisson. Commissioners discussed light rail alignment, GoPass transit incentives, and future UDO zoning updates to attract millennial talent.

agenda_items.title: Museum of Life and Science Capital and Exhibit Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Museum leadership outlined attendance growth and major upcoming exhibits: a pedestrian tunnel under the train tracks into a forested nature-climbing, water, and sound play area within the train loop, and an expansion of the Catch the Wind exhibit into 'Wind, Water, and Rock.'

agenda_items.title: 2040 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) and Comprehensive Transportation Plan Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Henry reviewed air quality conformity modeling schedules (targeting December draft approval and April adoption) and regional projects including East End Connector links to NC 55 and Alston Avenue. Responding to Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's questions about northern Durham congestion along Roxboro Road, staff noted express bus service is planned rather than fixed rail, and commissioners noted the November 14 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Preview: University and College Zoning District UC-2 Text Amendment (TC1100015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Aaron Cain and an NCCU representative previewed TC1100015 establishing the UC-2 zoning district for North Carolina Central University and other public universities, following Fayetteville Street corridor and historic district updates. Staff explained the 75-foot transitional use area (1:1 setback-to-height ratio) and greater internal campus flexibility, noting Planning Commission's 12-0 recommendation, City Council's unanimous September 4 approval, and extensive community outreach ahead of the October 22 BOCC public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Review, Recruitment Video, and County Brand Reveal Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed pending Board directives (including workforce job-readiness partnerships), discussed a new boards/commissions recruitment video, and confirmed three October 22 launch events for the new Durham County brand (9:30 a.m. employee event, 11:30 a.m. Durham Central Park community event, and 7:00 p.m. regular meeting).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 24, 2012 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners issued proclamations declaring October 2012 as Big Sweep Month and October 1-5, 2012 as Minority Enterprise Development Week, and unanimously (5-0) approved the September 4 and September 10 minutes as well as Consent Agenda Items A-O. Following public hearings with no opposing speakers, the Board unanimously (5-0) adopted UDO Text Amendment TC1100009 (permitting off-premises wayfinding and non-residential entry signs up to 16 square feet), UDO Text Amendment TC1200001 (Technical Changes #7), and a CDBG grant application to help address Rougemont groundwater contamination. Commissioners also discussed deferring a Workforce Development Board private-sector appointment to November 26 to clarify recruitment language and target major businesses, appointed Delores Campbell Stevenson by ballot to a board vacancy, excused Chair Michael D. Page from the October 1 work session (5-0), and entered closed session for economic development discussions (5-0) before adjourning with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and read standard announcements regarding county television rebroadcasts and volunteer board/commission recruitment.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 4 Work Session and September 10 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved the minutes of the September 4, 2012 work session and September 10, 2012 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: October 2012 as Big Sweep Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board proclaimed October 2012 as Big Sweep Month, presented to Soil Conservation Education Coordinator Jennifer Brooks of the Durham Soil and Water Conservation District, who highlighted litter's impacts on business attraction, tourism, and public health.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Minority Enterprise Development (MED) Week (October 1-5, 2012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation designating October 1-5, 2012 as Minority Enterprise Development Week, presented to Pamela Gales, highlighting Durham County's MWBE ordinance, good-faith contracting efforts, and technical assistance for minority and women business owners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No consent items were pulled; commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A through O.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Off-Premises Wayfinding and Entry Signs (TC1100009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1100009, a privately initiated text amendment allowing off-premises wayfinding and non-residential entry signs under an approved signage plan, incorporating a JCCPC recommendation reducing maximum wayfinding sign size from 24 to 16 square feet (Planning Commission 11-0). No speakers signed up for the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Technical Changes #7 (TC1200001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC1200001, the seventh package of UDO technical revisions covering floodplain processes, watershed boundary interpretations, minor use-table edits, accessory structures, and building placement standards (Planning Commission 9-4; City Council approved). No speakers signed up for the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Second Public Hearing: CDBG Grant Application for Rougemont Groundwater Issue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Drew Cummings and Community Development Project Coordinator Warren Wooten conducted the second required public hearing (following an August 13 hearing and Citizens Advisory Committee briefing) to submit an early-October CDBG grant application supporting a community well system to address Rougemont groundwater contamination. No speakers signed up.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Excusal of Chair Page from October 1 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed deferring a Workforce Development Board private-sector slot until November 26 to clarify job-posting wording ('private sector business') and recruit major business representatives, and voted by ballot to select Delores Campbell Stevenson for a board vacancy. The Board also voted to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the October 1 work session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Business or Industry Location/Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location/expansion, returning to open session at 02:46:11 to report staff direction had been provided before adjourning at 9:48 p.m.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of September 4 work session and September 10 regular session.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted text amendment allowing off-premises wayfinding (16 sq ft max) and entry signs subject to signage plans.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment TC1200001 — Technical Changes #7
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted seventh set of UDO technical changes.

votes.item_title: CDBG Grant Application for Rougemont Groundwater / Community Water System
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved submission of CDBG grant application to the state for the Rougemont community water system following second public hearing.

votes.item_title: Excusal of Chair Michael D. Page from October 1, 2012 Work Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Formally excused Chair Michael D. Page from attending the October 1 work session.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; returned at 02:46:11 with direction provided to staff.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 10, 2012 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners introduced new Department of Social Services Director Michael Becketts (appointed August 6 from Baltimore) and presented resolutions honoring the late Joyce Clayton Nichols—the nation's first woman and first African American woman physician assistant—and London Olympic volleyball silver medalist Megan Hodge. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved the August 27 minutes and Consent Agenda Items A-Q (eliminating Item I and amending Item P to appoint Drew Cummings to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), with Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow highlighting over $500,000 in annual savings from a city-county contract negotiated by General Services. Following a public hearing, the Board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve in principle up to $17 million in charter school revenue bonds issued through the Wisconsin-based Public Finance Authority for Voyager Academy/Voyager Foundation, and heard an informational briefing on two city historic landmark applications (including East Durham Graded School/Y.E. Smith) with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Consent Item P Adjustment, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page adjusted Consent Item P to appoint Drew Cummings rather than Lee Worsley to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council. Announcements covered county broadcast schedules, board vacancies, and the September 22 Durham County Women's Agenda Assembly at North Carolina Central University.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (August 27, 2012 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the August 27, 2012 regular session minutes as presented.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of New DSS Director Michael Becketts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Manager Marqueta Welton introduced Michael Becketts, appointed Director of the Durham County Department of Social Services on August 6, 2012, noting his background in Baltimore overseeing 1,100 staff, a $100 million budget, and the transition of over 800 children out of foster care.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Joyce Clayton Nichols
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution honoring the late Joyce Clayton Nichols, the first woman and first African American woman physician assistant in the United States, longtime clinician at Lincoln Community Health Center, and founder of its foundation. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow recalled serving alongside her on the Lincoln board, and Nichols's family and Lincoln leadership accepted the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Olympic Silver Medalist Megan Hodge
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented a resolution honoring Durham native Megan Hodge, who won a silver medal with the U.S. women's indoor volleyball team at the 2012 London Olympics, accepted by her father Michael Hodge.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-Q, excluding Item I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Consent Agenda Items A through Q excluding removed Item I (and incorporating the Item P correction to Drew Cummings). Vice Chair Reckhow commended General Services Director Low for negotiating a collaborative contract with the City of Durham saving over $500,000 in the upcoming year.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Private Activity Bonds (up to $17 Million) for Voyager Foundation / Voyager Academy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy County Attorney Carol Hammett and bond counsel Jeffrey Poley (Parker Poe) explained the IRS-required TEFRA public hearing for up to $17 million in charter school revenue bonds issued by the Wisconsin-based Public Finance Authority for Voyager Academy/Voyager Foundation, emphasizing Durham County has no financial liability for the debt. Poley explained the national issuer was formed at the request of NLC and NACo to lower 501(c)(3) issuance costs.

agenda_items.title: Informational Report: City Local Historic Landmark Designations (East Durham Graded School)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Lisa Miller briefed the Board on two City historic landmark designation applications—including the East Durham Graded School (later Y.E. Smith), being redeveloped into a school by Self-Help—because landmark status impacts county property taxes. Vice Chair Reckhow asked staff to verify whether nonprofit charter schools such as Voyager and the redeveloped school are tax-exempt or remain on the property tax rolls. With closed session pulled, the meeting adjourned at 7:51 p.m.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved August 27, 2012 regular session minutes.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote; seconder name was garbled in transcript ASR ('Chair, Chair, Chair, Chair').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved resolution in principle under IRS TEFRA rules for up to $17 million in charter school revenue bonds issued by Public Finance Authority for Voyager Foundation/Voyager Academy with no County financial liability.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 4, 2012 work session, the Board of County Commissioners heard citizen comment from Ralph McKinney regarding workplace accountability and voter participation, then received an academic performance update from Durham Public Schools showing multi-year gains in elementary reading (59.9%) and math (77.1%) and 83% of elementary schools meeting expected growth, while Algebra I missed expected growth; commissioners also requested placing the final DPS budget on the September 18 joint board meeting agenda. Laura Benson of Partnership for Children and DPS leadership presented a multi-year Pre-Kindergarten expansion framework building on NC Pre-K and Head Start. Commissioners and staff also reviewed state legislative agenda proposals—including Pre-K funding for disadvantaged four-year-olds, adult guardianship funding transferred to DSS, local SBI crime lab capacity amid analyst testimony backlogs, and full funding for the Justice Reinvestment Act of 2011—and reviewed Human Resources' new internal criminal-background screening procedure allowing applicants to challenge inaccuracies and submit rehabilitation rebuttals before considering any broader ordinance, with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the Tuesday work session and recognized citizen Ralph McKinney, who spoke on workplace misconduct, civic accountability, and voter turnout ahead of the November 6 election.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) Academic Growth and Proficiency Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS leadership presented 2011-2012 state growth and proficiency data, highlighting gains in elementary reading (56.1% to 59.9%), elementary math (71.1% to 77.1%), science, and high school English/biology, with 83% of elementary schools meeting expected growth while Algebra I fell short. Commissioners asked about expected-growth calculations, disconnected youth metrics, and requested adding the final DPS budget to the September 18 joint BOCC-BOE meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Pre-Kindergarten Expansion Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Laura Benson of the Partnership for Children and DPS leadership outlined a multi-year plan to expand Pre-K classrooms across Durham County by building on NC Pre-K, DPS instructional standards, and Head Start eligibility.

agenda_items.title: State Legislative Agenda Proposals Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff reviewed draft legislative priorities ahead of Monday approval, covering county cable/cell-phone tax revenue disparities, Pre-K funding for all disadvantaged four-year-olds, adult guardianship costs shifted from mental health to DSS without new funding, feasibility of a local SBI crime lab to address analyst backlogs resulting from the 2009 Supreme Court testimony ruling, and closing the $4.5 million statewide probation-staffing funding gap under the Justice Reinvestment Act of 2011.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Procedure: Criminal Background Investigations in Recruitment and Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR Director Corrie Wilson and HR staff presented a new internal administrative procedure—vetted with senior management and community advocates—allowing job applicants to dispute inaccurate criminal records and submit a two-prong rebuttal regarding job relevance to a review committee. Commissioners and the Manager praised the 'Begin Again' second-chance hiring approach as a practical internal step before approaching private employers or considering a broader ordinance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of County Commissioners met in regular session with all five members seated (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, Pam H. Karriker, and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.) and voted unanimously on all six formal actions. The Board approved Plan Amendment Case A1100008 (5-0) redesignating approximately 42.5 acres for Alexander Park Development from Industrial to Low-Medium Density Residential over adjacent landowner objections regarding wetlands and flooding. Commissioners also unanimously approved up to $800,000 over six years in performance-based Economic Development Investment Funds for Sentinel Data Centers' planned $174 million, 300,000-square-foot wholesale colocation data center (5-0), held a public hearing and deferred adoption of the updated Hazard Mitigation Plan to September 10, 2012 for additional review, and approved pulled consent budget ordinance amendment #13BCC000010 ($57,424 NCDHHS carryover) 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Opening Ceremonies, Commissioner Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page opened the meeting with announcements regarding the Durham Reads Together library initiative. The Board then approved the minutes from the August 6, 2012 work session and August 13, 2012 regular session without revision.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: NACo National County Government Month Award and EMS Award Pulled
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Information Officer Deborah Craig-Gray and Michael Lee accepted recognition for Durham County winning second place nationally from NACo for National County Government Month programming featuring the Health and Wellness Education Fair flash mob. Item 6, recognizing paramedic Rick Johnson with the Vic Pearson Memorial Award, was pulled from the agenda for a future date.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-C, E-J; Item 7D Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 7D (Budget Ordinance Amendment #13BCC000010) was pulled for separate discussion while the remainder of the consent agenda (Items A-C and E-J) proceeded directly to a vote without objection.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment Case A1100008 (Alexander Park Development)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Aaron Cain and Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map amendment redesignating roughly 42.5 acres across approximately 10 parcels near Page Road from Industrial to Low-Medium Density Residential, which the Planning Commission had recommended 13-0 on July 10, 2012. Applicant attorney Patrick Byker (Morningstar Law Group), Lewis Cheek, Tommy Drake, and Rev. Johnny Bethea (Henderson Grove Missionary Baptist Church) spoke in favor of transitioning the area to residential uses. Adjacent property owner William Oakley opposed the change citing federally regulated wetlands, 100-year floodplain concerns, sedimentation issues, and a 2009 traffic study; staff and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted environmental and traffic mitigation would be evaluated at the rezoning and site plan stages.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Investment Funds for Sentinel Data Centers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Manager Marquita Welton and Sentinel Data Centers co-president Josh Rabiner presented a performance-based incentive contract providing up to $800,000 over six years for a $174 million, three-phase, 300,000-square-foot wholesale Tier 3+ colocation data center projected to create at least 19 direct full-time jobs alongside construction and tenant jobs. Chamber CEO Casey Steinbacher and Ted Conner supported the award as diversifying Durham's economy beyond pharma/biotech, while citizen Victoria Peterson urged local and African-American contractor hiring and reporting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Updated Durham County Hazard Mitigation Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Management Director Jeff Batten and Coordinator Mark Shell presented the 151-page five-year update to the Durham County Hazard Mitigation Plan, noting FEMA approved the plan in March 2012 and that erroneous template language referencing the McGuire Nuclear Power Plant had been removed. Commissioners closed the public hearing and agreed by consensus to defer final adoption until September 10, 2012 so members could review the full plan and adjust the September 4 work session hours to 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners completed written ballots for five county advisory bodies. At 01:22:25, the clerk announced the selections: Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee (Salb Silkbiker per transcript), Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (Sue Back), Dangerous Dog Appeal Board (Mimi Coker and Anthony Miller), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Warren Langley per transcript), and Nursing Home Advisory Committee (Katie Huffman).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7D: Budget Ordinance Amendment #13BCC000010 ($57,424 NCDHHS Carryover)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page noted that the resident who requested Item 7D be pulled had departed the meeting, allowing staff member Rebecca to be excused while the Board acted on rolling $57,424 in unspent FY 2011-12 NC Department of Health and Human Services funds into FY 2012-13.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Property Acquisition, IBM Tax Appeal, Attorney-Client Privilege, Initial Employment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adjourned into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding acquisition of 4527 Hillsborough Road, N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for the IBM Credit Corp. property tax appeal (01 PTC 544) and attorney-client consultation, and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for initial employment conditions. Upon returning at 03:03:58, the Board reported giving direction to staff and adjourned at 10:06 p.m.

disagreements.issue: Alexander Park Development Plan Amendment (A1100008): Wetlands, Floodplain, and Traffic Impacts

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Four commissioners attended the August 13, 2012 regular session (Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Pam H. Karriker, and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.), with Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow excused for the evening. The Board unanimously approved all five formal motions 4-0, highlighted by up to $2,000,000 in performance-based Economic Development Investment Funds over 10 years for 21C Durham LLC's $45 million renovation of the historic downtown Hill Building into a 125-room 21C Museum Hotel. Commissioners also approved SunTrust installment financing for a Trane US Inc. guaranteed energy savings performance contract (4-0), held a public hearing on an up to $600,000 CDBG Contingency Infrastructure grant application for Rougemont groundwater contamination without a vote yet, and approved pulled consent item 9B appointing Kimberly Shaw as Durham County ABC Board Chair (4-0).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board honored Fire Marshal Jeff Batten for his 2012 Department of Defense ESGR Freedom Award nomination, recognized Finance Director George Quick for being named Triangle Business Journal CFO of the Year, proclaimed September 14, 2012 as Bull City Stand Down Day for homeless veterans, and proclaimed Soil and Water Conservation Awareness Month marking the program's 75th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A, C-N; Item 9B Pulled)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Investment Contract with 21C Durham LLC (21C Museum Hotel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Manager Marquita Welton and 21C President Craig Greenberg presented the $45 million adaptive reuse of downtown Durham's historic Hill Building into a 125-room boutique hotel, 5,000-square-foot free contemporary art museum, and restaurant, with up to $2,000,000 in county performance-based incentives payable over 10 years after opening. Downtown and business supporters (Alice Sharp, Bill Kalkhof, Patrick Byker, Shelly Green, Heather Wagner, Ted Conner, and Chuck Watts) urged approval citing 150+ permanent jobs by July 2015 and 200+ construction jobs, while Victoria Peterson pressed for African-American and local contractor participation.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick and Sustainability Officer Tobin Freed presented the installment purchase financing resolution with SunTrust under N.C.G.S. 160A-20 to fund guaranteed energy conservation upgrades across county facilities with Trane US Inc., structured so guaranteed annual energy savings cover debt service.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Welcoming newly seated interim Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., the five-member Board experienced two contested 4-1 split votes during its July 23, 2012 session. First, on pulled consent Item 7I approving a utility contract extending County sanitary sewer and reuse water lines roughly four miles (including over a mile across Army Corps of Engineers land) for the 751 South development, the Board voted 4-1 in favor (Ayes: Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, Pam H. Karriker, and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.; Nay: Ellen W. Reckhow), with Reckhow and citizen opponents warning about Jordan Lake watershed impacts, Corps of Engineers environmental objections, and the lack of a filed special use permit. Second, following closed-session evaluations of the four board-appointed officials, commissioners voted 5-0 for a 4.25% raise across all four positions (plus a $250 monthly travel allowance increase for the County Attorney), and then passed an additional 4.0% market-equity raise (8.25% total) for Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson by a 4-1 voice vote (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Pam H. Karriker; the lone Nay voice was cast among Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, or Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., but the unrecorded voice vote is not attributed by name in the transcript). Separately, during written-ballot board appointments, Ellen W. Reckhow abstained on the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board tiebreaker because she had not reviewed candidate applications thinking the vote was deferred to August.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page welcomed interim Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. back to the Board and County Manager Mike Ruffin introduced new Human Resources Director Cora Wilson. Commissioners approved the June 25, 2012 regular session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens Steve Bocckino and Melissa Rooney opposed extending Durham County sewer and reuse water ~4 miles (including >1 mile across Army Corps of Engineers property) for the 751 South development, citing Jordan Lake pollution, potential sewer spills, and governance concerns over interim commissioners voting. Staff (Glen Whisnant, Brian Wardell, Steve Medlin) and developer representative Cal Cunningham argued engineered sewer is safer than a community septic system, while Ellen W. Reckhow questioned approving a utility agreement before a special use permit was filed and raised Corps biologist Michael Hosey's concerns over wetlands and the Northeast Creek Floodplain Forest Natural Heritage Area before voting Nay in a 4-1 split.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: 751 South Development Sewer and Reuse Water Utility Contract (Consent Item 7I)
disagreements.summary: The Board split 4-1 over approving a utility contract extending Durham County sanitary sewer and reuse water four miles, including over a mile through Army Corps of Engineers Jordan Lake property, for the 751 South mixed-use development.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the utility contract immediately so the developer can proceed with Army Corps permitting and connect to County sewer instead of an on-site treatment/community septic system.
side_a_arguments: Developer bears the capital cost of extending utilities and must still obtain Army Corps of Engineers easements, state approvals, and Board special use permit approval before construction.
Municipal sewer and reuse water lines are preferable to a large on-site package/community wastewater system near Jordan Lake.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer or deny the utility contract until the project's special use permit is submitted and Army Corps environmental objections are resolved.
side_b_arguments: No special use permit has even been filed yet, making the contract premature for a 1,300-unit/600,000-sq-ft project.
Army Corps biologist Michael Hosey warned of impacts to wetlands and the Northeast Creek Floodplain Forest Natural Heritage Area, and citizens raised spill/pollution and board-legitimacy concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 at 00:40:22 with Ellen W. Reckhow casting the lone Nay vote.

disagreements.issue: Additional 4.0% Market Equity Raise for Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson
disagreements.summary: After unanimously approving a 4.25% raise for all four board-appointed officials, the Board split 4-1 on granting Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson an additional 4.0% equity adjustment (8.25% total).
disagreements.side_a_position: Grant an extra 4.0% raise (8.25% total) to align the Tax Administrator's compensation with peer county tax assessors.
side_a_arguments: Peer county market comparisons showed Durham's Tax Administrator compensation trailed comparable counties despite strong performance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the additional 4.0% equity adjustment beyond the uniform 4.25% increase (unidentified lone voice-vote Nay among Michael D. Page, Brenda A. Howerton, or Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.).
side_b_arguments: Chairman Page specifically emphasized during debate that commissioners should be clear the combined raise equals 8.25%, and one commissioner registered a Nay vote on voice vote without on-record elaboration.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 by voice vote at 01:17:56 (identity of the single Nay among Page, Howerton, or Cousin not named in the audio/transcript).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Operating initially with four seated members (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker), the Board unanimously adopted the FY 2012-13 Budget Ordinance (4-0), lowering the property tax rate by 0.15 cents to 74.44 cents per $100 valuation and restoring $54,820 in net funding across five nonprofits after Triangle Champions Track Club director Tim Thorpe agreed to drop organized prayer from grant-funded programming. On Item 8 filling former Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's vacant seat, despite citizen pressure to select Democratic Executive Committee nominee Fred Foster Jr., commissioners voted 4-0 to appoint non-candidate former commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. so he could serve immediately without influencing the fall election. The Board also acted unanimously (4-0) on five pulled consent items (including Urban Ministries CHIN homelessness tracking, a $385,000 DCD childcare subsidy amendment, and an amended $3.408 million Correct Care Solutions jail health contract requiring tracking of 90-180 day state misdemeanor medical costs), directed a protest letter on NC DWQ Falls Lake rules, and approved newly hired DSS Director Michael Becketts's $129,000 salary (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Recognition of Delphine Sellers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved minutes from the May 31 special budget meeting, June 4 work session, and June 11 regular session 4-0. They also recognized Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers for winning the NC Distinguished Extension Community Development Service Award.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of FY 2012-13 Durham County Budget Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comments from Northeast Central Durham residents demanding answers from Durham Public Schools regarding vocational and alternative program changes at Holton Career and Resource Center, commissioners pushed to schedule an urgent joint meeting with the Board of Education and reinforced Section 9A's requirement for line-item DPS budget and capital project detail. County Manager Mike Ruffin summarized the final ordinance maintaining the 0.15-cent property tax reduction to 74.44 cents and adding $54,820 in net funding for five nonprofits (Child Care Services Association $29,783; Operation Breakthrough $71,451; Triangle Champions Track Club $7,098; African American Dance Ensemble $5,000; and a fifth $5,000 group), after Triangle Champions director Tim Thorpe appeared in person and agreed to replace organized prayer with silent reflection to meet legal requirements. Commissioners also requested an August work session to overhaul the nonprofit application process.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 7A, 7C, 7K, 7L, 7O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Items 7A, 7C, 7K, 7L, and 7O were pulled for separate discussion, and the Board approved all remaining consent items 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Appointment to Vacant County Commissioner Seat
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Dr. Darryl Roberts urged the Board to follow the Durham County Democratic Party Executive Committee's recommendation of primary runner-up Fred Foster Jr. and suggested sitting candidates recuse themselves. Commissioners Pam H. Karriker and Michael D. Page countered that appointing a non-candidate former commissioner avoided giving any November candidate an unfair incumbency advantage and ensured immediate experience on the dais, voting 4-0 to appoint Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. to fill the remainder of Joe Bowser's term.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Added NC DWQ Falls Lake Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointments and Workforce Development Board private-sector vacancies before voting by ballot on 13 advisory boards (tabulated at 02:16:40 and 02:21:12, selecting among others Dwayne Taylor and Cynthia F. Vanderweel/Vanderwall to Bike/Ped, George Kolasa to Board of Adjustment, Eddie Davis to Appearance, Ricky E. Padgett to Planning Commission, Walker French to Durham Tech Trustees, and Alvis Akins and Donald Hughes to Workforce Development). Under an added item at 01:47:30, the Board reviewed Manager Ruffin's June 22 letter to NC Division of Water Quality Director Charles Wakild opposing a state proposal to exempt state-permitted discharging sand filters from Falls Lake rules while burdening counties, reaching consensus to copy the Governor and legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7A: Interlocal Agreement for Gang Reduction Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed and unanimously approved the city-county interlocal agreement supporting Durham's Gang Reduction Strategy.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7C: Urban Ministries of Durham Shelter Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow's request, staff agreed to add contract requirements for tracking Homelessness Management Information System (CHIN) data points capturing clients' last permanent residence and institutional discharge status to measure out-of-county inflows.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 7K & 7L: Budget Amendments for Child Care Subsidies ($385,000) and Food Cards ($4,675)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item 7K (#12BCC00090), Ellen W. Reckhow questioned the one-month lag between state May 18 approval and June 25 Board action with six days left in the fiscal year; DSS staff explained the $385,000 state reallocation reimbursed existing 102% child care subsidy overspending. Both Item 7K and Item 7L (#12BCC00091 for $4,675 in donated food cards) passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7O: Correct Care Solutions Jail Health Contract Renewal ($3,408,258)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting jail health costs had reached $3.4 million and Sheriff Andrews was voluntarily housing state misdemeanants (90-180 days) for $40/day without excess-prescription coverage, Reckhow and Public Health Director Gayle Harris added Contract Amendment #5 requiring Correct Care Solutions to separately track medical costs for those state inmates and bill off-site care to the state special fund. Reckhow also urged shifting jail health funding from Public Health into the Sheriff's detention budget next year for fiscal transparency.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of DSS Director Michael Becketts's Salary ($129,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) (4-0) and returned to open session at 02:40:09, where commissioners voted 4-0 to approve the $129,000 annual salary for Michael Becketts, newly appointed DSS Director by the Board of Social Services.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Filling Vacant Commissioner Seat: Non-Candidate Former Commissioner vs. Democratic Party Nominee Fred Foster Jr.
disagreements.summary: Citizen speaker Dr. Darryl Roberts urged the Board to appoint Democratic Executive Committee nominee and primary candidate Fred Foster Jr. and called for sitting candidates to recuse themselves, while commissioners opted to appoint non-candidate former commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.
disagreements.side_a_position: Appoint a non-candidate former commissioner (Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.) for the remaining interim months to preserve neutrality in the November election and ensure immediate budget/board readiness.
side_a_arguments: Appointing a November general-election candidate (Fred Foster Jr.) would grant an unearned incumbency advantage over fellow candidates.
Under N.C.G.S. 153A-27, the Board consults with the party executive committee but retains statutory discretion and is not bound by its recommendation.
Former commissioner Cousin can step in seamlessly for the short interim term.
disagreements.side_b_position: Appoint Democratic Party nominee Fred Foster Jr. and require commissioners running in November to recuse themselves (citizen position; no board dissent).
side_b_arguments: Voters and the Democratic Party Executive Committee endorsed Fred Foster Jr., who finished immediately behind incumbents in the primary.
Sitting candidates choosing an appointee who will not run alongside them raises conflict-of-interest concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Motion by Pam H. Karriker, seconded by Michael D. Page, passed 4-0 at 01:28:57 appointing Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.

disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the FY 2012-13 budget with Section 9A demanding line-item DPS project detail, seek an urgent joint BOCC/DPS meeting on Holton, and restore five nonprofit grants contingent on secular contract compliance.
side_a_arguments: DPS had not yet furnished a detailed budget book or project-by-project capital breakdown.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: The four-member Board (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker) held a seven-hour budget and policy work session featuring two unanimous 4-0 action votes to immediately add 15 EMS positions (10 paramedics, 4 EMT-Intermediates, and 1 Clerk IV) to assume ambulance service from the Bethesda and Redwood volunteer fire departments at a projected $95,600 net savings. By contrast, a sharp 90-minute procedural and policy dispute erupted over the new courthouse parking deck policy and Lanier Parking contract: Public Defender Lawrence Campbell and Clerk of Court Archie Smith opposed charging state courthouse staff $25/month and capping employee spots at 200. Although Ellen W. Reckhow and Pam H. Karriker twice passed 4-0 motions suspending the rules to enable a same-day vote on the parking policy, Brenda A. Howerton and Chairman Michael D. Page objected to acting without letting courthouse officials weigh back in, resulting in deferral of the main parking vote to June 11. The Board also reviewed System of Care/MCO merger updates, Animal Control Ordinance revisions, Falls/Jordan Lake staffing, recycling cart contracts, nonprofit budget reviews, a 4.68% Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant rate increase, and General Services in-house courthouse maintenance savings.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments: Courthouse Employee Parking Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Defender Lawrence Campbell and Clerk of Superior Court Archie Smith addressed the Board during citizen comments to oppose the proposed $25/month parking charge for state courthouse employees in the new justice center parking deck, arguing state employees had faced prolonged state pay freezes and rising health costs.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Memorial Stadium Authority Fee Schedule Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stadium Authority Chair Tommy Hunt briefed commissioners on simplifying the Memorial Stadium fee schedule to predictable flat rental rates to market the facility for more regional and youth events. Because the Authority sets fees directly, no Board vote was required.

agenda_items.title: System of Care and Mental Health MCO Merger Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ellen Holleman, Ann Oshel, and System of Care staff reported on Durham's SAMHSA System of Care grant, Child and Family Teams, Network of Care online portal, and preparation for the July 1 Wake-Durham mental health MCO merger. Vice Chair Reckhow pressed staff on school system coordination and clearer public branding for the portal.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Amendments to Durham County Animal Control Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Attorney Curtis Massey and staff reviewed Animal Control Ordinance revisions accompanying the transition to the Sheriff's Office, including criminalizing leaving animals unattended in hot vehicles under exigent circumstances and updating Dangerous Dog Appeal Board composition. Commissioners agreed to place the public hearing/ordinance items on the upcoming regular session agenda.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Staffing Request (15 Positions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS Director Mike Smith presented a request for 10 paramedics, 4 EMT-Intermediates, and 1 Clerk IV so County EMS could assume ambulance operations from Bethesda and Redwood volunteer fire departments at a net budget savings of $95,600. After discussing staffing transitions, the Board unanimously suspended the rules (4-0) and approved the 15 new positions (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake & Jordan Lake Rules Budget Impact and Month-to-Month Recycling Contract Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Manager Drew Cummings and stormwater/planning staff (Robert Brown, Chris Roberts, Glen Whisnant, Eddie Culberson) outlined budget needs and two new positions (Environmental Health Specialist and Stormwater Manager) to implement Falls Lake and Jordan Lake nutrient rules. Staff also briefed the Board on extending the county recycling collection contract month-to-month ahead of transitioning from 18-gallon bins to 95-gallon roll carts.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Parking Policy and Lanier Parking Management Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated for roughly 90 minutes over charging state courthouse employees $25/month (capped at 200 spaces in the 897-space deck vs. $55 in city decks) and negotiating a $123,106 management contract with Lanier Parking. Ellen W. Reckhow and Pam H. Karriker favored immediate adoption and passed two 4-0 motions suspending work-session rules (04:42:10 and 04:42:51), but Brenda A. Howerton and Chairman Page objected to taking final action before Archie Smith and Lawrence Campbell had notice after agenda listings indicated June 11, leading the Board to hold the final policy vote until June 11.

agenda_items.title: Directives, Nonprofit Budget Process Review, Triangle Wastewater Rate Increase, and General Services Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented agenda directives and a stoplight review of FY 2012-13 nonprofit applications (highlighting CCSA's IRS Form 990 balance sheet and late-submission rules). Utilities staff (Glen Whisnant and Tobin Freed) reviewed a proposed 4.68% Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant consumption rate increase and a Sustainability Coordinator position, and General Services presented plans for Human Services Phase 2, bringing courthouse/jail maintenance in-house with 12 staff for ~$300,000 in annual savings, and a $10 solid waste fee increase.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Act on EMS Position Request During Work Session
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work session rules so the Board could immediately authorize EMS hiring ahead of the Bethesda/Redwood takeover.

votes.item_title: Approval of 15 New EMS Positions (Assume Bethesda & Redwood VFD Ambulance Service)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 10 paramedics, 4 EMT-Intermediates, and 1 Clerk IV to absorb Bethesda and Redwood ambulance operations at a net savings of $95,600.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Address Durham County Parking Policy for Justice Center Deck
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend rules specifically for the Justice Center parking deck policy, immediately clarified/restated to cover countywide parking policy.

votes.item_title: Amended Motion to Suspend Rules to Address Countywide Durham County Parking Policy
votes.notes: Main vote on parking policy deferred to June 11 following procedural debate.
votes.discussion_detail: Re-affirmed rule suspension for countywide parking policy, but subsequent objections from Howerton and Page over lack of notice to courthouse officials led the Board to defer the final policy vote without taking a substantive vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
disagreements.issue: State Courthouse Employee Parking Fees ($25/Month) and Procedural Fairness on Same-Day Vote
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed over whether to immediately suspend rules and impose a $25/month parking charge capped at 200 state courthouse employees in the new justice center deck, or defer the vote to allow judicial officials who spoke that morning notice and opportunity to respond.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move forward at the work session to establish the $25/month state employee fee and deck rates so Lanier Parking contract negotiations and event parking revenues can start promptly.
side_a_arguments: $25/month is already a steep discount below the $55/month city parking deck rate and public rates.
County taxpayers should not subsidize state budget freezes, and revenue is needed to cover the $123,106 Lanier operating contract and deck debt service.
Staff needed pricing set ahead of weekend DPAC events.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer the substantive vote to June 11 and re-examine employee hardship/200-space cap concerns before adopting the policy.
side_b_arguments: Public Defender Lawrence Campbell and Clerk of Court Archie Smith spoke during morning comments expecting action on June 11, not an unannounced work-session vote after they left.
Limiting state staff to 200 paid spaces and charging $25/month burdens courthouse workers.
disagreements.resolution: Despite passing two 4-0 motions suspending rules (04:42:10, 04:42:51), the Board refrained from voting on the main parking policy and deferred final action to June 11.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting as a four-member Board (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker), commissioners unanimously passed all three formal actions 4-0 while receiving County Manager Mike Ruffin's recommended FY 2012-13 budget. The recommended $347.4 million general fund budget kept the property tax rate flat at 74.59 cents, reflected the removal of $25.1 million due to the Wake-Durham mental health MCO merger (+4.22% adjusted growth), added 48.5 new positions, increased Durham Public Schools current-expense funding to $115.8 million ($244,880 above DPS's request), raised Open Space funding from $300,000 to $500,000, and challenged the Board to consider city-county consolidation. Commissioners also formally voted 4-0 to relocate Animal Control from General Services to the Sheriff's Office effective July 1 to establish 24/7 two-shift enforcement, approved the consent agenda 4-0 after Ellen W. Reckhow urged eventual digitization in joint Warrant Control, and appointed members to eight advisory boards.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 7 and May 14, 2012 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After opening ceremonies, the four seated commissioners unanimously approved the minutes of the May 7, 2012 work session and May 14, 2012 regular session 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Dr. LeRoy T. Walker Sr., Hunger Awareness Month, and Mountains-to-Sea Trail
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adopted a memorial/honorary resolution for Dr. LeRoy T. Walker Sr., proclaimed June 2012 as Hunger Awareness Month with DSS staff, and accepted a Certificate of Appreciation from NC Parks & Recreation recognizing the Mountains-to-Sea Trail at Falls Lake (with Vice Chair Reckhow and Jane Korest).

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Presentation of FY 2012-13 Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented a $347.4 million recommended FY 2012-13 general fund budget (a 3.10% headline drop caused by transferring $25.1M in mental health MCO funding to the Wake-Durham merger, representing +4.22% adjusted growth) with an unchanged 74.59-cent tax rate. Highlights included employee merit/performance pay raises, a 2.4% health insurance increase, 48.5 new positions, $192,295 for strategic plan initiatives, 'Begin Again' ex-offender employment slots, $115.8M for DPS current expense plus $1.37M capital, 35 Sheriff vehicles, a fire tax district consolidation study, Open Space preservation raised to $500,000, and a challenge for commissioners to pursue city-county consolidation; the Board also adjusted June 12 and 14 budget work session dates.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before the consent vote, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow spoke on Item 9E (Warrant Control), praising Sheriff and Police backlog reductions while urging future electronic warrant entry/retrieval to reduce joint city-county staffing costs. The Board then approved Consent Items A-J unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Relocation of Animal Control Department from General Services to Sheriff's Office
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Ruffin and Sheriff Worth Andrews presented the statutory reorganization transferring Animal Control from General Services to the Sheriff's Office by July 1, expanding coverage from one shift to two shifts (24/7 dispatch via Sheriff communications) while retaining current employees subject to background checks and phasing vacant slots into sworn deputies over time. Reckhow praised Sergeant Brendan Hartigan and the Sheriff's Office before the Board approved the relocation 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners completed written ballots for appointments across eight county boards and committees (results announced between 01:44:32 and 01:45:25) and adjourned at 8:43 p.m.

votes.item_title: Relocation of Animal Control Department to Durham County Sheriff's Office
votes.discussion_detail: Approved reorganizing Animal Control under the Sheriff's Office by July 1 to provide 24/7 two-shift response and unified dispatch.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opening its May 14, 2012 regular session, the four remaining commissioners (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker) voted 4-0 to formally accept Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's May 9, 2012 resignation, then engaged in a lengthy governance debate over N.C.G.S. 153A-27 replacement procedures. Chairman Michael D. Page urged rapidly vetting experienced candidates before budget deliberations began (publicly naming former commissioner Philip Cousin and recent candidate Anita Daniels), while Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Pam H. Karriker insisted on formally notifying and consulting the Durham County Democratic Party Executive Committee without pre-empting its process. The Board went on to pass every formal item unanimously 4-0, including appointing Michael D. Page to replace Bowser on the DSS Board, adopting the 2040 Durham Comprehensive Plan Update, and approving DPS Resolution & Capital Project Amendment #12CPA000010 reallocating $9,039,001 in unspent 2007 GO High School A bond proceeds to school instructional technology.

agenda_items.title: Acceptance of Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's Resignation and Vacancy Replacement Process Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board accepted Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's May 9, 2012 resignation 4-0 and heard County Attorney Lowell Siler outline the 60-day replacement clock and mandatory consultation with the Durham County Democratic Party Executive Committee under N.C.G.S. 153A-27. Commissioners debated whether to immediately put forward former commissioner Philip Cousin and recent candidate Anita Daniels (preferred by Page to move quickly before budget hearings) or send a neutral letter inviting the Democratic Executive Committee's recommendation first (advocated by Howerton, Reckhow, and Karriker); the Board directed Siler to hand-deliver the notification letter seeking an expedited response.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (March 29 Legislative Breakfast, April 21 PAC 1, April 23 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved the minutes from three prior meetings and legislative events without modification.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Proclamations (Lions Club 90th, Veterans Services Officer, Older Americans Month, Foster Care Month, Gayle Harris, Kimberly Simpson)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board honored the Durham Lions Club's 90th anniversary, welcomed new Veterans Services Officer Lois Harvin Raven and MPA intern Emily Wapuda, proclaimed Older Americans Month/Senior Corps Week and Foster Care Month, recognized Public Health Director Gayle Harris for her Duke School of Nursing Distinguished Alumni Award, and congratulated Tax Collector Kimberly Simpson on being named 2012 NC Tax Collector of the Year.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-O) and Added Appointment of Chairman Page to DSS Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Items A through O (4-0) and added a unanimous vote (4-0) appointing Chairman Michael D. Page to replace Joe Bowser on the Board of Social Services.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: Durham Comprehensive Plan Update (2040 Horizon)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Laura Woods presented the Comprehensive Plan Update projecting Durham growth to roughly 400,000 residents by 2040. Vice Chair Reckhow praised the update and reiterated the need for a joint City-County-Schools capital planning committee before the Board unanimously adopted the update 4-0.

agenda_items.title: DPS Resolution and Capital Project Amendment #12CPA000010 ($9,039,001 GO Bond Reallocation for School Technology)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Chief Operating Officer Hugh Osteen presented the resolution reallocating $9,039,001 from unspent 2007 General Obligation Bond proceeds originally earmarked for High School A (Project SH126) to fund districtwide instructional technology. Following discussion from the May 7 work session, the Board approved the reallocation unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners acknowledged an email notice regarding Fred Foster Jr.'s interest in the vacant board seat and voted 4-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for business expansion discussions, adjourning at 9:20 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Process and Timing for Consulting Democratic Party on Joe W. Bowser's Vacancy
disagreements.summary: Following Joe W. Bowser's resignation, Chairman Michael D. Page favored immediately advancing and acting on experienced candidates (naming Philip Cousin and Anita Daniels), whereas Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Pam H. Karriker insisted on formally notifying the Democratic Executive Committee without predetermining names.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move rapidly and put forward willing experienced names (Philip Cousin and Anita Daniels) so a replacement is seated in time for FY 2012-13 budget work sessions.
side_a_arguments: FY 2012-13 budget presentation starts May 29, leaving little time for a drawn-out selection.
Both named individuals indicated willingness to serve and Page expressed disappointment after revealing names that the Board would not act or transmit them immediately.
disagreements.side_b_position: Send a neutral statutory notice requesting the Democratic Executive Committee's expedited recommendation first without sending pre-selected commissioner names.
side_b_arguments: N.C.G.S. 153A-27 requires consulting the party executive committee, which was meeting the next evening (May 15).
Sending names prematurely risks disrespecting or pre-empting the Democratic Party's internal selection process and raising openness concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners agreed by consensus (00:40:12) to have County Attorney Siler hand-deliver a general vacancy notice requesting an expedited recommendation without attaching specific commissioner names.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: All five seated commissioners (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Joe W. Bowser, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker) held a lengthy pre-primary work session on May 7, 2012—the final recorded meeting with Joe W. Bowser prior to his May 9 resignation. Ahead of North Carolina's May 8 Marriage Amendment (Amendment 1) referendum, County employees, retirees, and partners urged commissioners to protect health benefits; after receiving a legal opinion from Assistant County Attorney Kathy Everett-Perry and County Attorney Lowell Siler that Durham County's 2003 policy did not depend on affirming a marriage-like relationship, the Board unanimously suspended its rules (5-0) and passed a motion reaffirming commitment to domestic partner benefits (5-0). The Board also voted 5-0 to open the County building for election returns, suspended rules (5-0) to approve the City-County FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan ($767,896 HOME consortium) with a formal request for City Council to reconsider zeroing out Operation Breakthrough weatherization funding (5-0), heard DPS Superintendent Eric B. Becoats on the $9M 2007 bond technology shift, and reviewed Durham-Orange light rail interlocal disputes and Strategic Plan goals.

agenda_items.title: Election Night Building Opening and Citizen Comments (Domestic Partner Benefits, Amendment 1, and DPS Technology)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted 5-0 to open the County administration building on May 8 evening for primary election returns. During a 30-minute citizen comment block, County employees, retirees, and partners (Joanne Abel, Nancy Blood, Kathy Chandler, and Mel Downey-Piper) urged the Board to preserve domestic partner health benefits if Amendment 1 passed, Allen Lang urged waiting for Microsoft Windows 8 before spending $9M on DPS technology, Victoria Peterson voiced support for Amendment 1 and raised jail overcrowding concerns, and Harry Leary and Darius Little spoke on animal control subpoenas and Annual Action Plan scoring.

agenda_items.title: Legal Review and Reaffirmation of 2003 Domestic Partner Benefits Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Attorney Kathy Everett-Perry and County Attorney Lowell Siler advised the Board that Durham County's 2003 domestic partner health benefit policy rests on financial interdependence rather than a marriage-like legal relationship and should therefore withstand North Carolina's Amendment 1. Commissioners unanimously suspended the rules (5-0) and adopted a formal reaffirmation of the 2003 policy (5-0).

agenda_items.title: DPS Presentation on $9 Million 2007 GO Bond Reallocation for Instructional Technology
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Superintendent Dr. Eric B. Becoats, COO Hugh Osteen, Elaine Batten, and principals Cathy Bonner, Sheldon Reynolds, and Patrice Williams presented the plan to shift $9.04 million from High School A bond proceeds to laptops, tablets, and classroom technology, while Finance Director George Quick explained the four-year bond maturity alignment. The item was scheduled for formal action on May 14.

agenda_items.title: Stadium Authority Legislation Expansion and Charter Schools / DPS Joint Work Session Follow-up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stadium Authority Chair Tommy Hunt and Commissioner Pam H. Karriker presented draft legislative amendments expanding the Stadium Authority from five to seven members alongside a simplified rental fee preview. Staff then reviewed follow-up items from the April 2 Charter Schools/DPS work session covering weighted lotteries, socioeconomic diversity, free/reduced-price lunch reporting, and closing achievement gaps.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing and Approval: FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan ($767,896 HOME Consortium)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Deputy Manager Drew Cummings returned with the FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan ($767,896 HOME total, including $38,385 County share) after the April 23 continuance. Commissioners expressed strong frustration over late packets and the City's defunding of Operation Breakthrough's weatherization program, suspending the rules 5-0 and approving the plan 5-0 with an explicit request that Durham City Council revisit Operation Breakthrough's allocation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Business Location/Expansion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recessed into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) following a morning greeting with visiting students and returned to open session at 04:28:26 reporting staff direction given.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Update, Property Tax Revenue Update, Durham-Orange Light Rail Interlocal Agreement, and Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Laura Woods, Keith Luck, Aaron Cain) reviewed 2040 Comprehensive Plan station design districts and East Durham group home issues, followed by a property tax briefing projecting $30 billion valuation (+1.54% growth, +$3.91M revenue). Triangle Transit CEO David King and Manager Ruffin then presented the Durham-Orange Light Rail Interlocal Agreement amendment requiring an extra $150,000/year capital contribution from Durham for 23 years while highlighting an impasse over Orange County's request for +$57,000/year in operating support; Michael Davis closed with a Strategic Plan implementation briefing.

votes.item_title: Open County Administration Building on May 8 Evening for Primary Election Returns
votes.notes: Preceded at 00:20:12 by completion of an earlier opening 5-0 vote whose title precedes the transcript start.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized opening the County building on May 8 evening for public viewing of election returns.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Reaffirm County Domestic Partner Benefits Policy
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work session rules for immediate action on domestic partner health insurance policy.

votes.item_title: Reaffirmation of 2003 Domestic Partner Health Benefits Policy
votes.discussion_detail: Reaffirmed County commitment to retaining the 2003 domestic partner benefits policy based on legal counsel opinion that it remains valid regardless of Amendment 1.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Approve FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules to approve the City-County Annual Action Plan to meet HUD submission timelines.

votes.item_title: Approve FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan with Request for City Council to Revisit Operation Breakthrough
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the FY 2012-13 HOME Consortium Annual Action Plan while formally requesting Durham City Council reconsider funding for Operation Breakthrough's weatherization program.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) Business Expansion)
votes.notes: All five commissioners voted 5-0 one minute earlier at 03:22:08; ASR transcribed Chair's voice-vote announcement at 03:23:38 as 'four to zero' with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under economic development privilege after greeting visiting students.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
disagreements.issue: City-County Annual Action Plan Allocation Process and Exclusion of Operation Breakthrough
disagreements.summary: Following the April 23 continuance, commissioners criticized the City of Durham's Community Development scoring and allocation process for eliminating Operation Breakthrough's weatherization grant without transparent justification or timely county input.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan under deadline pressure only with an explicit condition asking City Council to reconsider Operation Breakthrough funding.
side_a_arguments: HUD deadlines forced timely plan approval, but County officials were frustrated by insufficient notice and inconsistent scoring affecting Operation Breakthrough.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the City Community Development committee's scoring criteria that excluded Operation Breakthrough from FY 2012-13 allocations (City staff presentation; no board dissent).
side_b_arguments: City Community Development staff noted applications were evaluated under competitive RFP/committee thresholds prior to Council review.
disagreements.resolution: Approved unanimously 5-0 at 03:22:08 with the added formal request asking City Council to revisit Operation Breakthrough's allocation.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
disagreements.issue: Durham-Orange Light Rail Interlocal Agreement Cost-Sharing Dispute
disagreements.summary: Staff and Triangle Transit CEO David King reported an impasse in amending the Durham-Orange light rail interlocal agreement over Orange County's demand for an extra $57,000/year in Durham operating funds in addition to Durham's +$150,000/year 23-year capital commitment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support adding $150,000/year in capital support to extend light rail design toward Chapel Hill/Orange County, while resisting extra county operating subsidies demanded by Orange County.
side_a_arguments: Durham taxpayers already committed substantial local transit funding and should not absorb disproportionate operating transfers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Orange County negotiators requested +$57,000/year in additional operating support to proceed (external partner position; informational briefing only).
side_b_arguments: Orange County sought greater operating support from Durham/Triangle Transit before signing the amended agreement.
disagreements.resolution: Informational briefing; no formal vote taken at the May 7 work session.
