meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: All five seated commissioners (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Joe W. Bowser, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker) began the April 23, 2012 regular session with a closed-session attorney-client consultation before announcing that a proposed Board resolution opposing North Carolina's Amendment One had been pulled from the agenda because N.C.G.S. 153A-456 bars using public funds or resources once referendum early voting has begun. During open session, the Board passed every formal vote unanimously 5-0, including two quasi-judicial and development approvals for Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. at 5325 Old Oxford Road: a Transportation Special Use Permit (TSUP Case T120001) authorizing build-out up to 824,000 square feet (5-0) and Major Site Plan Case D1100203 for a 65,400-square-foot warehouse expansion and 6,142-square-foot boiler enclosure (5-0). Commissioners also continued action on the Draft FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan to May 7 after objecting to missing plan packets and Operation Breakthrough's exclusion, and made seven advisory board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Initial Closed Session and Pulling of Amendment One Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 00:11:54, the Board unanimously entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation, returning at 00:40:08 with no action taken. Chairman Page and County Attorney Lowell Siler explained that the proposed resolution on Amendment One had been pulled because N.C.G.S. 153A-456 prohibits expending public resources to endorse or oppose a ballot referendum once early voting begins, though individual commissioners stated their positions and scheduled a 30-minute citizen comment block on May 7.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Ceremonial Proclamations (Mental Health, Louis Washington Retirement, Durham Chorale, Week of the Young Child)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved the April 2 and April 9, 2012 minutes 5-0. They then proclaimed Children's Mental Health Awareness Week (May 6-12 with Ellen Holleman), adopted a retirement resolution honoring Veterans Services Officer Louis B. Washington for 10 years of service securing over $25 million in veteran claims, celebrated the Durham Chorale's 25th Anniversary (Melanie Zinter), and proclaimed Week of the Young Child (April 22-28 with Laura Benson and Child Care Services Association).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved Consent Agenda Items A through I without any items pulled.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Draft FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan ($767,896 HOME Program)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and staff presented the Draft FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan ($767,896 HOME consortium, including a $38,385 County match), while public speakers Darius Little, Victoria Peterson, and DeWorn Langley questioned project allocations. Commissioners objected that they had not received the full plan documents ahead of the hearing and questioned the exclusion of Operation Breakthrough's weatherization grant, continuing action to the May 7 work session.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Public Hearing: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. Transportation Special Use Permit (TSUP Case T120001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Killian, Merck representatives, and expert witnesses (Raymond Raine, Mike Sanchez, and traffic engineer Mr. Overcast) testified in support of TSUP Case T120001 at 5325 Old Oxford Road, with Chamber/economic testimony from Ted Conner noting nearly $1 billion invested and over 1,000 employees since 2004. Planning Manager Patrick Young clarified the TSUP authorized build-out up to 824,000 square feet total and that the Development Review Board had recommended (not finally approved) the companion site plan; the Board unanimously approved the TSUP 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Merck Warehouse Expansion and Boiler Enclosure Major Site Plan (Case D1100203)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Manager Patrick Young presented Major Site Plan Case D1100203 authorizing a 65,400-square-foot warehouse expansion and 6,142-square-foot boiler enclosure compliant with all UDO requirements. The Board approved the site plan unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments and Closing Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners elected seven appointees by ballot (02:47:59): Carolyn Henderson, Greg Savage, Robert Barbara (per transcript), Dr. James P. Weaver, and Farad Ali to the Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees; Linda Lane to the Nursing Home CAC; and Stephanie DeBerry to the Transportation Advisory Committee. The Board then entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3) (5-0), returned at 03:08:17 with staff direction, and adjourned at 10:00 p.m.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Initial Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) Attorney-Client Privilege)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for legal advice regarding the Amendment One referendum restriction under N.C.G.S. 153A-456; returned at 00:40:08 with no action taken.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 2 and April 9, 2012 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved prior April regular and work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Quasi-Judicial Transportation Special Use Permit Case T120001 (Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp.)
votes.notes: ASR transcribed '5-0' as '520'; unanimous voice approval with zero opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved TSUP authorizing campus build-out up to 824,000 square feet at 5325 Old Oxford Road based on competent traffic and site testimony.

votes.item_title: Merck Warehouse Expansion and Boiler Enclosure Major Site Plan (Case D1100203)
votes.notes: Chair stated 'motion carries five' with zero opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved major site plan for a 65,400-sq-ft warehouse addition and 6,142-sq-ft boiler enclosure at Merck.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closing Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for business expansion and attorney-client consultation; returned at 03:08:17 with staff direction and adjourned at 10:00 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Procedural Withdrawal of Amendment One Resolution Under N.C.G.S. 153A-456
disagreements.summary: After entering closed session for legal advice, the Board pulled its scheduled resolution on North Carolina's Amendment One because N.C.G.S. 153A-456 bars expending public funds/resources once voting begins, prompting individual commissioner remarks and public debate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Comply with County Attorney advice pulling the official resolution due to the N.C.G.S. 153A-456 statutory ban once early voting is underway, while allowing personal remarks and May 7 public comment.
side_a_arguments: N.C.G.S. 153A-456 prohibits using public funds or resources to endorse or oppose a referendum on the ballot.
Individual commissioners retain First Amendment rights to voice personal views and invite public comment at the May 7 work session.
disagreements.side_b_position: Critique the Board's failure to pass an official resolution opposing Amendment One prior to early voting (raised subsequently by community advocates).
side_b_arguments: Other Triangle local governments passed formal resolutions opposing Amendment One before voting started.
disagreements.resolution: Resolution pulled on legal counsel advice; individual statements delivered and 30-minute citizen comment block scheduled for May 7.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 9, 2012 Regular Session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners recognized Human Resources benefits staff for securing $186,520 in federal Early Retiree Reimbursement Program funds and issued proclamations for Let's Move Durham Day (June 2, 2012) and National Volunteer Week (April 15-21, 2012). The Board devoted its primary policy discussion to a comprehensive resolution on hydraulic fracturing (fracking), incorporating four clauses recommended by the Environmental Affairs Board addressing regulatory compliance, road and bridge maintenance, local zoning authority, and millions of gallons of freshwater usage per well. Commissioners voted unanimously 5-0 to adopt the hydraulic fracturing resolution for transmission to the North Carolina General Assembly and the Durham legislative delegation, and separately voted 5-0 to send the resolution and supporting report to the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners while considering outreach to neighboring counties. The Board also approved minutes unanimously and recessed into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3) to discuss economic development prospects and the lawsuit Geraldine Robinson v. Joe W. Bowser and the Durham County Board of Commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page called the meeting to order, welcomed visiting graduate and undergraduate students from the North Carolina Central University Public Administration Department, and confirmed there were no agenda adjustments. Announcements covered the In Touch with Durham County broadcast schedule, Governor Perdue's 2012 Spring Litter Sweep (April 14-28), and the Friends of the Durham Library book sale (April 13-15).

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page presented the minutes from the March 26, 2012 Regular Session and the March 10, 2012 meeting for approval. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Human Resources Benefits Staff for Early Retiree Reimbursement Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Benefits Manager Diane Pearson and Interim Human Resources Director Marquito Welton for securing $186,520 in federal Early Retiree Reimbursement Program funds. Staff noted they submitted timely applications and remained in the queue for any reallocated federal funds.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for Let's Move Durham - Walk a Mile with a Child Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page read a proclamation declaring Saturday, June 2, 2012 as Let's Move Durham Day, citing childhood obesity statistics and encouraging youth participation at Solite Park along the American Tobacco Trail. Dr. Sheila Allison outlined partnerships with the school board and County Health Department, and commissioners noted Durham County ranked 8th healthiest out of 100 North Carolina counties in the University of Wisconsin rankings.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for National Volunteer Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized National Volunteer Week (April 15-21, 2012) with remarks from Chuck Hemrick, President of the North Carolina Association of Volunteer Administration, and Vaughn Brown, Volunteer Coordinator for Durham County's Welcome Baby program. Speakers highlighted the contributions of community volunteers and the Volunteer Center of Durham's annual awards.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on Hydraulic Fracturing (Fracking) to the NC General Assembly and NCACC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a hydraulic fracturing resolution incorporating four additional clauses from the Environmental Affairs Board on regulatory compliance, road and bridge maintenance, local zoning authority, and freshwater consumption, while Planning staff (Kathleen Snyder) noted Lee County had passed a similar resolution. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton sought confirmation that housing impacts referenced both city and county residents, and commissioners discussed sharing the resolution and supporting study with neighboring counties, the Durham legislative delegation, General Assembly leadership, and the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development and Pending Litigation, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled from the consent agenda, the Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business or industry location/expansion and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with the county attorney regarding Geraldine Robinson v. Joe W. Bowser and the Durham County Board of Commissioners (12 CVS-02-044). Upon returning to open session at 01:54:36, the Board reported providing direction to staff and adjourned at 8:50 PM.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 26, 2012 Regular Session and March 10, 2012 Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: All five seated commissioners were named on the meeting's hydraulic fracturing resolution.
votes.discussion_detail: No changes or objections were raised to the minutes prior to the voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Hydraulic Fracturing Resolution for NC General Assembly and Durham Legislative Delegation
votes.notes: Board also discussed sending cover letters and study links to neighboring counties in the Triassic Basin/corridor.
votes.discussion_detail: Chairman Page read the resolution citing impacts on housing valuations, mineral rights, water supply, and local zoning authority, and confirmed EAB-added clauses were included before the 5-0 voice vote.

votes.item_title: Transmission of Hydraulic Fracturing Resolution and Supporting Study to NCACC
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chairman Page asked Vice Chair Reckhow to offer a formal motion so the record reflected Board authorization to forward the resolution and study to the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3))

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: During the April 2, 2012 Worksession, the Board heard citizen comments from Ed Davis praising the planned inclusive photo mosaic for the new Durham County Courthouse and proposing a 21st-century addition to the 1920s World War I monument to unify its racially segregated casualty lists. Under urgent infrastructure business, the Board voted unanimously 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve Agenda Item 1A for emergency replacement of 850 feet of corroded ductile iron sewer force main near Hobson Road, avoiding $2,400-per-week bypass costs and main failure risk. Purchasing staff also briefed the Board on extending the Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) ordinance by one year beyond its December 31, 2012 expiration to allow time for a new disparity study, prompting commissioners to request discussions with the City of Durham on a potential joint study. The worksession concluded with FY 2012-13 budget funding presentations from local nonprofits, including Senior PharmAssist, youth literacy and athletics groups, and People's Channel, ahead of the May 29 budget presentation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page opened the April 2 worksession and recognized resident Ed Davis as the sole citizen speaker. Davis commended the inclusive photo mosaic planned for the new courthouse and urged the Board to add an inclusive 21st-century marker to the 1920s World War I monument on the old courthouse lawn, which lists fallen white and African-American soldiers separately.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Sewer Force Main Replacement near Hobson Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Utilities Assistant Director Dan Mowley requested immediate authorization to replace 850 feet of corroded ductile iron pipe on the county's largest sewer force main serving Research Triangle Park to Highway 70 near Hobson Road without a 30-day formal bid delay. Staff explained that the emergency bypass cost $2,400 per week and posed ongoing operational risks if delayed, and confirmed engineers verified the contractor's estimate as fair.

agenda_items.title: Update on Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) Ordinance and Disparity Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Purchasing Manager Jacqueline Boyce and Assistant Purchasing Manager Pamela Gales reported that the county's MWBE ordinance expires December 31, 2012, and requested a one-year consent-agenda extension at the next regular meeting alongside FY 2012-13 funding for a new five-year disparity study. Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow inquired about program metrics, database accuracy, and partnering with the City of Durham on a joint disparity study, which the County Manager agreed to raise at the upcoming City-County managers meeting.

agenda_items.title: FY 2012-13 Nonprofit Agency Funding Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community nonprofit organizations presented funding requests and service outcomes for the upcoming fiscal year, including Senior PharmAssist (expanding to 1,700 seniors with a new Community Care of North Carolina medication management contract), youth literacy and track programs, and People's Channel. Budget staff noted that funding recommendations would remain under review until the County Manager presents the budget on May 29, 2012.

votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Board suspended rules to take immediate action on an emergency utility repair during the worksession.

votes.item_title: Approval of Agenda Item 1A (Emergency Replacement of Hobson Road Sewer Force Main)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved proceeding with replacing 850 feet of corroded ductile iron force main pipe without waiting 30 days for formal bidding due to $2,400/week bypass costs and traffic/environmental risks along Hobson Road.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 26, 2012 Regular Session, the Board unanimously approved 5-0 the minutes of the February 28 school board tour and March 12 regular session, recognized Durham Center Housing Specialist Stephanie Williams for receiving a City of Durham Human Relations/Fair Housing Award, and adopted a proclamation for National County Government Month. Commissioners reviewed a Durham Public Schools Board of Education resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to eliminate state discretionary reversions—citing $32.05 million in four-year reversion losses, $11.23 million projected for 2012-13, 405 eliminated school positions, and North Carolina's 42nd national ranking in per-pupil spending—and agreed to include it in their upcoming legislative delegation meeting. The Board also reviewed 2012 short-session legislative priorities (including Memorial Stadium Authority membership, Social Services funding, and mental health guardianship), completed balloting for county advisory boards, and voted unanimously to enter closed session on open space real estate acquisitions, economic development, personnel, and attorney-client matters.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page called the meeting to order, reminded commissioners to speak directly into microphones for broadcast viewers, and read television broadcast announcements. The Board then approved the minutes from the February 28, 2012 Durham Public Schools tour and the March 12, 2012 Regular Session.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Stephanie Williams (The Durham Center Housing Specialist)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Center Director Ellen Holliman introduced Housing Specialist Stephanie Williams, who received the City of Durham's Fair Housing/Human Relations Award. Commissioners praised her work securing over $300,000 in HUD grant funds and assisting 600 individuals with housing over the prior year.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Eliminate Discretionary Reversions of Durham Public Schools Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page read a resolution from the Durham Public Schools Board of Education calling on the General Assembly to eliminate discretionary reversions, noting $4.29 million reverted in 2011-12, $11.23 million projected for 2012-13, $32.05 million in cumulative reversion losses, 405 positions cut, and North Carolina ranking 42nd in per-pupil funding ($8,565 vs. $10,976 nationally). Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Pam H. Karriker strongly endorsed adding the resolution to Thursday's legislative delegation agenda and sending it to General Assembly leadership and education committee chairs.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Boy Scout Troop 467 and National County Government Month Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page recognized visiting Boy Scout Troop 467 and its assistant scoutmasters, Paul Davis and Brent Guy. Deborah Craig-Ray then introduced a resolution designating April 2012 as National County Government Month under the theme 'Healthy Counties, Healthy Families.'

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 2012 North Carolina Short-Session Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney and Deborah Craig-Ray outlined May 2012 short-session bill-drafting deadlines and reviewed potential legislative items, including expanding the Memorial Stadium Authority from five to nine members, Social Services funding requests, mental health guardianship provisions during the LME/MCO transition, and pending state legislative issues affecting counties. Commissioners requested that Durham Public Schools and mental health representatives attend Thursday's meeting with the Durham legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk to the Board Mr. Fowler distributed and tallied ballots for county advisory boards and commissions. Appointees announced included Harrison Shannon Jr., Cynthia F. Vander Wiele (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), Lauren Wright (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), Jessica Fines (Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee), and Ronald Bijken and Jamie Dimit (Piedmont Food and Agricultural Processing Center).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to adjourn into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding open space acquisition at Wake Forest Highway and 103 Santee Road, (a)(4) for business/industry location or expansion, (a)(6) for public officer/employee qualifications, and (a)(3) for attorney-client consultation. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Chairman Michael D. Page excused, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided over the March 12, 2012 Regular Session, where the four present commissioners passed every formal action unanimously 4-0. The Board approved three sets of minutes, recognized Soil and Water Conservation District award winners Daniel Adams and Jennifer Brooks, proclaimed March 2012 as Professional Social Work Month, and honored Girl Scout Bronze Award recipient Pearl A. Janice. On the consent agenda, the Board unanimously approved eight items including LME/MCO board appointments, $769,576 in human services grant revenues, a $2,255,880 courthouse construction contract allowance increase for contaminated soil and stormwater shoring within the existing $82.48 million budget, and transferring a vacant DSS position to create a Strategic Initiatives Manager. Following public hearings, the Board voted 4-0 to authorize up to $17 million in refunding bonds and up to $60 million in general obligation bonds to retire bond anticipation notes, and adopted Unified Development Ordinance text amendments regulating electric fences and establishing transit-oriented Compact Design Districts.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided in place of Chairman Michael D. Page (excused), announced Item 10 had been removed or delayed, and read Durham County TV broadcast schedules. The four present commissioners then unanimously approved three sets of prior meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Soil and Water Awards, Professional Social Work Month Proclamation, and Girl Scout Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and staff presented state Soil and Water Conservation District awards to Supervisor of the Year Daniel Adams and Outstanding Environmental Educator of the Year Jennifer Brooks. Vice Chair Reckhow then read a proclamation declaring March 2012 Professional Social Work Month for DSS Director Gayle Perry and recognized Girl Scout Pearl A. Janice on the Girl Scouts' 100th anniversary for earning the Bronze Award.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-H)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered an eight-item consent agenda covering the ABC Board chair appointment, ambulance franchise actions, Piedmont Food and Agricultural Processing Center nonprofit bylaws, Durham Center LME/MCO board appointments, $769,576 in social services crisis/energy/home care revenues, a $2,255,880 courthouse allowance increase for contaminated soil and NCDOT stormwater shoring within the $82,478,060 construction budget, and transferring $48,152 and a vacant DSS position to create a Strategic Initiatives Manager.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on General Obligation Refunding and Public Improvement Bonds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick requested increasing the refunding bond cap from $16.5 million to an amount not to exceed $17 million to accommodate market fluctuations while exceeding the Local Government Commission's 3% savings threshold, alongside issuing up to $60 million in general obligation bonds to retire temporary bond anticipation notes for school and capital construction. No members of the public spoke during the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Ratification of 2011 Comprehensive Plan Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Keith Luck of the City-County Planning Department presented the annual mutual ratification of 2011 Future Land Use Map and Comprehensive Plan amendments adopted by the City of Durham and Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on UDO Text Amendment for Electric Fences and Fence Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment requested by Sentry Security establishing usage, dimensional, and locational standards for electric fences and removing redundant quasi-judicial special use hearings when a Certificate of Appropriateness is required. Two applicant representatives (Keith Burns and Cindy Giselle) spoke in support, and the Board approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Compact Design District UDO Text Amendment (TC1000005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Lisa Miller presented text amendment TC1000005 establishing a framework for transit-oriented Compact Design Districts (modeled on the Ninth Street plan, with the North RTP station next), including Core and Support tiers, street-oriented building frontages, and maximum parking caps with a 20% by-right reduction. Vice Chair Reckhow noted the rules would have blocked the Hillsborough Road Harris Teeter site plan had they been adopted earlier, and after opening and closing a properly advertised public hearing, the Board approved the ordinance and adjourned at 7:52 PM.

votes.notes: Chairman Michael D. Page was excused from this meeting (per Feb 27 motion and Reckhow's opening announcement).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 27, 2012 Regular Session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the February 13 minutes 5-0, adopted ceremonial resolutions honoring the Braggtown Branch Library's 50th anniversary and paying tribute to the late Mary Duke Biddle Trent Semans, and passed the consent agenda unanimously 5-0. Commissioners also discussed an upcoming roughly $74 million bond and refunding package, and reviewed the expired 2005 Memorandum of Understanding between the Board of Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, expressing broad agreement on restoring regular year-round joint communication prior to budget season. Triangle Transit and Cooperative Extension staff presented the I-40 Bus on Shoulder System (BOSS) pilot initiative, and the Board completed ballot appointments to the City-County Planning Commission and other advisory bodies. The Board concluded by voting unanimously to enter closed session on business location and attorney-client matters and voting to excuse Chairman Michael D. Page from the March 12, 2012 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page called the meeting to order and accepted Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow's agenda adjustment to discuss the expired 2005 BOCC-Durham Public Schools Memorandum of Understanding, as well as a query regarding a Child Fatality Prevention Team item. The Board then approved the February 13, 2012 Regular Session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Congratulating Braggtown Branch Library on 50 Years of Service
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page read a resolution celebrating the 50th anniversary of the Braggtown Library Family Literacy Center, which opened March 11, 1962 on land funded and deeded by neighborhood residents. Library Director Tammy Baggett, Youth Services Coordinator Carleen, and Branch Manager Anita Speed-Hasty invited the community to the March 9 celebration and described the library's 'Garden of Wonders' children's garden.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring the Memory of Mary Duke Biddle Trent Semans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page read a memorial resolution honoring Mary Duke Biddle Trent Semans for her lifelong civic leadership, philanthropy, and service as one of the first two women elected to the Durham City Council and Mayor Pro Tem from 1953 to 1955.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Bond Refunding Clarification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved the consent agenda 5-0. On Item 10, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked for clarification on the bond issuance and refunding form; staff explained the public hearing request covered a roughly $74 million total issue including refunding bonds expected to yield approximately 8% (over $1 million) in four-year savings.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of BOCC and Durham Public Schools Board of Education MOU
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow distributed the 2005-expired Memorandum of Understanding between the Board of Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education as a framework to improve regular year-round communication, shared academic priorities, and budget reporting. Chairman Page, Commissioner Howerton, and other commissioners supported updating the working document and scheduling ongoing joint meetings with the school board ahead of the budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Presentation on I-40 Regional Partnership Bus on Shoulder System (BOSS) Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Tallmadge of Triangle Transit and Mobility Manager Margaret Scully presented the I-40 corridor Bus on Shoulder System (BOSS) pilot project for Durham County. Staff detailed NCDOT shoulder width, pinch-point, and rumble-strip safety evaluations intended to improve express bus reliability during traffic congestion.

agenda_items.title: Child Fatality Team Inquiry and Board/Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While ballots were tallied, a commissioner raised a constituent concern from a member rotated off the Child Fatality Prevention Team. Clerk Mr. Fowler then announced ballot selections including Sharon Mullen and Robert Tier to the City-County Planning Commission and Charles A. Gibbs to the Lebanon Township seat.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Chairman Excusal, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (business or industry location/expansion) and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (attorney-client privilege). Returning to open session at 02:19:06, the Board reported giving direction to staff, voted 5-0 to excuse Chairman Page from the March 12, 2012 meeting, and adjourned at 9:18 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The February 13, 2012 Regular Session opened with Chairman Michael D. Page's annual State of the County address, reviewing Durham's AAA credit rating, 98.88% tax collection rate, November 2011 local sales tax referenda, anti-crime efforts in Northeast Central Durham, Commissioner Pam H. Karriker's interim appointment following Becky Heron's retirement, and the launch of the county's Strategic Plan. The Board unanimously approved 5-0 three sets of prior meeting minutes and honored Dr. William Birch for 15 years of service on the Board of Health. Commissioners unanimously approved 5-0 both the Durham Center LME/MCO merger agreement and facility lease, and adopted 5-0 the Board of Health smoking rule as the Durham County Smoking Ordinance prohibiting smoking on city and county parks, grounds, trails, and bus stops with a six-month educational rollout. Finally, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the Durham County Strategic Plan developed with nearly 3,000 residents and recessed into closed session under attorney-client privilege.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, State of the County Address, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page delivered his fourth annual State of the County address, highlighting Durham's recognition as the #1 most tolerant city, Pam H. Karriker's appointment succeeding retired Commissioner Becky Heron, sluggish economic recovery alongside a lean budget and 98.88% tax collection rate, maintenance of the county's AAA credit rating, voter-approved sales tax referenda, anti-crime enforcement in Northeast Central Durham, and the forthcoming Strategic Plan. Announcements also noted the Northgate Mall free tax/legal clinic and a February 19 library program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page presented the minutes from the December 12, 2011 Regular Session, January 3, 2012 Worksession, and January 9, 2012 Regular Session. The Board approved all three sets unanimously 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Dr. William Birch (15 Years on the Board of Health)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page and Public Health Director Gayle Harris honored Dr. William Birch with a resolution recognizing 15 years of service on the Durham County Board of Health.

agenda_items.title: Durham Center LME/MCO Merger Agreement and Lease
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Board discussion, the Board approved the Durham Center LME/MCO merger agreement and lease unanimously 5-0. Durham Center Director Ellen Holliman thanked the commissioners and recognized Wake County Manager David Cooke in attendance.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Durham County Smoking Ordinance and Budget Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gayle Harris, Board of Health Chair Sue McLaurin, and Vice Chair Dr. Jim Miller presented the Board of Health's smoking rule for adoption as a Durham County ordinance alongside an implementing budget amendment. Extending beyond state law (S.L. 2009-27), the ordinance prohibits smoking on City of Durham grounds and parks, city and county bus stops and the transportation center, and county grounds, trails, and parks, backed by a six-month education and cessation campaign.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of the Durham County Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin and staff presenter Michael submitted the Durham County Strategic Plan after over a year of work by an interdepartmental team, consultants, and nearly 3,000 community participants. Staff introduced five Goal Champions tasked with aligning budget decisions and performance metrics ahead of the upcoming budget retreat, and the Board adopted the plan 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Attorney-Client Privilege and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled from consent, the Board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation. Returning to open session at 03:07:07, the Board reported providing direction to staff and adjourned at 10:05 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: In its first regular session of 2012 on January 9, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the December 5, 2011 worksession minutes 5-0 and recognized The Durham Center for winning two statewide Programs of Excellence awards for its crisis center and uninsured clinical assessment partnership with CJRC. During earlier comments, speakers addressed concealed-carry gun permit distinctions in crime discussions and defended the DSS Board's closed-session temporary hiring decisions made with county attorney counsel while questioning why qualified Durham residents were passed over for external applicants in other hires. The Board passed consent items A-C and E-G unanimously 5-0 while pulling Item D ($2,184,294 child welfare and childcare budget amendment) for clarification from DSS Director Gayle Perry, who warned that state funding cuts left the county unable to clear its childcare waitlist. Following uncontested public hearings, the Board also voted 5-0 to approve the $149,832 Section 5311 Community Transportation grant application, 5-0 to permanently close a 165-foot segment of South Middle Springs Road, and 5-0 to approve pulled Consent Item D.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Citizen/Board Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Michael D. Page opened the first meeting of 2012 with announcements including library humanities programming, a January 11 DCHC MPO rail transit public hearing, DATA bus route workshops, and an MLK observance featuring Chief District Court Judge Marcia Morey. Later remarks addressed distinguishing lawful gun permit holders from criminal offenders, defended the DSS Board's closed-session temporary employment actions taken with two county attorneys present, and raised concerns over Durham County job applicants being passed over for candidates from Wake and Franklin counties.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 5, 2011 Worksession Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Page presented the December 5, 2011 worksession minutes for approval. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser seconded.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of The Durham Center (2011 Programs of Excellence Awards)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Area Director Ellen Holliman and Area Board Chair LaSalle Webley accepted Board recognition for two of seven annual statewide Programs of Excellence awards from the NC Council for Community Programs. The awards honored Durham Center Access for crisis response and the Durham Center/CJRC clinical assessment team serving uninsured Durham residents.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-C, E-G; Item D Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow requested pulling Consent Item D for questions regarding childcare funding. The Board unanimously approved the remaining consent items (A, B, C, E, F, and G) 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2012-13 Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Mobility Manager Delphine presented the annual NCDOT Section 5311 grant request for $149,832 (with an $18,125 local match) to fund an administrative position and replace two lift-equipped vans. After an uncontested public hearing with no speakers, the Board approved the grant application and resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Street Closing: South Middle Springs Road (SC1100001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an order to permanently close a 165-linear-foot right-of-way segment at the southern terminus of South Middle Springs Road at Sherron Road, which became redundant after a 2003 roadway realignment and affects no property access. Applicant Ronald Horvath attended to answer questions, and following a public hearing with no opposition, the Board approved the closing order 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item D: Budget Ordinance Amendment 12BCC000045 (Child Welfare & Childcare)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow asked DSS Director Gayle Perry whether the $2,171,120 childcare portion of Budget Ordinance Amendment 12BCC000045 ($2,184,294 total) would allow families to move off the waitlist. Perry explained that DSS conservatively budgets 75% ($12 million) of anticipated state/federal funds and spends near capacity ($14 million actual after a $2 million state subsidy cut), meaning roughly one-eighth fewer children could be served overall; commissioners also noted the local job impact for childcare providers before approving Item D 5-0 and adjourning at 7:46 PM.

votes.item_title: Approval of December 5, 2011 Worksession Minutes
votes.notes: All five commissioners confirmed present by subsequent 5-0 tallies.
votes.discussion_detail: Minutes approved by unanimous voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of FY 2012-13 Section 5311 Community Transportation Grant Application
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $149,832 NCDOT grant application ($18,125 local match) and authorizing resolution following public hearing.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Street Closing Order for South Middle Springs Road (SC1100001)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved permanently closing a 165-linear-foot terminating right-of-way segment at South Middle Springs Road and Sherron Road.

votes.item_title: Approval of Pulled Consent Item D (Budget Ordinance Amendment 12BCC000045)
votes.notes: Unanimous 5-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $2,184,294 budget amendment for child welfare monthly caseworker visits and childcare subsidies after DSS Director Gayle Perry explained state cuts and waitlist impacts.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 12, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved all formal actions unanimously (5-0), with no split or contested votes. Commissioners recognized outgoing Sheriff Worth Hill for 47 years in law enforcement, celebrated the County Cares federated employee campaign raising $80,164.62 above its $75,000 goal, and accepted the 2011 North Carolina School Boards Association County Commissioners Award and US Green Building Council Triangle Chapter Municipality of the Year recognition. Following a public hearing, the Board unanimously approved the Durham Trails and Greenways 2011 Master Plan Update (5-0) and unanimously passed the Consent Agenda Items A through K (5-0). After a lengthy closed session regarding personnel and attorney-client privilege, the Board reconvened and voted 5-0 to set incoming Sheriff Mike Andrews's salary at $123,640.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting with the Pledge of Allegiance, adjusted the agenda to add recognitions for the Eno River Association and outgoing Sheriff Worth Hill plus a library meeting-room discussion item before closed session, and read county announcements. Announcements included the December 15, 2011 pre-application deadline for FY 2012-13 nonprofit funding, the DSS Share Your Christmas program, and thanks to residents for strategic plan input.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the November 28, 2011 Regular Session and the November 21, 2011 Strategic Plan Town Hall Meeting. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Outgoing Sheriff Worth Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored outgoing Sheriff Worth Hill for 47 years in law enforcement and praised his department's professionalism despite budget cuts. Sheriff Hill thanked his staff and community, and commissioners noted they looked forward to working with incoming Sheriff Mike Andrews.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Cares Federated Campaign Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff announced Nina as permanent County Cares Campaign Chair and reported on the inaugural year of a federated campaign format allowing employees to vote on recipient charities alongside United Way and JDRF. The five-week campaign (Sept 29 to Nov 3) raised $80,164.62 against a $75,000 goal, benefiting organizations including John Avery Boys and Girls Club, Susan G. Komen NC Triangle Affiliate, and Durham Rescue Mission.

agenda_items.title: NCSBA Award, USGBC Sustainability Recognition, and Community Speakers (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board acknowledged receiving the 2011 County Commissioners Award from the North Carolina School Boards Association on November 15 for collaborative FY 2011-12 school budget relations with the Board of Education. Commissioners also recognized Tobin Freid and staff along with the City of Durham for being named Municipality of the Year by the US Green Building Council Triangle Chapter, and heard remarks from local pastors and youth role models.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through K) (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented Consent Agenda Items A through K, noting no items were pulled by citizens or commissioners. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the consent agenda passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Durham Trails and Greenways 2011 Master Plan Update (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Helen Youngblood of City-County Planning presented the 2011 Master Plan Update recommended by the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission, highlighting revised project priorities, connections to schools and libraries, and regional Triangle J COG and NCDOT coordination toward RTP. Following a public hearing in which Trails Commission Chair John Goebel spoke in support and noted a $55,000 matching grant for a Mountains-to-Sea Trail bridge, the Board unanimously approved the update.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Item 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk to the Board distributed appointment ballots while commissioners briefly discussed scheduling a January 3 iPad training session. Ballots were tallied and appointment selections were read into the record at 01:12:31.

agenda_items.title: Library Meeting Room Reservation Policy Inquiry (Item 12a)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner raised a question comparing Durham library meeting-room access with neighboring Orange County facilities. Library staff clarified that meeting rooms require reservations in advance, though unreserved empty rooms can be used if available.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Incoming Sheriff Salary Determination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) (personnel) and 143-318.11(a)(3) (attorney-client privilege). Upon reconvening at 03:36:53 after providing staff direction on two of three closed-session items, the Board voted 5-0 to set the incoming Sheriff's salary at $123,640.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (November 21 and November 28, 2011)
votes.notes: Voice vote announced as carrying 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of the November 28, 2011 Regular Session and November 21, 2011 Strategic Plan Town Hall Meeting.

votes.item_title: Durham Trails and Greenways 2011 Master Plan Update
votes.notes: Seconder was not named on the record; motion carried 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 2011 Master Plan Update following staff presentation and public hearing remarks from Trails Commission Chair John Goebel.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3))
votes.notes: Voice vote announced as carrying 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adjourned into closed session to consider personnel qualifications/conditions of employment and consult with legal counsel.

votes.item_title: Set Incoming Sheriff Salary at $123,640
votes.notes: Voice vote announced as carrying 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Following closed session, set the compensation for incoming Sheriff Mike Andrews at $123,640.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 28, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton absent and excused), the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously adopted the resolution levying the voter-approved quarter-cent Article 46 county sales and use tax effective April 1, 2012 (4-0) and approved Consent Agenda Items A-E and H-N (4-0). Commissioners recognized Boy Scout Troop 137 and co-chairs of the grassroots sales tax campaign, and held a public hearing on rezoning case Z11-00016 (Claremont Acres) prior to a truncated transcript gap. On pulled consent items, the Board unanimously approved Item 10F expanding the FY 2012 ERP/HR upgrade capital project to $2.6 million with a Valtech Inc. contract and $1.75 million borrowing authorization (4-0), but divided 3-1 on Consent Item 10G, which passed with Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Pam H. Karriker voting Aye and Joe W. Bowser voting Nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Absent Member, Boy Scout Recognition, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting with the Pledge of Allegiance, noted Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's excused absence, and welcomed Boy Scout Troop 137. He also announced the FY 2012-13 nonprofit funding pre-application deadline (December 15) and the DSS Share Your Christmas program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the November 7 and November 10 Strategic Plan Town Hall Meetings and the November 14 Regular Session with distributed revisions. On a motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Pam H. Karriker, the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Education Sales Tax Campaign Leaders (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners recognized campaign co-chairs Meredith Holmes, Steve, John White, Casey, and Glenn for their grassroots effort leading to voter approval of the quarter-cent sales tax referendum on a modest budget.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-E and H-N) (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow commended the Sheriff's Office on Item C for aggressively pursuing outside grant resources, while Items F and G were pulled for separate discussion at Item 10. On a motion by Vice Chair Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Pam H. Karriker, the remaining consent items passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z11-00016 (Claremont Acres) (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Z11-00016 by Patterson Park LLC to rezone 4.88 acres across nine non-contiguous parcels on Closs/Clausen Drive from Rural Residential to RS-20 to allow reduced setbacks and home siting outside the floodplain, noting a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Staff confirmed buildable envelopes exist outside the floodplain on the two floodplain-impacted lots, and speaker Bill Ripley testified in support before a truncated gap in the transcript prior to any recorded vote.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Levying Quarter-Cent County Sales and Use Tax (Article 46)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the truncated gap, the Board reviewed the formal resolution levying the voter-approved quarter-cent county sales and use tax effective April 1, 2012 (exempting food and drugs), projected to yield $2.3 million in FY 2012 ($200,000 pledged toward $400,000 for Partnership for Children and $2.1 million unpledged). Vice Chair Reckhow clarified that the separate voter-approved transit tax would not be levied until Wake and Orange Counties act, and the Board approved the Article 46 resolution 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk distributed ballots for advisory board appointments. Results announced at 00:32:48 included selections for the Alcohol and Beverage Control Board, Animal Control Review Board, and Community Child Protection Team.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 10F: FY 2012 ERP/HR Upgrade Capital Project (DCOA4) & Valtech Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Joe W. Bowser pulled Item F to question moving $600,000 in unspent funds from the 2010 ERP upgrade (DCOA3) to increase DCOA4 to $2.6 million, executing a $2,046,888 Valtech Inc. contract for SAP ECC 6.5 HCM implementation, and borrowing $1,750,000, asking if the project could wait given economic conditions. Staff explained the software components had been deferred from Phase 1 under the approved CIP and any project savings would lower the borrowing amount, after which the Board approved Item F 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 10G
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Joe W. Bowser stated without extended debate that he would vote against Item G (whose subject is not detailed in the transcript digest). On a motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Pam H. Karriker, Item G passed 3-1 with Bowser opposed.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Business Location or Expansion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously (4-0) to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of a business or industry. Upon reconvening at 00:58:12, the Chair reported direction was given to staff and adjourned the meeting at 8:00 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 14, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow (with Chair Michael D. Page and Commissioner Pam H. Karriker absent and excused), the Durham Board of County Commissioners passed all items unanimously (3-0), with no split or contested votes. The Board heard Mental Health staff member Tawanda Witherspoon perform the National Anthem, recognized Register of Deeds Willie L. Covington for winning the Federation of Genealogical Societies Archives Award for vital records preservation, and highlighted the $6.25 million five-year Bristol-Myers Squibb Foundation Durham Diabetes Coalition grant with Duke Medical Center. Commissioners unanimously approved the unpulled Consent Agenda items (3-0) as well as pulled Consent Item H (Durham Center/Sheriff's Office charity softball proceeds, 3-0) and Consent Item K (Lincoln Community Health Center federal grant renovation amendments, 3-0), before meeting in closed session on litigation involving Chancellor's Ridge HOA and excusing Brenda A. Howerton from the November 28 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Absent Members, National Anthem, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided and opened with a unanimous 3-0 vote excusing Chair Michael D. Page and Commissioner Pam H. Karriker. Mental Health staff member Tawanda Witherspoon sang the National Anthem, Item 6A was removed and Item 8 added, and announcements covered the December 15 nonprofit pre-application deadline and the November 21 Strategic Plan Town Hall at East Regional Library.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (October 24, 2011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow presented the minutes from the October 24, 2011 Regular Session. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Commissioner Joe W. Bowser, the minutes were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Register of Deeds Willie L. Covington
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners recognized Register of Deeds Willie L. Covington for receiving the Federation of Genealogical Societies Archives Award in September for preserving deteriorating Durham County vital records. Covington credited the Board's funding support and Vital Records staff led by Mary Deeds.

With Item 6A removed and Items H and K pulled, the remaining consent items passed 3-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Joe W. Bowser pulled Item H to spotlight employee charity fundraising from the Durham Center–Sheriff's Office softball challenge benefiting Stewards for Children and homeless housing assistance. Durham Center Director Ellen Holliman, coach Felicia McPherson, and Tawanda Witherspoon shared remarks before the Board approved the item 3-0.

Washington Group within the $917,154 budget) to verify whether D. Washington Group was local and whether the funds would complete the project. Staff confirmed D. Washington Group is a local firm and that favorable 2009 federal grant bids left $116,000 for additional renovations, after which the Board approved Item K 3-0.

Howerton from the November 28 meeting and adjourned at 7:37 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 24, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners discussed community responses to a recent drive-by shooting on Driver Avenue that injured two children, issued proclamations for National Adoption Month and Veterans Day, and presented a resolution calling on Congress and President Obama to 'bring our war dollars home.' The Board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0) and Consent Agenda Items A through I (5-0). On Item 10 (Human Services Janitorial Services RFP 11-028 Phase 1 and Phase 2), commissioners split 4-1, with Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, and Pam H. Karriker voting Aye to approve the contract after staff negotiated $53,000 in Phase 2 savings, and Joe W. Bowser voting Nay because the incumbent firm was replaced without being given a chance to negotiate pricing. Balloting for the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council filled five seats and resulted in a three-way tie for the sixth slot, which was deferred to the next work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Discussion of Youth Gun Violence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and announced November Strategic Plan town hall forums, the FY 2012-13 nonprofit funding pre-application window, and a Ken Burns film screening. Commissioners then discussed a drive-by shooting on Driver Avenue that injured two children and recurring drive-by shootings in 2011, calling for better data and coordination with the Sheriff's Office and police (with a community meeting noted for the next evening at Shepherd's House Church).

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the October 3 Work Session, October 10 Regular Session, and September 12 Special Session. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were approved 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Adoption Month (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented a proclamation recognizing November as National Adoption Month to Department of Social Services staff including Janice Williams, Jovetta Whitfield, and John Holcamp, emphasizing the need for adoptive and foster families.

agenda_items.title: Resolution: Veterans Day and Employment Announcements (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution declaring November 11, 2011 as Veterans Day in Durham County and recognizing nearly 17,000 county veterans alongside Veterans Services Director Lou Washington. Additional remarks noted a veterans stand-down event and FedEx hiring 100 drivers.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Presentation (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated gap in the transcript, Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Executive Director Shelley Green presented an application/project update to the Board, and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow thanked her and staff for assembling the submission.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Calling to Bring War Dollars Home (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution signed by all five commissioners calling upon Congress and President Barack Obama to responsibly end the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and redirect military spending ($30.9 billion estimated North Carolina taxpayer share) toward local education, jobs, healthcare, housing, and infrastructure. Betsy Crites and NC Peace Action accepted the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through I) (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented Consent Agenda Items A through I with no items pulled by citizens or commissioners. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Human Services Janitorial Services Contract RFP 11-028 (Phases 1 and 2) (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff returned with RFP 11-028 for Human Services janitorial services after negotiating $53,000 in Phase 2 savings. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser opposed replacing a proven incumbent vendor with a firm serving Fayetteville State dormitories without allowing the incumbent to negotiate pricing, while Vice Chair Reckhow praised the $53,000 savings; the contract passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners praised the high quality of applicants for the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council and cast written ballots. Five candidates won seats (including Jennifer Rogers, Ronald Dennis, Ann Mosley, and Herman Scott), while a three-way tie (two votes each) for the sixth seat was deferred to the next work session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 10, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously appointed Mike Andrews by ballot to replace retiring Sheriff Worth Hill effective January 1, 2012, following a 4:00 PM special-session interview of four candidates (Mike Andrews, Rickey Hart, Roy Taylor, and Tony Butler). Commissioners also adopted an amended resolution memorializing the Board's intent to dedicate proceeds of the November 8 quarter-cent Article 46 sales tax referendum (projected at $9.2 million initially, plus $200,000 toward $400,000 for Partnership for Children) to public education for an initial 10-year period, after amending the language to vest allocation decisions in the Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees and Partnership for Children Board of Directors rather than individual executives. Earlier in the session, the Board approved prior minutes unanimously, proclaimed October 2011 as Community Planning Month, and passed Consent Agenda Items A through G unanimously, with no split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the regular session, noted the 4:00 PM special session held earlier, and announced that Items 6 and 7 were pulled from the agenda. Announcements highlighted the City-County Sustainability Office's Home Energy Retrofit Program (greenerdurham.net, first 200 homes) and a November 1 youth civic event.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 12 and September 26, 2011) (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the September 12 and September 26, 2011 Regular Sessions. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Replacement Sheriff (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Sheriff Worth Hill's resignation effective January 1, 2012 and afternoon interviews of candidates Mike Andrews, Rickey Hart, Roy Taylor, and Tony Butler (which Chair Page noted he missed due to a funeral), the Board voted unanimously by ballot to appoint Mike Andrews as Sheriff. Andrews thanked his family, Sheriff Hill, and Sheriff's Office staff.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Intent for Article 46 Quarter-Cent Sales Tax Proceeds (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution expressing the Board's intent to use proceeds of the November 8 quarter-cent sales tax referendum (~$9.2M initial annual revenue) for public education over an initial 10-year period, including Durham Tech scholarships and $400,000 for Durham Partnership for Children. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser emphasized that the resolution cannot legally bind future boards, and Chair Page, Bowser, and Vice Chair Reckhow agreed to amend the text so spending decisions require backing by the Durham Tech Board of Trustees and Partnership for Children Board of Directors before approving the amended resolution unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Community Planning Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin and Planning Supervisor Terry Danler accepted a proclamation declaring October 2011 as Community Planning Month. Staff highlighted upcoming October 27 mock rezoning and visioning activities for high school students and November Comprehensive Plan update workshops across county quadrants.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through G) (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled by citizens or commissioners, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items A through G on a motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and adjourned at 7:35 PM.

votes.notes: Tallied by written ballot and announced as unanimous.

votes.item_title: Amended Resolution Memorializing Intent for Article 46 Quarter-Cent Sales Tax Proceeds
votes.notes: No opposition was voiced when the Chair called 'all opposed'; transcript ASR rendered the announced tally as 'Five to three', an apparent ASR error for 'Five to zero' given the five-member Board and unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted resolution stating Board intent to dedicate Article 46 sales tax revenues to public education for 10 years, amended to vest allocation accountability with the Durham Tech Board of Trustees and Partnership for Children Board of Directors.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Binding Effect and Governance Oversight of Article 46 Education Sales Tax Resolution
disagreements.summary: During consideration of the resolution pledging quarter-cent sales tax proceeds to public education, commissioners debated whether the resolution bound future boards and whether spending authority should rest with institutional executives or governing boards.
disagreements.side_a_position: Clarify non-binding nature and require governing-board accountability
side_a_arguments: One Board of County Commissioners cannot legally bind a future board, which could redirect proceeds.
Vesting allocation decisions in two individual executives rather than the Durham Tech Board of Trustees and Durham Partnership for Children Board of Directors weakens accountability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Resolution establishes durable practical commitment once programs begin
side_b_arguments: While legally non-binding on future boards, unwinding established need-based Durham Tech scholarships would be practically and politically difficult.
Supported amending the draft to involve both governing boards alongside institutional leaders.
disagreements.resolution: The Board unanimously agreed to amend the resolution to reference the Durham Tech Board of Trustees and Partnership for Children Board of Directors and approved the amended resolution without opposition.

Palmer for four months of service, and proclaimed National Long-Term Care Residents' Rights Month. Howerton seconded and voted Aye among the four seated commissioners present (Page, Reckhow, Bowser, and Howerton), while the truncated digest does not identify which of the remaining three members cast the lone Nay vote. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Department of Social Services (DSS) Governance, Interim Salaries, and Public Accusations
disagreements.summary: Although the Board ultimately voted 4-0 to refer a 10-point list to the state for investigation, commissioners clashed sharply over media statements, interim director pay, and whether unsubstantiated accusations were worsening morale across 400+ DSS employees.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defend interim DSS salary motion and investigate all DSS rumors and board actions
side_a_arguments: The salary motion for interim directors Gail Perry and Jovetta Whitfield intended to match Ms. Robinson's pay (with an honest $129,000 vs. $139,000 figure mistake).
All outstanding allegations—including DSS Board appointments, illegal meetings, dismissal votes, relationships, and fundraising—should be examined by the state to end gossip and innuendo.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support an objective investigation while condemning divisive public accusations without proof
side_b_arguments: Elected officials should not make unproven public accusations or call colleagues 'flat-faced liars' in the press.
Divisiveness among the Board has damaged morale among more than 400 DSS employees, and all 10 raised items—including allegations affecting Ms. Hughes—should be handled responsibly.
disagreements.resolution: Passed unanimously (4-0) on a motion by Joe W. Bowser seconded by Ellen W. Reckhow to submit the 10-item list for state investigation.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 22, 2011 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page with four seated commissioners present (Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, Joe W. Bowser, and Brenda A. Howerton), the Durham Board of County Commissioners passed all formal votes unanimously (4-0), with no split or contested votes. Chair Page reported giving direction to staff in a 6:00 PM closed session, and Commissioner Bowser used announcements to refute claims that he had unilaterally dismissed three county employees. Commissioners honored Commissioner Howerton for achieving Master status in the Local Elected Leaders Academy and County Attorney Lowell Siler for becoming President of the NC Association of County Attorneys, proclaimed September as Mental Illness and Addiction Recovery Month, approved the Consent Agenda (4-0), and approved NCDOT's Secondary Road Construction Program (4-0) after questioning statewide funding reductions. Chair Page also announced September 6, 7, and 12 special-session dates to interview candidates and select a replacement for retired Commissioner Becky M. Heron.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Closed Session Report, Announcements, and Commissioner Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page reported that the Board met in closed session at 6:00 PM and provided direction to staff, then announced Board of Health Community Health Assessment listening sessions and a library video contest. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser spoke on personal privilege to refute statements claiming he had fired three people, noting dismissals require three board votes.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (August 1 and August 8, 2011) (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the August 1 Work Session and August 8 Regular Session. On a motion by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions and Mental Illness and Addiction Recovery Proclamation (Items 5-7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners recognized Brenda A. Howerton for earning Master status in the Local Elected Leaders Academy and County Attorney Lowell Siler on his election as President of the NC Association of County Attorneys. The Board also presented a proclamation declaring September as Mental Illness and Addiction Recovery Month to Ellen Holliman and mental health partners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through K) (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled by citizens or commissioners, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items A through K on a voice vote (seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: NCDOT Secondary Road Construction Program (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NCDOT Acting District Engineer Michelle Gray and Division Maintenance Engineer Brandon Jones presented the secondary road construction program. Commissioners questioned statewide secondary road funding reductions (explained as tied to the state budget and allocated by unpaved road mileage) and confirmed a 0.26-mile border listing; following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board approved the program 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments & Vacancy Interview Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While ballots were distributed for advisory boards, Chair Page announced dates for filling the vacant County Commissioner seat: September 6 at 1:00 PM for public candidate interviews, September 7 at 1:30 PM for work session, and September 12 at 4:00 PM for deliberations. The Clerk announced appointees across nine boards and committees before adjournment at 7:38 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioner Becky M. Heron opened the June 27, 2011 regular session by announcing her retirement effective August 1, 2011 on medical advice after nearly three decades of service since 1982, prompting tributes from Chair Michael D. Page and fellow commissioners. Following a middle segment omitted from the transcript digest, the Board unanimously approved (5-0) minutes with lottery-fund clarifications, an architectural contract amendment for building renovations, the Downtown Durham Inc. economic development contract, an extension of the Quintiles Transnational One NC match incentive agreement, and NCACC voting delegates. On two contested consent items, the Board passed a school capital project amendment for 2007 bond technology and equipment funds (Item U) by a 4-1 voice vote—with Ayes including mover Ellen W. Reckhow, seconder Brenda A. Howerton, Chair Michael D. Page, and one additional commissioner, against 1 unnamed Nay (either Joe W. Bowser or Becky M. Heron) who questioned facility spending amid flat enrollment—and approved a new gang strategy coordinator position (Item AA) by a 4-1 voice vote, with Ayes including mover Brenda A. Howerton, seconder Becky M. Heron, Chair Michael D. Page, and one additional commissioner against 1 unnamed Nay (either Joe W. Bowser or Ellen W. Reckhow) who opposed adding staff positions during economic hardship. The meeting concluded with appointments to nine county advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Retirement Announcement by Commissioner Becky M. Heron
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page led the Pledge of Allegiance, confirmed agenda adjustments, and shared county television and DSS foster care recruitment announcements. Commissioner Becky M. Heron then announced she would step down effective August 1, 2011 on medical advice after serving since 1982, reflecting on moving meetings to 7:00 p.m., being the first woman elected chair, and her work on environmental, planning, transit, mental health, education, and senior issues; fellow commissioners offered tributes.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (June 6 Work Session and June 13 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the June 6 work session and June 13 regular session minutes. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested clarifying additions to the June 6 minutes regarding Jack Morgan and concerns about how lottery funds were being shifted rather than used for their originally stated purposes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Durham Center Director Ellen Holloman

agenda_items.title: Architectural Services Contract Amendment for Expanded Building Renovation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned why an architectural contract amendment expanded project scope beyond the original plan. Staff explained that initial architectural work uncovered additional issues and functional deficiencies in crew quarters and office areas, expanding the project to a full renovation within the existing $2,063,049 capital improvement project budget.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Inc. Economic Development Contract

Staff clarified the 2007 bond-eligible funds would purchase media center and curriculum equipment for Lakewood Montessori and technology needed for the City of Medicine Academy facility.
