disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: School Capital Project Amendment and Renovation Spending (Consent Item U)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over a 2007 bond-funded capital project amendment for school equipment and technology, with one commissioner questioning ongoing school facility construction and renovation amid flat enrollment and tough economic conditions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 2007 bond-eligible capital project amendment to provide needed curriculum equipment and facility technology.
side_a_arguments: Funds cover media center and curriculum-specific equipment for Lakewood Montessori and essential technology needs in the new City of Medicine Academy facility.
Withholding the funds would be detrimental to the curriculum of the three affected facilities, and the expenditures are eligible under the 2007 bonds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the capital project amendment and question continued facility building and renovation spending during hard times for Durham Public Schools.
side_b_arguments: The number of students in Durham Public Schools is not increasing, making new building and large facility projects questionable.
Spending on projects such as the old YMCA recreation center renovation is difficult to justify without student growth while the legislature pressures school budgets.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 on a voice vote; the single dissenting commissioner (either Joe W. Bowser or Becky M. Heron) was not explicitly named on the record.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Creation of Gang Strategy Coordinator Position (Consent Item AA)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners divided 4-1 over funding a new coordinator position to implement the county's gang reduction strategy, balancing accountability safeguards against opposition to adding county staff during economic hardship.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the gang strategy coordinator position while requiring clear outcome metrics and a one-year evaluation.
side_a_arguments: The position is needed to coordinate organizations working on local gang reduction.
Advertising the role as non-permanent subject to a one-year evaluation and requiring an outcomes outline within 30 days of hiring will ensure accountability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adding new county staff positions during difficult economic times for taxpayers.
side_b_arguments: Taxpayers paying county bills are struggling financially.
The funding could be used more appropriately elsewhere rather than adding new positions.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 on a voice vote; the single dissenting commissioner (either Joe W. Bowser or Ellen W. Reckhow) was not explicitly named on the record.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 13, 2011 regular session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Board held a public hearing on the recommended FY 2011-2012 budget—featuring a $357.5 million general fund, an unchanged 74.59-cent property tax rate, and over $6.4 million for Durham Public Schools to backfill state cuts—and discussed declining state lottery revenues and pre-K funding without taking a budget vote. Commissioners unanimously approved minutes (5-0), adopted consent items A and E–H (5-0) while deferring Item D to the August work session, and later approved pulled Consent Items 7B (janitorial contract amendment) and 7C (advisory board meeting space and reporting) by 5-0 votes. The Board also approved Duke Energy's UDO text amendment (TC1100005) allowing utility facilities by right in the Science Research Park district (5-0 after clarifying attendance), extended the meeting past 11:00 p.m. (5-0), presented proclamations for Meatless Mondays and Elder Abuse Awareness Month, and appointed four members to the Durham County Research and Production Service District.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting, added a resolution for Elder Abuse Awareness Month under Item 6, and announced DCHC MPO open house sessions (June 14–16) on Durham and Orange County bus and rail investment plans. He also reminded the public that final FY 2011-2012 budget adoption was scheduled for June 27 and wished Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton a happy birthday.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 31 Special Budget Work Session, May 23 Regular Session, May 9 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the May 31, 2011 special budget work session, May 23, 2011 regular session, and May 9, 2011 regular session without modifications.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Meatless Mondays
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a Meatless Mondays proclamation citing obesity and nutrition statistics and presented it to Sustainability Manager Tobin Free and citizen organizers who led restaurant outreach and website development.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Vulnerable Adult and Elder Abuse Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation recognizing World Elder Abuse Awareness Day (June 15) and vulnerable seniors in Durham County. DSS representative Bob Wallace reported DSS received 600 reports of abuse, neglect, and exploitation in the past fiscal year, with nearly 100 substantiated; it was also noted that Ellen Holloman's recognition was removed from the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A, E, F, G, H; Item D Deferred; Items B and C Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson pulled Item 7B, a commissioner pulled Item 7C, and the Board agreed to move Item 7D to the August work session for a presentation. A request to pull Item 7A was withdrawn after staff noted it was time-sensitive, and the remaining consent items (A, E, F, G, H) were approved together.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Recommended FY 2011-2012 Durham County Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented the FY 2011-2012 recommended budget, featuring a $357.5 million general fund (nearly $500 million all funds), no property tax increase (74.59 cents per $100 valuation), a projected 98.55% collection rate (+$2.78 million), and over $6.4 million for Durham Public Schools to backfill state cuts. Following a middle-truncated public comment section and closing remarks from Victoria Peterson on per-pupil spending, commissioners discussed state lottery revenue falling from $4.5 million to $2 million, school debt coverage, and $200,000 for four pre-K classes at Hillandale; no vote was scheduled.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1100005 (Science Research Park Utilities)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a text amendment submitted by Duke Energy removing the prohibition on utility facilities (beyond accessory uses) in the Science Research Park district, restoring prior by-right standards; the Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Research and Production Service District)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board selected four appointees—Ronald Hunter, Ray Gunner, Robert [untranscribed surname] Jr., and Tom Coel—to the Durham County Research and Production Service District.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Extend Meeting to 11:15 p.m.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Approaching 11:00 p.m., the Board voted to extend the regular session until 11:15 p.m. to complete remaining consent items and board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 7B: Janitorial Service Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson questioned whether the contractor was a Durham company, asked about a $15,899 monthly increase and possible misprint in the contract summary, and urged the county to encourage subcontractors to hire individuals served by the Justice Resource Center.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 7C: Advisory Board Reports and Meeting Space
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner highlighted two advisory board reports, including the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee losing central public meeting space at the Durham Center for Senior Life, and asked the Clerk's office to press board and commission chairs to communicate scheduling and reporting needs.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes from the May 31 special budget work session, May 23 regular session, and May 9 regular session.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Becky M. Heron excused due to illness by a 3-0 vote prior to Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's arrival, Chair Michael D. Page and the four present commissioners also excused Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow from the Thursday budget work session (3-0) and approved prior minutes (4-0). The Board issued proclamations and resolutions recognizing June as Hunger Awareness Month, the Kappa Alpha Psi fraternity centennial and Durham chapter 90th anniversary, and departing Deputy County Manager Wendell Davis. Following a middle-truncated portion of the transcript and public hearings with no opposition speakers, the Board voted unanimously (4-0) across four financial and land-use items: a fee increase discussed with the Home Builders Association, the FY 2011-2012 Planning Department fee ordinance continuing a 4% technology surcharge, ratification of the 2010 Comprehensive Plan amendments (A1100003), and an interest rate swap modification adding $41 million (up to $227 million notional) with up to $250,000 in transaction costs.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal Motions, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioners excused Commissioner Becky M. Heron due to illness (3-0) prior to Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's arrival, excused Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow from Thursday's budget work session (3-0), and shared announcements including a May 24 mixed-use zoning workshop and Reckhow's report on the RDU Terminal 2 dedication.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 11, April 26 Special CIP, and May 2 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved minutes from the April 11 regular session, April 26 special CIP session, and May 2 work session.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: June as Hunger Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation designating June as Hunger Awareness Month, citing 15.6% Durham County poverty and 18.2% statewide food insecurity rates, and presented it to DSS Food and Nutrition Services and Family Economic Independence staff.

agenda_items.title: Resolution: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Centennial and Durham Alumni Chapter 90th Anniversary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read and presented a resolution honoring Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity's 100th anniversary and the Durham Alumni Chapter's 90th anniversary, accepted by Polemarch Heron Leak and fraternity members.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring Deputy County Manager Wendell Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page recognized departing Deputy County Manager Wendell Davis as he prepared to leave Durham County government for a position at North Carolina Central University. A middle portion of the meeting was omitted from the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Development/Building Fee Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted prior outreach to the Home Builders Association, which expressed understanding despite reluctance toward fee increases after years of holding rates down. The public hearing opened and closed with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2011-2012 Fee Ordinance (Planning Department and Related Fees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin requested continuation of the 4% technology surcharge on development applications for the Planning, Inspections, and Transportation departments to support real-time permitting access; commissioners asked about fee impacts on individual applicants, and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Ratification of 2010 Comprehensive Plan Amendments (A1100003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the annual evaluation and assessment report covering seven 2010 Comprehensive Plan amendments within city limits, including a downtown tier adjustment. Staff recommended ratification and no public speakers signed up.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Modifying Existing Interest Rate Swap
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick recommended modifying the county's existing interest rate swap by adding $41 million (bringing total notional amount not to exceed $227 million) to maintain a 45%/55% swap-to-debt ratio as new debt is issued, generating an estimated $500,000 in earnings, and confirmed Agenda Action Form authorization to spend up to $250,000 from the swap fund for transaction costs.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners agreed to hold off on the RTI/Research Triangle appointment pending clarity on Wake County's appointments, and the Clerk announced selections of Jeff Gold (Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee) and Tommy Hunt (Memorial Stadium Authority).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Michael D. Page excused, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided over the May 9, 2011 regular session with four commissioners present. The Board unanimously approved minutes (4-0) and the consent agenda excluding deleted Item 8G and pulled Item 8I (4-0), presented Foster Care Month and Older Americans Month proclamations, and received an operational update from Lincoln Community Health Center. Citizens spoke against Item 8I's proposed closure of Pickett Road in Orange County due to traffic shifting onto Randolph Road before a middle-truncated portion of the transcript. In subsequent action, commissioners unanimously voted 4-0 to approve a $225,000 economic development incentive contract with Syngenta Biotechnology Inc., refer zoning case Z1000006 and plan amendment A1000006 (TFD Facility) back to the Planning Commission, adopt broadcast tower text amendment TC1100001, and accept Duke University's $6.8 million upset-bid offer for the 300 North Duke Street Carmichael Building.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal Notice, Agenda Revision, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting, noted that Chair Michael D. Page was excused, and announced that Item 8G had been deleted from the revised agenda (later noted as pulled at the school system's request). Announcements covered a May 18 landlord training workshop and the May 21 Walk for the Animals.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the minutes presented without modification.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Foster Care Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow and Department of Social Services staff recognized May 2011 as Foster Care Month and highlighted community outreach and celebration activities for foster children.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Older Americans Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow proclaimed May 2011 as Older Americans Month. DSS staff including Bob Wallace noted that home-delivered meals and in-home services assist 350 seniors daily, helping them remain in their homes rather than entering nursing facilities.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Lincoln Community Health Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lincoln Community Health Center CEO Dr. Evelyn Schmidt and Pharmacy Director Lynn Robbins presented updates on facility renovations adding exam rooms, medication error tracking, Lincoln Pharmacy's World Culture Excellence Award, 100% patient satisfaction for respect and professionalism across main and seven satellite clinics, Project Access Durham County, and Health Department relocation to the new Health and Human Services building.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–F and H; Item G Deleted; Item I Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Consent Items A through F and H unanimously while pulling Item 8I for citizen speakers; Item 8G had been removed from the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Support Relative to Closing Portion of Pickett Road in Orange County
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow pulled Item 8I for three signed-up speakers. A resident spoke in opposition, arguing that closing Pickett Road in Orange County would divert roughly 600 vehicles per day onto Randolph Road in Durham County and create an excessive traffic burden; the remainder of this discussion fell in a middle-truncated portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Contract with Syngenta Biotechnology Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Syngenta Biotechnology Inc. (SBI) representatives described a proposed $71 million investment projected to generate over $3 million in net new property tax revenue over 10 years, operational in 2012, along with STEM student tours and a workforce roughly half drawn from Durham County. Commissioners praised the local hiring commitment and approved a $225,000 incentive contract.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Case Z1000006 and Plan Amendment A1000006 (TFD Facility)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin reported that the applicant submitted a revised development plan with significant modifications late that afternoon, requiring Planning Commission reconsideration by ordinance, and asked the Board to refer both Z1000006 and companion case A1000006 back to the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1100001 (Broadcast Towers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a BOCC-initiated text amendment requiring a minor special use permit from the Board of Adjustment for broadcast towers to ensure public participation and limiting site lighting to federal minimums. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 10-0, and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Sale of 300 North Duke Street Property (Carmichael Building)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented a $6.8 million letter of intent from Duke University (via Durham Realty Inc.) to purchase the Carmichael Building at 300 N. Duke Street prior to DSS's move to the Human Services building. Ruffin cited the need to use proceeds in the upcoming budget to hold property taxes down and capitalize on a qualified buyer; commissioners voted to accept the offer and initiate the statutory upset-bid process.

Following a public hearing with no speakers, the Board voted 5-0 to authorize submitting a roughly $195,000 NCDOT Section 5317 New Freedom transit grant application to support mobility management and disability transit trips. The Board also approved excusing Chair Michael D. Page from the May 9 regular session and made appointments to five advisory boards and the Durham County Hospital Corporation.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 11, 2011 regular session, the Board unanimously approved five sets of prior regular, special, and closed-session minutes (5-0), honored pioneering Durham intellectual property attorney B.B. Olive with a tribute resolution, and issued proclamations for Week of the Young Child and National Volunteer Week. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
meetings.executive_summary: At a 4:10 p.m. special session on March 28, 2011, the Board clarified that reviewing the County Manager's evaluation instrument and process had to occur in open session rather than closed session. UNC School of Government faculty member Dr. Vaughn Upshaw facilitated a workshop requested by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and County Manager Mike Ruffin to review ICMA management practices and core competencies as an update to the County's historical work-plan-based review. Commissioners debated rating scales (numerical 1–10 or even-numbered scales versus narrative expectation tiers), which core competencies to emphasize (such as financial management and board communication), and whether to seek outside stakeholder feedback, reaching informal consensus to develop a revised instrument for an April closed-session review. The Board then voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) to review confidential closed-session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Open-Session Determination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page called the special session to order at 4:10 p.m. and asked about a closed-session motion, but staff clarified that discussing the County Manager's evaluation instrument and process—rather than specific individual performance issues—belonged in open session.

agenda_items.title: Workshop on County Manager Performance Evaluation Instrument and Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: UNC School of Government faculty member Dr. Vaughn Upshaw walked commissioners through core process decisions and ICMA effective public management practices to modernize the County Manager's evaluation beyond annual work-plan goals. Commissioners exchanged views on 1–10 versus 4-/6-point or narrative rating scales, combining core competencies such as financial management and delegation, avoiding external non-citizen evaluations, and targeting an April closed-session review before May budget sessions, reaching consensus to proceed with drafting a revised form.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Confidential Minutes Review)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the workshop, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow moved, seconded by Commissioner Becky M. Heron, to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and N.C.G.S. 143-318.10(e) to review closed-session minutes for potential release.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Resuming from an earlier 3:00 p.m. special call meeting, the March 14, 2011 regular session opened with a musical performance by the Kidznotes El Sistema-inspired youth orchestra serving three Title I Durham elementary schools. Chair Michael D. Page delivered the annual State of the County Address, highlighting how Durham County saved public school teaching jobs through a modest tax increase and internal cuts, maintained its AAA bond rating from all three agencies, saved $25 million on the new courthouse, and braced for potential state budget shifts from a newly Republican-led General Assembly. With Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused (4-0), the four present commissioners approved four sets of February minutes (4-0), proclaimed National County Government Month, Child Abuse Prevention Month, and Professional Social Work Month, and approved Consent Items A through F (4-0).

agenda_items.title: State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page delivered the State of the County Address reviewing 2010–2011 fiscal conditions, noting the county preserved DPS teaching jobs via a modest property tax increase alongside position freezes, reduced library hours, and fee increases. He warned of potential state budget impacts (sunset of temporary sales tax, school bus and tort-claim shifts, and human services cuts), while celebrating Durham County's AAA bond rating, a $2 million Cree incentive, $25 million in courthouse construction savings, the Human Services Complex, and South Regional Library.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented proclamations for April 2011 National County Government Month (featuring a cell phone collection drive for soldiers and the Wounded Warriors benefits program), Child Abuse Prevention Month (highlighting Durham County's downward trend in abuse/neglect cases since 2000), and March 2011 Professional Social Work Month, where DSS social workers Janice Williams and Monte affirmed staff commitment despite budget cuts and pay freezes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Consent Items A through F by voice vote before adjourning at 8:05 p.m.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners approved the January 24, 2011 minutes (4-0), the consent agenda (5-0), and pulled consent Item I transferring leftover bond funds to Shepard Middle School (5-0) after supportive citizen comment. Durham Public Schools officials presented additional information on purchasing land for New High School A under the 2007 bond as a land-banking investment at 80-85% of market value, though commissioners questioned the tight timeline, budget constraints, and charter school impacts before the transcript digest truncates prior to any recorded vote on that item or the FY 2011-12 budget calendar. On the County Legislative Agenda, the board dropped Item 4 by consensus, approved Items 2 and 3 (5-0), excused Joe W. Bowser from Friday's legislative breakfast (5-0), and split 3-2 to retain Item 1 (pistol permit application fees). On that 3-2 split vote for Legislative Agenda Item 1, Becky M. Heron (mover) and Brenda A. Howerton voted Aye and Joe W. Bowser voted Nay, with the remaining Aye and Nay cast between Michael D. Page and Ellen W. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Pistol Permit Application Fee Proposal (Item 1) in Legislative Agenda
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over whether to approve Legislative Agenda Item 1 regarding Sheriff's Office pistol permit application fees prior to hearing directly from a Sheriff's Department representative at Friday's legislative breakfast.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance Item 1 into the legislative package now so the delegation can discuss it with a Sheriff's representative on Friday, while allowing commissioners to reconsider if unpersuaded.
side_a_arguments: In a resource-constrained environment, the Sheriff's Office performs substantial background research on pistol permit applications and receives no fee on 62% of applications if applicants do not qualify or fail to pick up permits within 30 days.
The permit application fee is small relative to the cost of buying a pistol.
Voting in the affirmative keeps the item on Friday's agenda with a Sheriff's representative present and preserves the option to change votes or move to reconsider.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold or oppose approving Item 1 until the Sheriff's Office provides a full explanation and questions are answered.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners should not endorse or place the item in the legislative package before hearing the Sheriff's Department's explanation on Friday.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-2 (Becky M. Heron and Brenda A. Howerton Aye; Joe W. Bowser Nay; the third Aye and second Nay split between Michael D. Page and Ellen W. Reckhow), advancing Item 1 to Friday's legislative breakfast with Sheriff's Office staff invited to explain.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners held a regular session featuring ceremonial recognitions for the 2010 NCHSAA 4A state champion Jordan High School boys' soccer team, elementary winners of the America Recycles Day poster contest, and Tuskegee Airmen, alongside an announcement of the upcoming Point-in-Time homeless count. The board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0), the consent agenda excluding Item L (5-0), and pulled consent Item 9L authorizing a local vehicle contract with University Ford (5-0) after a citizen urged greater oversight of Durham Public Schools out-of-county contracting. On Item 11, commissioners questioned whether changing Convention Center management to Global Spectrum could jeopardize the Marriott hotel flag, and unanimously voted (5-0) to enter negotiations on the condition that staff address those concerns and return the final contract for board approval. Following a closed session on personnel, attorney-client matters, and farmland conservation, the board unanimously approved (5-0) two farmland conservation easement purchase options for the Harris farm on Bacon Road and a 93-acre farm owned by David Krabby.

agenda_items.title: Announcements (Hope Valley Road Meeting and Criminal Justice Resource Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read the broadcast schedule for 'In Touch with Durham County' and commission rebroadcasts, and announced a January 27 public meeting at Jordan High School on City Public Works and Transportation's draft realignment designs for Hope Valley Road (NC 751). He also highlighted the Criminal Justice Resource Center open house held earlier that afternoon, commending staff and apologizing to Becky M. Heron for forgetting to announce her absence.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Dec. 6 Work Session, Dec. 13 Regular Session, Jan. 3 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered minutes from the December 6 work session, December 13 regular session, and January 3 work session. Brenda A. Howerton moved approval and Becky M. Heron seconded.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing Jordan High School 2010 State 4A Soccer Champions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a resolution saluting Coach Steve Turner and the Jordan High School boys' soccer team for defeating Charlotte Myers Park 2-0 on November 20, 2010 to complete a 25-0 season with 15 shutouts and capture the school's third NCHSAA 4A state title. Players and coaching staff were invited forward to receive the resolution.

agenda_items.title: 2010 America Recycles Day Poster Contest Recognition and Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff (Brian Haynesworth) and Keep Durham Beautiful, alongside city and corporate/civic sponsors, recognized elementary school winners of the first America Recycles Day poster contest, including overall winner Catherine Aidan Rooney of Creekside Elementary and calendar artist Jacqueline Fernandez of George Watts Elementary. Following a brief omitted interval, the board congratulated a newly appointed member at 00:22:10.

agenda_items.title: Tuskegee Airmen Recognition and Community Honors
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Veteran Services Director Lew Washington presented plans for Durham County's participation honoring Tuskegee Airmen, highlighting World War II B-25 pilot Dr. Fulbright. The board also recognized Jordan High School sophomore and honor student-athlete Camille and North Carolina Central University.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-K and M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board addressed consent agenda items A through M, noting that citizen Mr. Lane pulled Item L for separate comment. Brenda A. Howerton moved approval of Items A through K and Item M, and Ellen W. Reckhow seconded.

agenda_items.title: Point-in-Time Homeless Count Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page invited a community representative to announce the upcoming Wednesday Point-in-Time count after noting he had inadvertently left it off the printed agenda. The speaker highlighted new outreach efforts to identify unhoused families and children.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention Center Management Agreement (Global Spectrum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Drew Cummings, Deputy County Attorney Carol Hammett, and City General Services Director Joel Reitzer introduced a two-part management proposal with Global Spectrum covering ramp-up ahead of the Full Frame Film Festival in mid-April and a subsequent three-year contract with renewal options. Following a truncated middle portion, commissioners debated whether changing management would cost the adjacent hotel its Marriott franchise flag and sought assurance from legal and staff that approving negotiations would not bind the board before reviewing the final contract. Ellen W. Reckhow moved to proceed with negotiations on the condition that staff address commissioners' concerns and bring the final contract back for approval (earliest Feb. 7), seconded by Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Agenda Item L (University Ford Contract and School Spending Oversight)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Mr. Lane pulled Item 9L—authorizing the County Manager to contract with University Ford in Durham—to express support for using a local vendor while urging commissioners to tighten oversight of Durham Public Schools contracts with out-of-county and out-of-state architects and engineers. Commissioners discussed requesting a spending report on out-of-county/state dollars and conveying citizen concerns to the Board of Education before approving Item 9L.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Personnel, Farmland Conservation Easements, Attorney-Client)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read three statutory grounds for closed session: G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for personnel employment/qualifications, G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct staff on acquiring farmland conservation easements on properties owned by W.R. and Olivia Harris (Bacon Road) and David Krabby (4720 Bahama/Hamer Road), and G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Actions: Farmland Conservation Easement Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconvening from closed session at 03:25:16, the board took two formal actions authorizing the County Manager to sign options to purchase farmland conservation easements contingent on approved appraisals and 50% grant funding. The first covered the Harris farm at 1526 Bacon Road (75% of appraised value, $3,000-$4,500/acre, valid through Dec. 31, 2012), and the second covered a 93-acre farm owned by David Krabby at 4720 Hamer/Bahama Road (75% of appraised value, $4,000-$5,000/acre).

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (Dec. 6 Work Session, Dec. 13 Regular Session, Jan. 3 Work Session)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes from the December 6, 2010 work session, December 13, 2010 regular session, and January 3, 2011 work session without objection.

votes.discussion_detail: Authorized staff to proceed to the negotiation stage with Global Spectrum for Convention Center management, subject to addressing commissioners' questions—specifically the potential loss of the Marriott hotel flag—and returning the final contract to the board for approval (earliest February 7).

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) (personnel), (a)(5) (farmland conservation easement acquisitions on Bacon Road and 4720 Hamer/Bahama Road), and (a)(3) (attorney-client privilege).

votes.notes: Action taken in open session immediately following closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized the County Manager to sign an option through December 31, 2012 to purchase a farmland conservation easement on the Harris farm at 1526 Bacon Road (owned by W.R. and Olivia Harris), contingent on an approved appraisal and 50% grant funding, at a minimum of 75% of appraised value ($3,000-$4,500 per acre).

votes.item_title: Option to Purchase Farmland Conservation Easement (93-Acre Farm, 4720 Hamer/Bahama Road)
votes.notes: Action taken in open session immediately following closed session; expiration date transcribed as Dec. 31, 2020 (likely Dec. 31, 2012 as with the companion Harris farm option).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 13, 2010 organizational and regular session, the Board of County Commissioners debated whether to select its Chair and Vice Chair by motions requiring seconds or by unseconded nominations under Robert's Rules of Order before proceeding by nominations and show-of-hands votes. In the contested 3-2 Chair election, Michael D. Page defeated Joe W. Bowser (Michael D. Page, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Becky M. Heron for Page; Joe W. Bowser and Brenda A. Howerton opposing), and in the contested 3-2 Vice Chair election, Ellen W. Reckhow defeated Brenda A. Howerton (3 votes for Reckhow vs. 2 votes for Howerton, reflecting the same 3-2 Page/Reckhow/Heron vs. Bowser/Howerton division though individual hands were not read aloud on the Vice Chair vote). The Board also swore in Soil and Water Conservation District supervisors, introduced new Durham County Stadium manager Rico Chavez, recognized Health Department nutrition staff for a GSK award, and unanimously (5-0) adopted UDO Technical Changes VI (TC1000004) and an amended BOCC Code of Ethics expanding tax-payment language beyond Durham County taxes. Finally, the Board approved its consent agenda (5-0), confirmed Michael D. Page as Transportation Advisory Committee representative and Ellen W. Reckhow as alternate, and made multiple board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Election of Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and turned the gavel over to Deputy County Attorney Carol Hammett (transcribed Hammond) to preside over the Chair election. Commissioners debated whether to use motions requiring seconds (as initiated at the prior week's session) or traditional unseconded nominations under Robert's Rules of Order before agreeing to proceed with nominations. Michael D. Page won Chair 3-2 over Joe W. Bowser, and Ellen W. Reckhow won Vice Chair 3-2 over Brenda A. Howerton.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair: Page over Bowser (3-2); Vice Chair: Reckhow over Howerton (3-2)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Public Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no agenda adjustments, Chair Page recognized Robin Jacobs of the Eno River Association, who thanked the Board for its work amid difficult economic times. Chair Page also announced the regular broadcast and rebroadcast schedule for In Touch with Durham County and BOCC meetings.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 22, 2010 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Becky M. Heron seconded approval of the November 22, 2010 regular session minutes. The motion passed unanimously among the four voting members present.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In of Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisors
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Soil and Water Conservation staff and Board of Elections Director Mike Ash spoke following the November 2 election (noting over 81,000 Durham voters and optical-scan voting security). Newly elected Durham Soil and Water Conservation District supervisors were administered the oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Durham County Stadium Manager and Staff Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services introduced Rico Chavez, hired November 15, 2010 from North Carolina Central University into a newly approved FTE role as Durham County Stadium Manager. The Board later recognized departing service/honorees (middle portion truncated in transcript) and Public Health Director Gayle Harris introduced Health Department nutrition staff honored with a GSK award for school and SNAP nutrition outreach.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A and C through N)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 11B (Code of Ethics) was pulled for separate consideration, and after brief inquiry regarding Item C, commissioners kept all remaining items on consent. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser seconded approval of all consent items except 11B.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change, Technical Changes VI (TC1000004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Technical Changes VI (TC1000004), covering minor clarifications, typographical corrections, and state-law alignment, noting 13-0 Planning Commission and 7-0 City Council approval. With no speakers signed up, the public hearing opened and closed, and the Board approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 11B: Board of County Commissioners Code of Ethics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Allen Lang urged expanding the proposed Code of Ethics tax-compliance clause beyond Durham County taxes to cover all federal and other taxes. Following discussion noting the draft already exceeded the state model code, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser seconded adopting the Code of Ethics as amended.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and TAC Representative Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners voted on appointments to multiple advisory bodies, including the Animal Control Advisory Committee, Boxing and Wrestling Commission, Environmental Affairs Board, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, Open Space and Trails Commission, Public Health Board, RDU Airport Authority, and Transportation Advisory Board. The Board also approved Michael D. Page as regular representative and Ellen W. Reckhow as alternate to the Transportation Advisory Committee.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Voice vote on TAC; ballots tabulated for boards)

votes.item_title: Election of Board of County Commissioners Chair (Michael D. Page vs. Joe W. Bowser)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands election presided over by Deputy County Attorney Carol Hammett; Michael D. Page won 3 votes to 2 for Joe W. Bowser. At [00:06:08], Page thanked Ellen W. Reckhow for nominating him and Becky M. Heron for her vote, alongside Page himself (3), vs. Bowser and Howerton (2).
votes.discussion_detail: After debating whether Chair elections should proceed by seconded motions or unseconded nominations under Robert's Rules of Order, the Board voted by show of hands on nominations of Michael D. Page and Joe W. Bowser.

votes.item_title: Election of Board of County Commissioners Vice Chair (Ellen W. Reckhow vs. Brenda A. Howerton)
votes.notes: Show-of-hands tally announced as 3 votes for Ellen W. Reckhow and 2 votes for Brenda A. Howerton; individual hand-raisers were not read aloud on the Vice Chair vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the Vice Chair election between nominees Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton via show of hands.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 22, 2010 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Passed 4-0 by voice vote; the fourth Aye voter (either Joe W. Bowser or Brenda A. Howerton) was not identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the November 22, 2010 regular session.

votes.item_title: Item 12: UDO Text Change, Technical Changes VI (TC1000004)
votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote (ASR transcribed 'five to zero' as 'fire too').
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Unified Development Ordinance Technical Changes VI (TC1000004) following a public hearing with no speakers.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 11B: Board of County Commissioners Code of Ethics (as amended)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 5-0 by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Board of County Commissioners Code of Ethics as amended after public comment from Allen Lang regarding tax-payment scope.

votes.item_title: Transportation Advisory Committee Representative and Alternate Appointments
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Designated Chair Michael D. Page as regular representative and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow as alternate to the Transportation Advisory Committee (correcting an initially transposed statement of roles).

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Board Chair and Vice Chair Elections and Voting Procedure (Motions vs. Nominations)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed procedurally over whether Chair and Vice Chair elections must use seconded motions or unseconded nominations under Robert's Rules of Order, followed by 3-2 split elections for both leadership posts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect Michael D. Page as Chair and Ellen W. Reckhow as Vice Chair; Deputy County Attorney initially recommended continuing the prior week's seconded-motion format before agreeing to unseconded nominations.
side_a_arguments: Proceeding by motion keeps one motion on the table at a time, as Attorney Silor initiated the prior week.
If the Board prefers, nominations without seconds can be voted on sequentially by show of hands.
disagreements.side_b_position: Follow historical Robert's Rules nomination procedure without requiring seconds and support Joe W. Bowser for Chair and Brenda A. Howerton for Vice Chair.
side_b_arguments: Clerk minutes from December 2002 onward show previous county attorneys used open nominations under Robert's Rules rather than seconded motions.
An Attorney General inquiry should clarify the proper process if the Board deviates from standard nomination rules.
disagreements.resolution: Deputy County Attorney Hammett agreed to proceed by unseconded nominations; Michael D. Page was elected Chair 3-2 over Joe W. Bowser, and Ellen W. Reckhow was elected Vice Chair 3-2 over Brenda A. Howerton.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 22, 2010 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners adjusted the agenda to defer Item 7I to the December 6 work session, add Item 7P extending the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition Ten-Year Plan agreement through January 31, and discuss referring barking-dog, roaming-animal, and enforcement-discretion concerns raised by Commissioner Joe W. Bowser to the Animal Control Advisory Committee. Commissioners voted 4-0 to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the December 6 meeting, heard announcements on nonprofit funding deadlines and a Duke Energy-backed Durham Tech training grant, and unanimously (5-0) amended and approved revised Rules of Procedure governing citizen comment and public hearing rebuttals. After an exchange over maintaining privacy on personnel matters and rescinding a motion to reconsider Item 7P so Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton could question staff on required reporting, the Board voted to enter closed session for economic development and personnel matters under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6) with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Referral of Animal Control Ordinance Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board pulled Item 7I (mental health / Ellen Holliman item) to the December 6 work session and added Item 7P extending the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition contract to January 31. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser raised citizen complaints regarding barking dogs, loose dogs, and animal control officer discretion; after County Attorney clarification on county versus city noise ordinances, commissioners agreed to send the issues to the Animal Control Advisory Committee. The Board approved the agenda adjustments and voted 4-0 to excuse Chair Page from the December 6 meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda adjustments passed (Voice); Page excusal passed 4-0

agenda_items.title: Announcements: Nonprofit Funding and Durham Tech Workforce Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced the December 15, 2010 deadline for FY 2011-12 nonprofit agency pre-application questionnaires through Budget and Management Services. He also highlighted a Duke Energy-supported Facilities and Critical Support Systems Maintenance Training Program at Durham Technical Community College to train facility technicians for high-tech research and manufacturing firms.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Rules of Procedure Revisions (Public Comment and Hearings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief exchange over keeping personnel matters confidential and rejecting claims that the County Manager yelled at commissioners during a Friday meeting, the Board reviewed proposed revisions to its Rules of Procedure. Commissioners discussed the 30-minute citizen comment period, restrictions on yielding speaking time, and the Chair's discretion over public hearing rebuttals. The Board voted 5-0 to amend the rule to state the Board 'may or may not comment' and adopted the revised document.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Approval of Commercial General (CG) 'Bubble' Development Plan Without Building Footprints
disagreements.summary: The Board divided 3-2 on a Commercial General zoning/development plan submitted as a 'bubble plan' without building footprints, amid concerns over staff guidance and plan specificity.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the zoning/development plan because a CG bubble plan complies with the Unified Development Ordinance and protects site design through UDO performance standards.
side_a_arguments: Commercial General (CG) rezoning does not legally require a development plan at all, and a bubble plan is one of three compliant options under the UDO when the end tenant is not yet identified.
UDO performance standards still strictly regulate siting, parking, impervious surfaces, stormwater, landscaping, and tree coverage at site-plan review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approval without greater site-plan specificity or stronger staff guidance (two commissioners voted Nay; individual Nay names were not read aloud).
side_b_arguments: Commissioners raised concerns about whether bubble plans leave too little binding detail on project layout and noted a communication breakdown in staff guidance.
disagreements.resolution: Motion moved by Brenda A. Howerton and seconded by Michael D. Page passed 3-2.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: 751 Assemblage (C080003) Zoning Map Change and Urban-Fringe / Jordan Lake Impacts
disagreements.summary: The Board split 3-2 to approve the 751 Assemblage rezoning near Jordan Lake over staff infrastructure concerns, five advisory-board denial recommendations, and process controversies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 751 Assemblage (C080003) zoning map change with proffered committed elements 19–29 as compliant smart growth addressing jobs and community needs.
side_a_arguments: The project complies with North Carolina state rules and Durham's own Unified Development Ordinance and will not pollute Jordan Lake.
The development provides economic growth, jobs, and community benefits while balancing environmental protections with human needs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning as inappropriate in scale and location due to infrastructure sprawl, Jordan Lake water-quality risks, and process irregularities.
side_b_arguments: Planning staff warned the development draws infrastructure investment to the urban fringe away from planned transit nodes, and five advisory bodies (Planning Commission, DOST, EAB, New Hope Creek Advisory Commission, and Soil and Water Conservation District) recommended denial.

High-density development adjacent to Jordan Lake risks drinking-water pollution, and developer actions involving a 'spite strip' conveyed to NCDOT, revised appraisals, and protest-petition battles undermined trust.
disagreements.resolution: Motion moved by Joe W. Bowser and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton passed 3-2.

meetings.executive_summary: At the July 29, 2010 continued regular session (resuming Monday July 26 business), the Board of County Commissioners voted 4-0 to approve pulled Consent Items 7A, 7L, and 7M before splitting 2-3 to defeat Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's motion to place a quarter-cent (0.25¢) Article 46 county sales tax referendum dedicated to public education on the November 2, 2010 ballot. In that 2-3 failure, Joe W. Bowser (mover) and one other commissioner (between Brenda A. Howerton and Becky M. Heron) voted Aye to prepare for expiring federal stimulus teacher funding, while Ellen W. Reckhow, Michael D. Page, and one other commissioner (between Becky M. Heron and Brenda A. Howerton; exact individual names for the second Aye and third Nay were not read aloud) voted Nay over poor economic timing, lack of stakeholder and school board consultation, state education-funding equity concerns, and DPS budget efficiency questions. Commissioners also approved pulled Consent Item 7N (the jail food-service contract exceeding $500,000) after resident Victoria Peterson raised MWBE participation concerns and commissioners questioned inmate meal nutrition, discussed reconciling a Rules of Procedure timing discrepancy for public hearings, and tabulated ballot appointments to six boards including the Library Board of Trustees.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 7A, 7L, and 7M

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow opposed rushing a referendum without stakeholder or school-board input, citing state-versus-local funding equity, the sunsetting state 1-cent sales tax, Durham's top per-pupil local spending, and DPS's $13M classroom-teacher transfer; the motion failed 2-3.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session (continuation from July 26)
disagreements.issue: November 2010 Quarter-Cent Sales Tax Referendum (Article 46) for Public Education
disagreements.summary: The Board voted 2-3 against putting a 0.25-cent sales tax referendum dedicated to public education on the November 2010 ballot ahead of the August 1 statutory deadline.
disagreements.side_a_position: Place a 0.25-cent sales tax referendum dedicated to Durham Public Schools on the November 2010 ballot to offset expiring federal stimulus teacher funding.
side_a_arguments: Federal stimulus money funding roughly 340 to 350 teachers is expiring next year, and voters pushed back against property tax increases.
Waiting until a May or later election loses months of revenue (~$8 million annually) and the General Assembly is unlikely to replace lost federal funds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject a rushed November 2010 sales tax referendum and instead work with the General Assembly, school board, and public on long-term education funding and efficiency.
side_b_arguments: Shifting school funding to local taxes worsens statewide inequity between wealthier and poorer counties, and the state's temporary 1-cent sales tax does not sunset until June 30, 2011.

There has been no public hearing, stakeholder input, or consultation with the Board of Education ahead of an August 1 ballot deadline, and Durham already leads peer counties in per-pupil local funding while DPS transferred $13 million out of classroom teachers.
disagreements.resolution: Motion moved by Joe W. Bowser failed 2-3 (with Reckhow, Page, and one additional commissioner voting Nay, and Bowser plus one additional commissioner voting Aye).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 26, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved minutes with a LEED building energy-savings clarification (5-0), approved most of the consent agenda including the sale and leaseback of the Durham County Home Health Agency to Innovative Senior Care Home Health of Durham LLC (5-0, with Items A, M, and N pulled and Item J flagged for citizen comment), and held a public hearing on Recovery Zone Facility Revenue Bonds for The Hill project. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript covering a contentious zoning hearing involving a protest petition and a last-minute NCDOT land donation, the Board voted 5-0 to keep the public hearing open and continue the matter to August 9, 2010 so the County Attorney could investigate. When the session approached midnight, a motion by Joe W. Bowser seconded by Brenda A. Howerton to extend the meeting by 30 minutes to address remaining items—including a resolution for a November 2 one-quarter-cent sales tax referendum—failed because Board rules require a unanimous vote to extend past midnight and at least one unidentified commissioner voted Nay in the voice vote (Ayes included mover Joe W. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow asked about statewide bonding capacity, and Rusher explained that North Carolina's initial $697 million allocation had been pulled back into a statewide pool. (The middle portion of the transcript following this item is truncated.)

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated rezoning hearing involving a protest petition and an email forwarded that morning from NCDOT's Joey Hopkins regarding a developer land donation, the County Attorney requested additional time to review the validity and legal effect of the donation on the protest petition. Commissioners debated whether to close the public hearing and defer deliberation or keep the hearing open so citizens could respond to new findings. The Board voted 5-0 to continue the public hearing to August 9, 2010.

agenda_items.title: Midnight Extension Request and Recess to July 29 Special Meeting (Including Item 10 Sales Tax Referendum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Facing a midnight rule requiring unanimous consent to continue past 12:00 AM, commissioners disputed whether to extend by 30 minutes to vote on remaining contracts and Item 10 (a resolution placing a one-quarter-cent sales tax referendum on the November 2 ballot). A motion to extend by 30 minutes failed due to opposition on the voice vote, prompting a disagreement over agenda overloading on heavy public hearing nights. The Board then voted to recess and continue the meeting to Thursday, July 29, 2010 at 7:00 PM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Extending Session Past Midnight vs. Recessing Remaining Business (Sales Tax Referendum and Contracts)
disagreements.summary: At midnight following a lengthy zoning public hearing, commissioners disagreed over whether to extend the meeting by 30 minutes to vote on time-sensitive contracts and Item 10 (a resolution placing a one-quarter-cent sales tax referendum on the November 2 ballot) or stop due to fatigue and agenda overloading.
disagreements.side_a_position: Extend the meeting past midnight to finish time-sensitive contracts and approve the November 2 sales tax referendum resolution immediately.
side_a_arguments: The November 2 sales tax referendum resolution was up against a ballot deadline.
Staff waited through the evening and wanted to finish the remaining contracts in 15 to 30 minutes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Refuse unanimous consent to extend past midnight and criticize overloading public hearing agendas with extra items.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners and staff were exhausted after nearly five hours and could not properly cover the remaining items.
Too many items—including the commissioner-added sales tax item—were placed on the same agenda as a major public hearing.
disagreements.resolution: The 30-minute extension motion failed for lack of unanimity; the Board then voted to recess and continue the session to Thursday, July 29, 2010 at 7:00 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 28, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners adopted the Fiscal Year 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance by a split 4-1 voice vote after debate over funding $120,000 for new Durham County Memorial Stadium staff positions and public testimony from the Umbrella Coalition regarding 52 unfilled Durham Public Schools teaching positions (moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Becky M. Heron on the Aye side; Commissioner Joe W. Bowser spoke against the $120,000 stadium positions during debate, though the voice-vote announcement did not identify the lone Nay voter by name). Earlier in the meeting, the Board unanimously approved corrected minutes (5-0), approved the 16-item consent agenda A through P by voice vote (5-0), deferred Michael Perry's employee recognition to July 26 due to a family emergency, and heard Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request alongside Interim Executive Director Macdonald Vick and residents to reconsider a $15,000 funding request for youth mentoring organization Durham Companions. In closing business, the Board unanimously designated Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow as NACO voting delegate and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton as alternate, and announced appointments to seven county boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Reconvening from Closed Session and Announcements (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reconvened from closed session (having given direction to staff) and heard announcements including a June 29 public meeting at Trinity School on the possible closure of Pickett Road, Durham County receiving a Historic Preservation Society Neighborhood Conservation Award for the former East Durham Junior High School, a June 30 Environmental Management Commission public hearing at Neal Middle School on proposed Falls Lake rules, an engineering crash update following the June 7 work session, and the upcoming opening of the Lowe's Grove library.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Item 6) and Deferred Employee Recognition (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners corrected the June 14 regular session minutes to state that the Falls Lake rules public hearing was at Neal Middle School rather than the main library, and approved the May 25 budget work session and June 14 regular session minutes 5-0. Chair Page then announced that employee recognition for Michael Perry (Item 7) was rescheduled to July 26 because Perry left during closed session for a family emergency.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 8, Items A through P)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented Consent Agenda Items A through P, noting no commissioners or citizens had requested to pull any items. The Board approved Items A through P by voice vote without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Review of Funding Recommendations for Durham Companions (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request, the Board reviewed the recommended denial of $15,000 in county funding for Durham Companions, a 27-year-old youth mentoring nonprofit. Interim Executive Director Macdonald Vick apologized for the prior director's application and cited a 75% loss of state Governor's One-on-One funding despite a 95% success rate, while citizens questioned funding animal shelter operations over youth mentoring and staff noted the agency had reported declining first-quarter activity. (The remainder of this discussion is truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: Fiscal Year 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated including $120,000 for new Memorial Stadium positions during a tight budget year with no employee raises; Commissioner Joe W. Bowser opposed funding new stadium positions instead of providing employee bonuses, while Chair Page urged the County Manager to look for mid-year funds for small employee bonuses. After speakers from the Umbrella Coalition criticized 52 unfilled teaching positions and program cuts despite saving 185 teaching jobs, and citizen Alan Lang warned of rising foreclosures and expiring federal stimulus funds, the Board adopted the FY 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance 4-1.

agenda_items.title: NACO Conference Delegate Designation and Board & Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously designated Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow as voting delegate and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton as alternate for the National Association of Counties (NACO) conference. Ballot appointments were then announced for the City-County Appearance Commission (Olamaiyowa Alabi), Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board (Lao Rubert), EMS Council (Kerry D. Cain II and Dennis Tengine), Environmental Affairs Board (Winona Sacher), Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Timothy A. Barris, Rev. Johnny W. Foster Jr., Roger B. Parker, Karen K. Thompson), Women's Commission (Ruth G. Kennedy, Stephanie Watson), and Workforce Development Board (Alvis Akins).

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (May 25 Budget Work Session and June 14 Regular Session with Correction)
votes.notes: Voice vote ('Motion carries five to zero').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved May 25 and June 14 minutes after correcting the June 14 Falls Lake public hearing location from main library to Neal Middle School.

votes.item_title: Fiscal Year 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance
votes.notes: Passed 4-1 by voice vote ('Motion carries four to one'). Mover Ellen W. Reckhow and seconder Becky M. Heron voted Aye; Commissioner Joe W. Bowser spoke against the $120,000 Memorial Stadium positions during debate, though the voice-vote record did not explicitly call individual names.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the FY 2010–2011 County Budget Ordinance following debate over $120,000 for Memorial Stadium positions and public comments from the Umbrella Coalition and Alan Lang.

votes.item_title: Designate Ellen W. Reckhow as NACO Voting Delegate and Brenda A. Howerton as Alternate
votes.notes: Approved by unanimous consent ('All in favor by consent').
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow as voting delegate and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton as alternate for the National Association of Counties conference.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Funding $120,000 for New Memorial Stadium Staff Positions in FY 2010–2011 Budget
disagreements.summary: During final deliberations on the FY 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance, commissioners split over including $120,000 for new Durham County Memorial Stadium personnel during a recessionary year without county employee raises, resulting in a 4-1 adoption vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Retain the stadium staffing funds in the FY 2010–2011 budget while holding off hiring until needed to market and operate the renovated stadium.
side_a_arguments: The renovated stadium must be marketed and prepared for events beyond football.
The Stadium Authority does not expect the stadium manager to be hired until the facility is ready.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose putting $120,000 toward new stadium positions in FY 2010–2011 and prioritize modest employee bonuses instead.
side_b_arguments: In tough economic times when existing county employees receive no raises, $120,000 should be redirected to $150 appreciation checks for staff rather than creating new positions.
disagreements.resolution: The FY 2010–2011 Budget Ordinance passed 4-1 on a voice vote, with Chair Michael D. Page also asking the County Manager to explore mid-year funds for employee bonuses.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 14, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved all formal votes with no split or contested votes. The Board proclaimed June 2010 as Vulnerable Adult and Elder Abuse Awareness Month alongside DSS and Triangle J Area Agency on Aging staff, approved the eight-item Consent Agenda (Items A through H) by voice vote, and adopted the FY 2010–2011 Planning Department Fee Resolution 5-0 after a public hearing extending a 4% technology surcharge and adding architectural review and adjusted plan/certificate fees. Following a public hearing on the County Manager's $339.2 million recommended FY 2010–2011 budget (proposing a 4.9-cent property tax increase and a 3.16% current-expense increase for Durham Public Schools), a truncated middle section of the transcript gave way to extended scheduling deliberations on the 751 South rezoning public hearing. To satisfy the UDO's 30-day deferral window while ensuring all five commissioners could hear the case on July 26, the Board voted unanimously to convene a brief advertised meeting on Wednesday, July 14 at 10:00 AM solely to open the public hearing and immediately continue it to July 26.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Vulnerable Adult and Elder Abuse Awareness Month (June 2010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joined by Adult Protective Services representative John Margolis and Triangle J Area Agency on Aging representative Joan Palateo, Chair Michael D. Page read a proclamation recognizing World Elder Abuse Awareness Day (June 15) and proclaiming June 2010 as Vulnerable Adult and Elder Abuse Awareness Month in Durham County, citing more than 400 annual DSS referrals for adult abuse, neglect, or exploitation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 6, Items A through H)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented Consent Agenda Items A through H with no items pulled by citizens or commissioners. On a motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the Board approved the consent agenda unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2010–2011 Planning Department Fee Resolution (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the proposed FY 2010–2011 Planning Department Fee Resolution, extending the 4% technology surcharge for three years and establishing a $150 architectural review fee for new design districts alongside fee reductions/clarifications for combined development-and-site plans and minor certificates of appropriateness. Citizen Mr. Novak spoke in opposition to government fees in principle, arguing expenses should be funded through tax-deductible property taxes; after closing the public hearing, the Board approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Recommended FY 2010–2011 County Budget (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented the $339.2 million recommended FY 2010–2011 budget (<1% general fund increase), proposing a 4.9-cent property tax increase (raising the rate from 70.81 cents to 75.10 cents, adding $85.80 annually on a $200,000 home) and a 3.16% current-expense increase for Durham Public Schools ($80 per pupil) plus $4 million in lottery funds for school construction and debt service, while absorbing an 18% health insurance increase. (The public comment portion of the budget hearing is truncated in the transcript digest.)

agenda_items.title: Scheduling Special Meeting to Comply with UDO 30-Day Deferral Window for 751 South Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler and Planning Director Steve Medlin advised that under the UDO, a public hearing deferred from June 23 could not be rescheduled directly to July 26 because that exceeded the mandatory 30-day window by one day. To comply with the ordinance while allowing all five commissioners to attend the substantive hearing on July 26, commissioners agreed to have at least three members convene briefly on Wednesday, July 14 at 10:00 AM solely to open the advertised public hearing and continue it to July 26.

votes.item_title: FY 2010–2011 Planning Department Fee Resolution (Item 7)
votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('Motion carries five to zero').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved extension of the 4% technology surcharge for three years, new $150 architectural review fee, and fee adjustments for combined site/development plans and minor certificates of appropriateness.

votes.item_title: Schedule Special Meeting on July 14, 2010 at 10:00 AM for 751 Project Public Hearing Continuance
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion carries'). ASR at 02:20:27 transcribed the mover/seconder reference as 'commissioner, we're talking about commissioner Halton', confirming Brenda A. Howerton.
votes.discussion_detail: Set an advertised special meeting for Wednesday, July 14, 2010 at 10:00 AM for a majority of the Board to formally open the 751 South public hearing within the 30-day UDO window and immediately continue it to July 26, 2010.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 24, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners received County Manager Mike Ruffin's recommended FY 2010–2011 budget and navigated a contested scheduling vote over the 751 South / Southern Durham Development Corporation public hearing (T09-003). The Board voted 5-0 to add K&L Gates's deferral/scheduling request as Item 10 (eliminating a planned closed session), approved prior minutes 5-0, recognized the NC Envirothon winning team, approved an item regarding delaying controls until the June 7 work session (5-0), and excused Chair Page from the June 7 meeting by unanimous voice vote. On Item 10, after extended debate balancing the UDO's 30-day window and commissioner schedules, the Board passed a split 4-1 voice vote to reschedule the 751 South public hearing to Wednesday, June 23, 2010 at 7:00 PM (moved by Brenda A. Howerton and seconded by Joe W. Bowser on the Aye side; one unidentified commissioner voiced opposition on the Nay side, citing a conflict and preference for June 24 or an earlier date in June). The meeting concluded with announcements of appointments to seven boards and commissions, including Willie Bradshaw to the Memorial Stadium Authority and Donald Hughes to the Workforce Development Board.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Agenda Adjustments (Item 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Announcements highlighted the May 25 Fayetteville Street corridor open house at the Hayti Heritage Center, the opening of the Southwest Durham Branch Library, and youth attendance at the budget presentation. Chair Page noted a planned closed session was unnecessary and moved to add a late request from K&L Gates regarding the T09-003 public hearing date as Item 10; after a commissioner initially questioned voting before reading the packet memo, the Board voted 5-0 to add Item 10.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 3 Work Session and May 10 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the minutes of the May 3, 2010 work session and May 10, 2010 regular session. On a motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Becky M. Heron, the Board approved the minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of North Carolina Envirothon Winning Team (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Soil Conservation Education Specialist Jennifer Brooks and Soil & Water Conservation District Director Eddie Culberson introduced the North Carolina Envirothon winning team for recognition by the Board.

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Recommended FY 2010–2011 Budget Presentation (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented his recommended FY 2010–2011 budget—describing it as the most difficult in his 32-year career—and referenced recent courthouse rallies by parents, teachers, and students seeking to save 237 DPS teaching positions threatened by state cuts. He reviewed the Board's December seven-point budget framework, including capping the property tax rate at 73.81 cents (up to 3 cents for debt only) and maintaining at least a 15% unreserved fund balance, with a public hearing set for June 14. (Subsequent budget slides and the following agenda item are truncated until 02:10:21, when the Board voted 5-0 to hold off on certain controls and revisit them at the June 7 work session.)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Excused Absence (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously excused Chair Michael D. Page from the June 7, 2010 work session and conducted ballot voting for board and commission vacancies, noting Willie Bradshaw as the sole applicant for the Memorial Stadium Authority. Final ballot results announced later appointed Jeff Gold and Jessica Simo (Adult Care Home CAC), Tanya Battle and Howard Holcomb (City-County Appearance Commission), Marcia Owen (Criminal Justice Partnership Advisory Board), Mike Ruffin, Karen Flush, Steven Hancock, Theodore Pappas, and Michael D. Page ex officio (Durham County Hospital Corporation), Willie Bradshaw (Memorial Stadium Authority), Tiffany Washington (Nursing Home CAC), and Donald Hughes (Workforce Development Board).

agenda_items.title: K&L Gates Request to Schedule Public Hearing for Southern Durham Development Corporation (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a memo from K&L Gates representing Southern Durham Development Corporation requesting to schedule the T09-003 (751 South) public hearing for June 24, 2010 (the 30-day UDO maximum from May 24) following withdrawal of an adjacent appeal. After extensive debate over June 1 versus June 14, 22, 23, and 24 around budget sessions and commissioner travel, the Board passed a 4-1 voice vote setting the hearing for Wednesday, June 23, 2010 at 7:00 PM.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Scheduling the Rescheduled 751 South / Southern Durham Development Corp. Public Hearing (June 1 vs. June 23 vs. June 24)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed over when to hold the deferred 751 South public hearing requested by K&L Gates, weighing whether to keep the June 1 date after an appeal withdrawal, grant the full 30-day maximum to June 24, or pick June 23 amid budget sessions and personal travel conflicts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Schedule the hearing on Wednesday, June 23, 2010 at 7:00 PM to stay within the 30-day UDO window and accommodate most schedules.
side_a_arguments: June 23 falls inside the 30-day statutory deferral limit from May 24 and avoids conflicts with budget sessions and other meetings on June 21 and 22.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold the hearing either on June 24 (as requested by K&L Gates) or earlier in June (June 1 or the first/second week of June).
side_b_arguments: Because the citizen appeal was withdrawn and the application had been pending since January 2008, the Board could proceed on June 1.
One commissioner had already planned around June 24 and out-of-town travel and opposed June 23.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to set the hearing for June 23 at 7:00 PM passed with one opposing voice vote (4-1); the dissenting commissioner later inquired about an early-June replacement motion, which was not adopted.
