meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 26, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page (with Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow excused and Assistant County Attorney Carol Hammett substituting for County Attorney Lowell Siler), the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved all formal motions unanimously 4-0 while encountering sharp debate over board and commission appointment procedures. The Board approved consent items A, C, D, E, and F (4-0) and approved pulled Item 7B (4-0)—amending the Turner Business Appraisers property-discovery tax contract by $450,000—only after commissioners caught a drafting error listing a $1.2 million cap instead of the correct $793,250 not-to-exceed total. Commissioners also voted 4-0 to approve Durham Public Schools' $31.03 million construction and capital plan for Middle School B (Item 8) and 4-0 to approve DPS's $543,200 acquisition of 6.79 acres at Lowe's Grove School (Item 9), while demanding disaggregated DPS data at a future work session. Under Item 10, commissioners clashed over fairness, last-minute seat shifting (which Carol Hammett advised violated advertisement rules), and a 2-2 tie between Tanya Battle and Howard Holcomb for the City-County Appearance Commission, deferring the tied seat while appointing Antana Jones, Mark Soshowski, Jennifer Albright, and Clayton Swenson to other boards.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Announcements, Approval of Minutes, and Proclamations (Items 5–6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page noted Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow was excused and Assistant County Attorney Carol Hammett was sitting in for County Attorney Lowell Siler. The Board approved minutes (including the November 3, 2009 joint meeting with Durham County Hospital Corporation), recognized Durham's Partnership for Children on its 15th anniversary, and proclaimed April Financial Literacy Month with Consumer Credit Counseling Services Director Glendola Beasley.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 7, Remaining Items A, C, D, E, F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner pulled Item 7B and citizen Dr. Lavonia Allison pulled Items 7G and 7H. On a motion by Joe W. Bowser seconded by Becky M. Heron, the Board approved the remaining consent items 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7B: Turner Business Appraisers Contract Amendment (#10BCC000070)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned Tax Office staff on the $450,000 amendment (paid at 30% of collected discovered taxes), confirming the county was not paying 30% on the city's tax share and identifying a mathematical discrepancy where the contract text listed $1.2 million instead of $793,250 ($343,250 prior cumulative cap plus $450,000). On a motion by Joe W. Bowser seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the Board approved Item 7B 4-0 with the contract amended to state a $450,000 increase to a total not to exceed $793,250. (Citizen comments on pulled Item 7G are truncated after 00:30:00.)

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Construction and Capital Plan: Middle School B (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS representatives and Dr. Lavonia Allison discussed the $31,034,250 project budget for new Middle School B (roughly $30 million construction plus $581,981 in 2003 bond land funds and ~$2 million already invested in design/traffic resolution). Commissioners noted favorable construction bid pricing and the need to build ahead of enrollment growth, approving Item 8 by a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Real Property Acquisition at Lowe's Grove School (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a proposed purchase of 6.79 acres (with an uninhabitable structure) at $80,000 per acre ($543,200) under a co-development site plan shared with the new library and State Employees' Credit Union for a future elementary school. While supporting an elementary school in Lowe's Grove, commissioners criticized DPS for lacking disaggregated data and requested a future work session on the issue before approving Item 9 by a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners clashed over the City-County Planning Commission appointment process, including the non-reappointment of Linda Smith after one term, whether Darius Little remained on the ballot, and a proposal to shift a candidate between an at-large seat and an Oak Grove seat, which Assistant County Attorney Carol Hammett advised against without re-advertisement. Voting produced a tie between Tanya Battle and Howard Holcomb for the City-County Appearance Commission (held to the next meeting after neither side reconsidered) and appointed Antana Jones (Planning Commission), Mark Soshowski (CJPA Advisory Board), Jennifer Albright (Nursing Home CAC), and Clayton Swenson (Open Space and Trails Commission).

votes.notes: Mover Brenda A. Howerton identified; ASR audio gap omitted seconder and roll/voice tally announcement before moving to proclamations.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved prior regular session minutes and November 3, 2009 joint meeting minutes with Durham County Hospital Corporation.

votes.notes: Passed 4-0 by voice vote (Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow excused).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved $450,000 amendment for property tax discovery collections at 30% of collected tax, correcting the contract cap from $1.2 million to $793,250.

votes.notes: Passed 4-0 by voice vote ('Motion carries four to zero'; Vice Chair Reckhow excused).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved DPS acquisition of 6.79 acres at Lowe's Grove at $80,000 per acre ($543,200) for a future elementary school site.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: City-County Planning Commission Seat-Shifting & City-County Appearance Commission Tie
disagreements.summary: During Item 10 board appointments, commissioners disputed the fairness of Planning Commission nominations (including Linda Smith's non-reappointment, Darius Little remaining on the ballot, and shifting a member from an at-large seat to an Oak Grove seat), and deadlocked 2-2 on the City-County Appearance Commission appointment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain existing ballot slates and proceed with appointments or shift seats as proposed, declining to change votes on the tied Appearance Commission seat.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners should proceed to vote on the candidates before them rather than reopening completed processes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Object to 'stacking the deck' and shifting applicants across seats without re-advertising, and decline to reconsider Appearance Commission votes.
side_b_arguments: Assistant County Attorney Carol Hammett advised that moving an appointee from an at-large seat to the Oak Grove seat without resignation and re-advertisement violates the Board's appointment resolution.
An opposing commissioner argued the process lacked integrity and fairness toward citizens who applied through regular channels.
disagreements.resolution: Antana Jones was appointed to the Planning Commission; the City-County Appearance Commission tie between Tanya Battle and Howard Holcomb was carried over to the next meeting after commissioners refused to reconsider their votes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 12, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) on all formal motions—including a 5-0 vote to reconsider its April 5 Oak Grove appointment of Darius Little to the City-County Planning Commission—while debating the format of a proposed county strategic planning session. Earlier in the meeting, the Board excused Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow from three upcoming April–May events (5-0), approved four sets of March minutes (5-0), proclaimed Child Abuse Prevention Month, congratulated the Duke University men's basketball team on its fourth NCAA national title, celebrated an NCACC award for HR's Dependent Eligibility Audit, and approved unpulled consent items (5-0) while reviewing pulled Items E and F regarding NCDOT-driven cost increases for the Jordan High School Access Drive. Following emotional public comments criticizing flaws in the city/county appointment process and allegations involving Darius Little, Chair Michael D. Page moved and Becky M. Heron seconded the 5-0 motion to reconsider Little's April 5 appointment so it could be deferred for review. Before adjourning into closed session on tax litigation (*Kendrick Estates* and *IBM Credit Corp.*), commissioners disagreed over whether a May strategic planning session proposed by Brenda A. Howerton should include outside experts on the first day.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Excused Absences, Announcements, and Minutes (Items 3–4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton added a strategic planning session scheduling discussion before closed session, and the Board voted 5-0 to excuse Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow from the April 26 regular session, May 3 work session, and legislative breakfast. After reminding residents of the April 15 deadline for the 2010 Census, the Board approved the March 16, March 23, and March 30 special session minutes and March 22 regular session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions: Child Abuse Prevention Month, Duke Basketball, and NCACC HR Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joined by DSS Director Gerri Robinson and Gail Engel, Chair Page proclaimed Child Abuse Prevention Month (noting 432 children served and 61 taken into custody). He also read a resolution congratulating the Duke University men's basketball team on winning its fourth NCAA championship (61–59 over Butler on April 5), and the Board recognized Human Resources and Diane Pearson for winning an NCACC Outstanding County Programs Award for the Dependent Eligibility Audit.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–J) and Pulled Items E & F: School Bond Transfers / Jordan High Access Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Items E and F pulled by citizens and for questions from Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the Board voted 5-0 to approve Consent Items A, B, C, D, G, H, I, and J. On Items E and F, DPS staff explained that while Creekside Elementary and most 2007 school bond projects were bidding 15–20% under budget, additional NCDOT requirements on the Jordan High School Access Drive exceeded the original bond allocation, and clarified that bond funds cannot be transferred outside the designated bond program. (Subsequent discussion is truncated until 02:06:58.)

agenda_items.title: Reconsideration of April 5 City-County Planning Commission Appointment (Darius Little, Oak Grove Seat)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public testimony from speakers including Darius Little's mother and Victoria Peterson criticizing the integrity of the city-county appointment process, and a commissioner's statement emphasizing race was not a factor, the County Attorney advised that under Board rules any motion to reconsider an April 5 vote had to be made at this meeting by a member on the prevailing side. Chair Michael D. Page moved, and Becky M. Heron seconded, a restated motion to reconsider the April 5 Oak Grove Planning Commission appointment of Darius Little, which passed 5-0 and lifted the appointment for deferral pending resolution of the allegations.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Planning Session Dates and Format Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton proposed meeting May 10 or 11 to begin a county strategic plan covering areas such as economic development, human services, and community revitalization. Commissioners disagreed over whether to bring in outside resource experts on day one or simply circulate comparable local governments' strategic plans to read ahead of an internal board discussion.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding Kendrick Estates Development Corporation v. Durham County and Appeal of IBM Credit Corporation (COA 08-1514). Reconvening at 03:21:46, Chair Page reported the Board provided direction to staff and adjourned at 10:25 PM.

disagreements.issue: Whether to Include Outside Experts at Initial Strategic Planning Session
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed over how to structure a proposed May strategic planning session requested by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton—specifically whether to invite outside resource people on the first day or review written examples internally first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring in resource people to outline strategic planning possibilities and categories (economic development, human services, community revitalization) for the Board to question.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 22, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously on all motions (5-0) while deferring contested board appointments amid internal disagreement over the Workforce Development Board nomination process. Chair Page opened by urging commissioners and staff to respect board-liaison protocol, reading a formal statement rebutting Durham PTA President Trilby McClammy's letter demanding that county reserves cover Durham Public Schools' deficit, and announcing the March 31 courthouse groundbreaking. The Board approved five sets of prior minutes (5-0), issued proclamations for Professional Social Work Month, Week of the Young Child, and County Government Month, and—after a truncated middle section—discussed state legislative revenue options (such as a local payroll tax and airport revenue data) ahead of the May short session. Under Item 16, the Board voted 5-0 to defer the three Planning Commission seats after Chair Page cited late-breaking information requiring research, and voted unanimously to defer the Workforce Development Board appointment after Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and other members objected to last-minute packet materials and staff bypassing commissioners to offer Donald Hughes a committee seat instead of the main board. Appointments were completed for the Farmland Protection Advisory Board (William Wilson) and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (Angela O'Teary) before the Board entered closed session (5-0) on personnel matters.

agenda_items.title: Liaison Protocol Remarks, Announcements, and Statement on PTA Budget Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page asked commissioners, staff, and citizens to consult a board's designated commissioner liaison before intervening with appointed boards, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton offered prayers for Mike Gosh of the Board of Elections after an accident and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser noted an award for Operation Breakthrough. Chair Page announced March 23 and March 30 community budget conversations, the March 31 courthouse groundbreaking at 247 South Mangum Street, and read a statement refuting Durham PTA President Trilby McClammy's letter requesting county reserve funds for DPS, citing severe revenue shortfalls and 3% county department reduction targets.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Five Sets of Prior Minutes (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Becky M. Heron, the Board voted 5-0 to approve minutes from the February 8 work session, February 8 Person County joint session, February 8 regular session, February 22 regular session, and March 1 work session. A commissioner asked the Clerk to avoid bundling five sets of minutes into one meeting so members have adequate time to read them.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page presented the Professional Social Work Month proclamation to DSS Program Manager Jovetta Whitfield and the Week of the Young Child proclamation to Triangle Area Child Care Resource & Referral leadership. Staff noted that due to budget constraints, County Government Month observances would be scaled back to educational outreach and modest employee recognition. (The middle portion of the transcript is truncated after 00:29:18.)

agenda_items.title: Short-Session Legislative Agenda and Local Revenue Options Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ahead of the General Assembly's May 12 short session, commissioners discussed potential revenue options—including whether special legislation would be needed for a payroll tax and obtaining state-held expenditure data from RDU Airport—and noted prior conversations with Senator McKissick, deciding to bring the matter back to a work session after public speaker Deborah commented.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Deferrals (Item 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page requested delaying three Planning Commission appointments to research information received that afternoon, and the Board voted 5-0 to defer them to April 5. Commissioners then debated the Workforce Development Board seat—with Brenda A. Howerton and others criticizing last-minute paperwork, feeling bypassed, and objecting to staff offering candidate Donald Hughes a subordinate committee role rather than the board seat—and voted unanimously to defer that appointment to April 5 as well, while electing William Wilson (Farmland Protection) and Angela O'Teary (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 22, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously 5-0 on all five land-use and capital construction motions, with no split or contested votes. Chair Page opened with the annual State of the County Address—highlighting Durham County's AAA bond ratings, 2009 budget resilience without tax hikes or layoffs, a $1.2 million EMC Corp. incentive contract, ~$21 million in federal stimulus aid, and growing tax-payment plans—followed by announcements for the March 12–13 Mission of Mercy free adult dental clinic and a consent agenda revision for the 2010 Equalization and Review board. Following a truncated middle section, the Board closed a public hearing on a new school on Snow Hill Road (addressing citizen questions about busing and traffic in precincts 25, 26, 28, and 29) and approved 5-0 the Major Special Use Permit (consistent with D08-219), Transportation Special Use Permit T09-003 (requiring Snow Hill/Roxboro Road turn-lane extensions and access lanes), and Item 11 Major Site Plan. Commissioners then approved 5-0 the construction contract for the new Durham County Courthouse and parking deck—celebrating a low bid nearly 25% below the $99.2 million budget—along with supplemental Items L through Q (5-0), and announced appointments to three advisory boards.

agenda_items.title: State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page delivered the State of the County Address (noting County Manager Mike Ruffin's absence for the birth of a granddaughter), praising his fellow commissioners for re-electing him Chair and maintaining AAA ratings from S&P, Moody's, and Fitch while balancing the 2009 budget without tax increases or employee layoffs. He highlighted a $1.2 million EMC Corporation incentive, ~$21 million in federal stimulus aid (including nearly $2 million for Lincoln Community Health Center), a jump in taxpayer payment plans from 307 to 1,531, surplus computer distributions to students, and upcoming community budget conversations.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Consent Agenda Revision (Item 7I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page announced the NC Dental Society's Mission of Mercy free adult dental clinic on March 12–13 at the National Guard Armory for patients under 200% of the federal poverty index, and noted a revised consent agenda updating Item 7I (2010 Equalization and Review board appointments). (The middle portion of the transcript is truncated after 00:38:05.)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approvals: School Major Special Use Permit (D08-219), Transportation Special Use Permit (T09-003), and Major Site Plan (Item 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comments questioning school busing, feeder districts, and traffic across precincts 25, 26, 28, and 29, Chair Page closed the public hearing and Planning staff's Michael Stock recommended approval of the school Major Special Use Permit and Transportation Special Use Permit T09-003, conditioned on extending westbound and southbound left-turn lanes at Roxboro Road and Snow Hill/Mason Road and constructing two site accesses prior to Certificate of Occupancy. The Board approved the Major Special Use Permit, Transportation Special Use Permit T09-003, and Item 11 Major Site Plan in three separate 5-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: New Durham County Courthouse and Parking Structure Construction Contract (Item 12) and Supplemental Items L–Q
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the construction contract award for the new Durham County Courthouse and parking deck, emphasizing that the low bid came in nearly 25% below the $99.2 million construction budget. The Board voted 5-0 to approve the construction contract and then voted 5-0 to approve supporting supplemental Items L through Q.

agenda_items.title: Schedule Confirmations and Board & Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners confirmed community budget conversation dates for March 16, March 23, and March 30 and noted no meeting on March 8. Ballot appointments were announced for Patricia Crispell (Adult Care Home CAC), Elizabeth Frenzel and Donna McNeil (Nursing Home CAC), and Will Wilson (Open Space and Trails Commission), before adjourning at 10:31 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 8, 2010 Regular Session presided over by Chair Michael D. Page, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved minutes (5-0), the consent agenda (5-0), and a closed session motion (5-0), before passing a contested 4-1 voice vote on Item 9 approving an amended interlocal agreement with Durham Public Schools to capture sales tax reimbursements on lottery-funded and capital projects. Earlier in the evening, the Board introduced its new General Services Director, heard Public Health Director Gayle Harris and Dr. Alec Parker preview the March 12–13 Mission of Mercy free adult dental clinic, and opened advance public comment on the FY 2010–2011 budget (where Donald Hughes advocated participatory budget workshops and youth internships). Following a truncated middle section, Item 9 sparked sharp debate: supporters including Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow argued the agreement ensured accountability and saved DPS $180,000 to $300,000, while an opposing commissioner criticized it as circumventing state legislative restrictions and Brenda A. Howerton protested that her questions about urgency had not been answered in writing. When the Chair called the voice vote and announced it passed 4-1 (with Ellen W. Reckhow speaking in favor on the Aye side and one unidentified commissioner casting the recorded Nay vote from debate), Brenda A. Howerton declared her vote was No—but declined to move for reconsideration after the County Attorney noted she would need to move to reconsider to alter the already-announced 4-1 count.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Staff Introduction (Item 3A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A revised agenda added Item 9 (Interlocal Agreement with Durham Public Schools) and Item 10 (Closed Session deferred from the afternoon work session). Chair Page announced the opening of the Durham 2010 Local Census Office at 201 West Main Street, and the County Manager introduced the new General Services Director who started January 25, 2010 with architecture degrees from Kansas State and the University of New Mexico.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: NC Dental Society Mission of Mercy Free Adult Dental Clinic (Item 3B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gayle Harris introduced Dr. Alec Parker, Executive Director of the North Carolina Dental Society, who presented on the March 12–13 free adult dental clinic in Durham. Dr. Parker highlighted that the statewide program had treated over 25,000 patients and provided more than $7 million in free care since 2003.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Item 4) and Consent Agenda (Item 5, Items A–G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the January 4, 2010 work session and January 25, 2010 regular session minutes 5-0, and then approved Consent Agenda Items A through G by a 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Advance Public Comment for FY 2010–2011 Budget (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Pam Meyer reported bleak preliminary FY 2010–2011 forecasts showing flat sales tax and minimal property tax growth, outlining the budget calendar ahead of the May 24 recommended budget. Citizen Donald Hughes urged the County to replicate the City of Durham's Lyon Park participatory budget workshop model and expand paid internships for DPS and local college students. (The middle portion of the transcript is truncated after 00:25:35.)

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement with Durham Public Schools on Capital/Lottery Sales Tax Savings (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public criticism demanding documented written policies and procedures, commissioners divided over an amended interlocal agreement enabling DPS to recoup $180,000 to $300,000 in sales taxes on lottery-funded and non-bond capital projects. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow backed the savings and accountability, whereas an opposing commissioner argued it circumvented state law and Brenda A. Howerton stated she had not received written answers regarding urgency; the Chair announced a 4-1 passage, after which Howerton declined to move to reconsider when advised on recording her No vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Personnel Qualification and Performance (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding an individual public officer or employee. Reconvening at 03:06:35, the Board noted it gave direction to staff and adjourned at 10:06 PM.

votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('motion carries five, two, zero').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes from the January 4, 2010 work session and January 25, 2010 regular session.

votes.notes: Passed 4-1 by voice vote ('motion carries four to one'). Ellen W. Reckhow argued in favor; an opposing commissioner spoke against circumventing state law at 02:08:13. Immediately after the 4-1 announcement, Brenda A. Howerton stated she had not voted and wanted to vote No without her questions answered, but declined to move to reconsider when informed by the County Attorney that a motion to reconsider was required to change the recorded 4-1 vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the amended interlocal agreement with DPS allowing sales tax savings on lottery-funded and non-bond capital projects.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding qualifications, competence, and performance of an individual public officer or employee.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Interlocal Agreement with Durham Public Schools for Capital/Lottery Sales Tax Reimbursements (Item 9)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners clashed over an amended interlocal agreement allowing Durham Public Schools to capture sales tax reimbursements through the county on lottery-funded and non-bond capital projects, passing 4-1 amid objections over circumventing state law and unanswered procedural questions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the amended interlocal agreement to save DPS $180,000–$300,000 and maintain county accountability.
side_a_arguments: In a resource-constrained budget environment, the county should help DPS save $180,000 to $300,000 on $2.3 million+ in lottery and capital projects.
The 'shall' clause gives the Board of County Commissioners leverage and accountability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the agreement as an improper circumvention of state legislative policy and object to voting before written answers on urgency were provided.
side_b_arguments: The General Assembly enacted legislation barring school systems from receiving these sales tax reimbursements while supplying roughly $500 million (the majority of DPS's budget), and local legislators reported they had not been consulted by DPS.
Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated she was still awaiting written answers explaining the urgency of adopting the agreement immediately rather than deferring two weeks.
disagreements.resolution: The motion passed 4-1 on a voice vote; Brenda A. Howerton declined to move to reconsider after the vote was announced, leaving the 4-1 approval standing.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Michael D. Page excused by a unanimous 4-0 vote, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presided over the January 25, 2010 regular session. The Board clarified draft minutes regarding farmland pollution mitigation efforts before approving them 4-0, and presented a resolution expressing solidarity and encouraging verified relief support for victims of the January 2010 Haiti earthquakes. Following public hearings with no opposition speakers, commissioners unanimously approved (4-0) special purpose project revenue bonds in principle for both the Durham-Chapel Hill Jewish Federation and RTI International's new LEED Gold office building and parking deck. The meeting concluded with announcements of upcoming February board retreats and work sessions along with appointments to four county advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Excusal of Chair Michael D. Page
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the January 25, 2010 regular session and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Commissioner Becky M. Heron moved, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow confirmed there were no agenda adjustments. She announced the Durham County Television Channel 8 broadcast schedule for 'In Touch with Durham County' and BOCC meeting rebroadcasts, and noted ethics materials placed at commissioners' seats.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Clarification on Farmland Pollution Comments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a sentence in the draft minutes referencing Commissioner Heron's disagreement with Commissioner Bowser's earlier remarks on farmland pollution in Durham lakes and streams. To ensure the permanent record was clear, they agreed to revise the language to state that Commissioner Heron noted steps are being taken to reduce pollution from farmland in Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on the January 2010 Haiti Earthquake
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heron read a Board resolution mourning the casualties of the January 12 and January 20, 2010 earthquakes in Haiti and urging Durham County residents to support verified relief organizations. Isabel Figaro of the Duke chapter of the North Carolina Haitian Student Alliance and former Haitian Ambassador Dr. Jean Casimir accepted the resolution and thanked the community and local universities for medical and humanitarian mobilization.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Tax Software and Audit Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow introduced the consent agenda, reading Item 6a (a $62,500 contract renewal with Cox and Company for tax office software) and Item 6b (amending a contract with Tax Management Associates, Inc. by $90,000). Remaining consent items and the consent vote occurred inside a middle portion of the video transcript omitted from the digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Special Purpose Project Revenue Bonds for Durham-Chapel Hill Jewish Federation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bond counsel explained that low construction costs and a February 2009 federal stimulus provision enabling banks like BB&T to purchase 501(c)(3) tax-exempt bonds directly were driving renewed interest in special purpose project revenue bonds, and confirmed County Attorney staff time is reimbursable if billed. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, Jewish Federation Executive Director Shelley Katz briefed the Board on the project's roughly one-year completion timeline.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Special Purpose Project Revenue Bonds for RTI International (RTI Inc.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In response to a question from Commissioner Howerton about RTI's '09 office building project, RTI played an informational video detailing its 1958 founding, global research footprint, and ties to UNC-Chapel Hill, NC State, and Duke. RTI representatives explained the LEED Gold-capable building and parking deck will house over 560 staff while preserving green space, and noted RTI pays over $64 million in wages to Durham County residents; no public speakers signed up for the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Schedule Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed receiving appointee demographic data from the clerk and confirmed plans for a February 1 work session (up to 4:00 p.m.) and a February 18 meeting (9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). Appointments were announced for Stephanie Felder and Marcus A. Weeks (Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board), Wannona Satcher (Environmental Affairs Board), Heather Wagner (Historic Preservation Commission), and Jason R. Nelson (Open Space and Trails Commission).

votes.notes: Chair Michael D. Page was excused and absent for the meeting; ASR transcribed seconder as 'Howardton'.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow requested a motion to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the January 25, 2010 regular session.

votes.notes: ASR at [00:10:06] transcribed 'motion made by Commissioner Heron, seconded by Commissioner Heron'; actual seconder name is ambiguous in ASR.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes as amended to clarify that Commissioner Heron stated steps are being taken to reduce pollution from farmland in Durham County, along with other minor changes noted.

votes.notes: Unanimous among the 4 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved in principle the issuance of special purpose project revenue bonds for the Durham-Chapel Hill Jewish Federation (to be purchased directly by BB&T) following a public hearing with no speakers.

votes.notes: Unanimous among the 4 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved in principle the issuance of special purpose project revenue bonds for RTI Inc.'s LEED Gold-capable office building and parking deck following a presentation and public hearing with no speakers.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presided over the January 11, 2010 regular session, which opened with a recognition of Friends of the Durham Library volunteer Jane Goodrich, a resolution supporting 2010 Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. holiday events, and a proclamation for Durham TRY's 'Talk It Up. Lock It Up!' youth alcohol prevention campaign. On the consent agenda, citizens pulled Items 7A and 7B and commissioners pulled Items 7C and 7E, leaving Item 7D setting the Sheriff's salary for the election filing period, which passed unanimously 5-0. Following a public hearing on an economic development performance contract for a woman-owned business, the Board voted 5-0 to provide up to $100,000 over three years, and also held the first HUD public hearing on the Five-Year Consolidated Plan (FY 2010-2015) and HOME consortium housing needs. The Board concluded with a 5-0 vote to enter closed session regarding public officer and employee performance before adjourning at 10:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page called the meeting to order and confirmed there were no agenda adjustments. Announcements covered the Channel 8 broadcast schedule for 'In Touch with Durham County' and BOCC rebroadcasts, as well as the FY 2010-2011 nonprofit agency funding pre-qualification period that opened December 15, 2009.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Friends of the Durham Library Volunteer of the Year
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Library Director Skip Auld and Friends of the Durham Library Board President joined the Board in honoring volunteer Jane Goodrich. Goodrich received the statewide Friends of North Carolina Public Libraries Volunteer of the Year award in Salisbury in October 2009.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting 2010 Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Events
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Coretta Scott King and supporting the Durham Community MLK Jr. Steering Committee's January 15-18, 2010 events under the theme 'From the Dream to Reality.' He also announced the January 14 City-County employees' MLK celebration at First Presbyterian Church featuring Pastor J.D. Greer.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for 'Talk It Up. Lock It Up!' Campaign (Durham TRY)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a proclamation declaring January 22 as the start of Durham Together for Resilient Youth's (TRY) 'Talk It Up. Lock It Up!' campaign, citing survey data on youth obtaining alcohol from home and friends' homes. Wanda Boone addressed the Board on securing alcohol in households to prevent underage drinking.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Approval of Item 7D — Sheriff's Salary; Items 7A, 7B, 7C, 7E Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens (including Victoria Peterson) pulled Consent Items 7A and 7B, and commissioners pulled Item 7C (city-county affordable housing / 10-year homelessness plan contract) and Item 7E (Parker Poe legal conflict waiver up to $10,000 for the IBM Credit Corp. property tax appeal). The Board proceeded to approve remaining Item 7D, setting the salary of the Sheriff for the election filing period; discussion of pulled items occurred within the truncated middle portion of the transcript.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Grant ($100,000 Over Three Years)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the visible portion of this public hearing, speakers including Mr. Ruffin and Ms. Peterson questioned company operations, salary tiers, and training pathways. Economic development staff (Ms. Titus) and company representatives noted the firm is a woman-owned business entering a standard annual performance contract and explained student training and employment readiness before the Board voted to provide up to $100,000 over three years.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Five-Year Consolidated Plan (FY 2010-2015) and Annual Action Plan Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development Director Mike Barrels and Federal Grant Coordinator Wilmur Conyers held the first of two HUD-required public hearings for the FY 2010-2015 Consolidated Plan and anticipated $1.2 million HOME consortium allocation. Citizen speaker Ms. Peterson urged pairing boarded-up inner-city housing repairs with youth carpentry training, while Barrels and commissioners discussed neighborhood redevelopment strategies, 2% second-mortgage assistance, youth work-ethic training, and financial literacy.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Public Officer and Employee Performance) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider the performance of a public officer and employee. Upon returning to open session at 02:55:32, the Board reported it had provided directions to staff and adjourned at 10:00 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham County Board of Commissioners approved a quasi-judicial Transportation Special Use Permit (T09-00002) and major site plan for Elementary School E off Hebron Road (5-0), honored retiring General Services Director Mike Turner and DCVB CEO Reyn Bowman, and swore in new Clerk to the Board V. Michelle Parker-Evans. During discussion of an internal audit of the Families First faith-based DSS program, Commissioner Joe W. Bowser disputed audit figures and media claims regarding participating congregations. On pulled consent Item M, the Board voted 3-2 to approve the Criminal Justice Resource Center (former jail) renovation contract with a reduced 10% ($210,000) contingency cap (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, Brenda A. Howerton; Nays: Joe W. Bowser, who opposed capital spending amid budget pressures, and Michael D. Page, who opposed restricting staff's proposed 15% contingency). On pulled consent Item R, after lengthy public comment regarding foreign government IDs (Matrícula Consular) and Sheriff's Office policy, the Board voted 4-1 to adopt a revised Bill of Rights Day and Human Rights Day Resolution emphasizing equal treatment without explicit ID recognition (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Joe W. Bowser, Becky M. Heron, Michael D. Page; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page added Kendrick Estate Investment Corp. v. Durham County (09 CVS 007684) to the closed session agenda. Commissioners and staff shared announcements on Neighborhood College, FY 2010-11 nonprofit funding pre-qualification workshops, H1N1 vaccination clinics, rail-crossing safety improvements, and a domestic violence vigil. After a typographical correction to the November 4 minutes, the Board approved four sets of minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Swearing-In of Clerk to the Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored retiring General Services Director Mike Turner for 33 years of county service and retiring Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau CEO Reyn Bowman for 20 years of tourism leadership. The Board adopted a proclamation declaring December 21 as National Homeless Persons' Memorial Day and swore in newly appointed Clerk to the Board V. Michelle Parker-Evans.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Uncontested Items A-L, N, P, Q)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Items M, O, and R were pulled from the consent agenda for separate discussion and votes. The Board approved the remaining consent items (A through L, N, P, and Q) without objection.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Public Hearing: T09-00002 Transportation Special Use Permit for Elementary School E
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning and transportation staff (Steve Medlin, William Judge) and Durham Public Schools counsel Grady Sanders and engineer Dan Jewell presented evidence for a 107,600 sq. ft., 800-student elementary school at 1417 Old Oxford Highway generating 691 AM peak trips. NCDA&CS botanist Rob Evans testified about federally endangered smooth coneflower habitat nearby, prompting a condition requiring a spring plant survey prior to site disturbance.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan Approval for Elementary School E
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the major site plan for Elementary School E on a 25-acre parcel under the 24.5% high-density watershed option in the Falls/Jordan protected area. After clarifying site impervious surface thresholds, the Board approved the major site plan.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Internal Audit of DSS Families First Faith-Based Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Joe W. Bowser challenged the County's internal audit and newspaper reporting on the Families First program operated by Durham Congregations in Action and Rev. Pebbles Lucas. Bowser presented letters and Governor's Award documentation indicating over 80 congregations had participated rather than the 39 cited in the audit.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item M: Former Jail / Criminal Justice Resource Center Renovation Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated awarding the $2,193,000 base construction contract (capped at $2.5 million with contingency) for renovating the former jail / CJRC building on East Main Street. Commissioner Bowser opposed capital spending ahead of projected budget shortfalls, Vice Chair Reckhow pushed to reduce the contingency from 15% to 10% ($210,000), and Chair Page favored keeping staff's original 15% contingency without conditions.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item O: Reality Check Principles for Quality Growth Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a resolution endorsing the Reality Check Principles for Quality Growth. With no members of the public signed up to speak, the Board adopted the resolution unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item R: Revised Bill of Rights Day and Human Rights Day Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers including Joan Walsh, Ricardo Correa, and Luis Garcia Hernandez urged the Board to include explicit endorsement of Matrícula Consular / foreign consular IDs. Sheriff's Office counsel Curtis Massey explained that the Sheriff declined to recognize foreign IDs due to verification concerns and proposed compromise language affirming equal treatment regardless of national origin or immigration status, which Vice Chair Reckhow moved forward as an incremental step while Commissioner Howerton opposed it.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to extend the meeting past 11:00 PM, made appointments to county boards and commissions, and adjourned to closed session regarding IBM Credit Corp. tax appeal and Kendrick Estates v. Durham County.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 2, November 4 (as amended), November 9, and November 23, 2009 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved with a minor grammatical correction to the November 4, 2009 minutes.

votes.item_title: T09-00002 Transportation Special Use Permit for Elementary School E (1417 Old Oxford Hwy)
votes.discussion_detail: Quasi-judicial approval with staff conditions plus an added condition requiring an endangered smooth coneflower survey in spring prior to site disturbance.

votes.item_title: Major Site Plan for Elementary School E
votes.discussion_detail: Approved major site plan for 107,600 sq. ft. school under the 24.5% high-density watershed option.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item M: Former Jail / CJRC Building Renovation Contract with 10% Contingency Cap
votes.notes: Bowser opposed the capital expenditure during economic strain; Page opposed adding the 10% contingency restriction.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $2,193,000 base construction contract while reducing the contingency allowance from 15% to 10% ($210,000), as accepted by General Services Director Mike Turner.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item O: Resolution Endorsing Reality Check Principles for Quality Growth
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted regional quality growth principles resolution unanimously.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item R: Revised Bill of Rights Day and Human Rights Day Resolution
votes.notes: An earlier motion to defer by Howerton failed for lack of a second; Howerton voted nay because resident advocates sought stronger ID protections.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted revised resolution removing explicit consular ID endorsement while pledging equal law enforcement treatment regardless of immigration status.

votes.item_title: Motion to Extend Meeting Past 11:00 PM
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended time limit to complete board appointments and closed session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session (IBM Credit Corp. & Kendrick Estates Litigation)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under attorney-client privilege.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: CJRC / Former Jail Renovation Contract and Contingency Cap
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over approving the $2.193M CJRC renovation contract with a reduced 10% contingency cap.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the construction contract while tightening the contingency cap from 15% to 10% ($210,000) to control project cost creep.
side_a_arguments: Requiring Board approval above a 10% contingency protects taxpayers from change-order creep while honoring previously issued bond commitments.
General Services Director Mike Turner confirmed staff could work within a 10% contingency and start disruptive demolition during the holidays.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose either the capital expenditure altogether amid fiscal pressure (Bowser) or oppose restricting staff's 15% contingency allowance (Page).
side_b_arguments: Bowser argued the county should halt discretionary capital projects rather than risk layoffs, service cuts, or a projected property tax increase.
Page argued the Board should trust staff's recommendation of a 15% contingency for an old former jail with concealed conditions behind walls.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-2 with the 10% contingency cap.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Consular ID Language in Bill of Rights / Human Rights Day Resolution
disagreements.summary: Commissioners divided 4-1 over adopting a Sheriff-negotiated resolution that omitted explicit acceptance of Matrícula Consular and foreign government IDs.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the revised resolution affirming equal policing regardless of immigration status as a constructive first step without compelling the Sheriff to accept unvalidated foreign IDs.
side_a_arguments: The Sheriff's Office cited verification concerns with foreign consular IDs but agreed to explicit equal-treatment and non-discrimination language.
Passing the compromise resolution moves human rights dialogue forward immediately rather than stalling.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose (or defer) the diluted resolution because immigrant community advocates requested retention of consular ID recognition.
side_b_arguments: Public speakers representing immigrant residents urged the Board not to drop recognition of foreign IDs without broader community agreement.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 after an earlier deferral motion by Howerton failed for lack of a second.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting with a three-member quorum (Chair Michael D. Page, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser; Commissioners Becky M. Heron and Brenda A. Howerton had excused absences), the Board passed all agenda items unanimously 3-0. Commissioners presented the Community Circle Award to Hold Your Head Up founder Rachel Grady and recognized County State Fair volunteers. On pulled consent Item 7K, Commissioner Bowser questioned whether a Cooperative Extension gang-outreach position improperly targeted a specific ethnicity rather than bilingual skill, and County Attorney Lowell Siler clarified hiring follows merit rules. On pulled consent Item 7Q, residents questioned the $142,200 Durham Chamber of Commerce contract over minority contracting inclusion before the Board approved it, and following a public hearing, the Board adopted Unified Development Ordinance sedimentation and erosion control amendments implementing state Falls Lake mandates.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Commissioners Heron and Howerton on excused absence, Chair Page convened the three-member quorum and noted the removal of the Families First internal audit review from the agenda. The Board approved minutes from the October 5 work session, October 26 regular session, and October 28 budget workshop.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Hold Your Head Up and NC State Fair Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented the Commissioners' Community Circle Award to Hold Your Head Up, a youth organization founded by Rachel Grady serving youth in Oxford Manor and McDougald Terrace. Commissioners also recognized county staff and NCACC State Fair booth volunteers for winning third place.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A-J, L-P, R)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consent Items 7K and 7Q were pulled at citizen request by Victoria Peterson. The Board unanimously approved all remaining consent items.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7K: Cooperative Extension / Project Build Gang Outreach Position
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $28,000 grant-funded FTE street outreach position for Cooperative Extension's Project Build after Victoria Peterson questioned recruitment practices and Commissioner Bowser challenged staff remarks referencing hiring a Latino candidate. County Manager Ruffin and County Attorney Siler clarified the position is recruited strictly on merit with a Spanish bilingual requirement.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7Q: Durham Chamber of Commerce Industrial Development Contract ($142,200)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson argued the $142,200 Chamber economic development contract lacked an open RFP process and omitted minority and women-owned firms. Vice Chair Reckhow noted the Board had reduced the annual contract by $30,000 during budget cuts and moved forward with approval.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change — Sedimentation and Erosion Control
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning and Engineering staff presented Unified Development Ordinance text amendments implementing Session Law 2009-486 (Falls Lake temporary ground-cover rules) alongside Environmental Enhancements Steering Committee recommendations, previously backed 13-0 by the Planning Commission. No speakers opposed the changes.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners completed written ballots to fill vacancies on county boards and commissions, noting an appointment to the Library Board of Trustees was deferred to the next meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 5, October 26, and October 28, 2009 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes with Becky M. Heron and Brenda A. Howerton on excused absence.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 7K: Cooperative Extension Project Build Street Outreach FTE ($28,000 Grant)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after County Attorney confirmed non-discriminatory merit recruitment with bilingual Spanish proficiency.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 7Q: Durham Chamber of Commerce Industrial Development Contract ($142,200)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved annual economic development contract following reduction of $30,000 from prior year.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Change — Sedimentation and Erosion Control (SL 2009-486 Compliance)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Planning Commission-backed (13-0) UDO sedimentation and erosion control revisions.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With four commissioners present (Chair Michael D. Page, Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, Commissioner Becky M. Heron, and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused absent), the Board split repeatedly over transparency on the Jordan Lake rezoning protest petition and school land acquisition. Commissioner Heron's motion to receive an open-session legal report on why the Jordan Lake protest petition was invalidated failed 2-2 (Ayes: Becky M. Heron, Ellen W. Reckhow; Nays: Michael D. Page, Joe W. Bowser), after which the Board voted 3-1 to discuss Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County (09 CVS 004125) and the protest petition in closed session (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Joe W. Bowser, Michael D. Page; Nay: Becky M. Heron, who read a public dissent demanding openness). Later, the Board voted 3-1 to approve purchasing 33.2 acres on South Roxboro Road for Elementary School F for $1.87 million and transferring bond funds under Capital Project Amendment 09CPA-008 (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, Michael D. Page; Nay: Joe W. Bowser, citing rock-blasting risks and recession budget constraints). Unanimous 4-0 votes appointed Clerk V. Michelle Parker-Evans and awarded $77,175 in DOST open-space matching grants.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments Debate: Jordan Lake Rezoning Protest Petition and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heron requested an open-session report from County Attorney Lowell Siler explaining why the Jordan Lake rezoning protest petition was rejected, backed by Vice Chair Reckhow. Chair Page and Commissioner Bowser objected to discussing active/threatened litigation publicly, resulting in a 2-2 tie defeating open-session review and a 3-1 vote to place Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County in closed session, prompting Heron to read a public statement urging transparency.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Home Care & Hospice Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Bowser criticized Herald-Sun coverage of the Families First internal audit and requested a November 23 agenda review. The Board approved the October 12 regular session minutes (pulling October 5 work session minutes for review) and proclaimed November 2009 as National Home Care and Hospice Month.

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Clerk to the Board V. Michelle Parker-Evans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a national recruitment process, the Board appointed V. Michelle Parker-Evans as Clerk to the Board at an annual salary of $61,000 effective November 30, 2009.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A-I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed and unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items 6A through 6I without items being pulled.

agenda_items.title: DPS Land Purchase for New Elementary School F (South Roxboro Rd) and 09CPA-008 Bond Transfer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Public Schools officials presented a $1.87 million purchase contract for 33.2 acres on South Roxboro Road appraised at $2.94 million, funded by transferring $1.086 million in 2007 bond funds and 2008 two-thirds GO bonds (09CPA-008) near five overcrowded southern elementary schools. Commissioner Bowser objected to buying unbuilt land without construction funds ahead of a projected tax hike and warned of rock-blasting damage, while the remaining three commissioners supported securing the discounted neighborhood site.

agenda_items.title: DOST Commission 2009 Matching Grants ($77,175)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and Durham Open Space & Trails (DOST) representatives presented $77,175 in matching grants for three projects: Center for Community Self-Help trail access, Friends of Mountains-to-Sea Trail Little Lick Creek bridge, and Woodcroft Community Association path repairs.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adjourned into closed session to consult with the County Attorney regarding Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County (09 CVS 004125) and property/personnel matters.

votes.item_title: Motion to Add Open-Session Legal Report on Jordan Lake Protest Petition Disallowance to Agenda
votes.notes: Page and Bowser opposed open-session debate over active/imminent litigation.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to require a public report explaining why protest petition signatures on A0900004/Z0900009 were invalidated tied 2-2 with Brenda A. Howerton absent.

votes.item_title: Motion to Add Closed Session Item on Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County (09 CVS 004125) & Protest Petition
votes.notes: Heron voted nay and read a public statement advocating open-session accountability.
votes.discussion_detail: Added closed-session legal briefing on the Jordan Lake rezoning litigation and protest petition challenge.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 12, 2009 Regular Session Minutes (Oct 5 Work Session Pulled)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved October 12 minutes and pulled October 5 work session minutes for revision.

votes.item_title: Appointment of V. Michelle Parker-Evans as Clerk to the Board ($61,000 Annual Salary)
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed V. Michelle Parker-Evans effective November 30, 2009.

votes.item_title: Elementary School F Land Acquisition ($1.87M, 33.2 Acres on South Roxboro Rd) & 09CPA-008 Bond Transfer
votes.notes: Bowser dissented due to recession tax pressures, lack of construction funding, and rock-blasting liability concerns.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved purchase contract and bond funds transfer for future Elementary School F site.

votes.item_title: DOST Commission 2009 Matching Grants ($77,175)
votes.discussion_detail: Awarded matching grants to Center for Community Self-Help, Friends of Mountains-to-Sea Trail, and Woodcroft Community Association.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Moved to closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Public Disclosure vs. Closed Session for Jordan Lake Protest Petition Review
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 2-2 on hearing an open-session explanation of why the Jordan Lake rezoning protest petition was invalidated and 3-1 on discussing the matter in closed session.
disagreements.side_a_position: Provide an open-session factual report from the County Attorney explaining why citizen protest petition signatures were ruled invalid.
side_a_arguments: Citizens who filed the protest petition deserve public transparency on why staff and the County Attorney rejected signatures.
Reckhow initially sought public facts before later supporting closed session to receive attorney-client legal advice on Southern Durham Development litigation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict legal discussion of the protest petition and Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County to closed session.
side_b_arguments: Publicly debating legal validity while litigation (09 CVS 004125) is pending violates attorney-client best practices and recent ethics guidance.
Commissioner Howerton's excused absence favored avoiding unscheduled substantive debate in open session.
disagreements.resolution: Open-session report failed 2-2; closed-session addition passed 3-1 (with Reckhow joining Page and Bowser, and Heron dissenting).

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Elementary School F Land Acquisition and Bond Transfer ($1.87M)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 over purchasing 33.2 acres on South Roxboro Road for a future elementary school.
disagreements.side_a_position: Purchase the discounted 33.2-acre parcel now using transferred bond funds to relieve five overcrowded southern elementary schools.
side_a_arguments: The $1.87M price is roughly $1.07M below the $2.94M appraisal and secures a walkable neighborhood school site.
Adjacent elementary schools operate at 104% to 144% of capacity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose purchasing land during a fiscal downturn when construction funding is unavailable and site rock-blasting poses risks.
side_b_arguments: With a projected ~5-cent tax increase looming and no school construction bond authorized, banking land ties up debt capacity.
Blasting rock on the parcel could cause structural damage to neighboring homes similar to past MLK Parkway blasting.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Reconvening after an early closed session with all five commissioners present, the Board approved every agenda item unanimously 5-0. Commissioners granted excused absences for November meetings to Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Becky M. Heron, presented the Community Circle Award to New Beginnings Outreach CDC, honored school nurse Lee Lichtenthaler, and proclaimed November as Adoption Awareness Month. On pulled consent Item 8E, public speakers Victoria Peterson and Tim Hill pressed for stronger oversight of Juvenile Crime Prevention Council and Project Build grant outcomes before the Board passed Budget Ordinance Amendment 10BCC000027 ($62,500) 5-0. Following public hearings, the Board unanimously adopted the Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report and Future Land Use Map Rectification (A09-00005) and UDO Historic Landmark Criteria revisions (TC09-00006), though commissioners flagged the need to review the fiscal impact of 50% historic property tax abatements.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Excused Absences, and Approval of September 28 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page opened the public session after an earlier closed session and oversaw unanimous votes excusing Commissioner Howerton from the November 9 and November 23 meetings and Commissioner Heron from the November 23 meeting. The Board then approved the September 28 regular session minutes.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: In a marathon late-night session with all five commissioners present, the Board unanimously approved $1.2 million in seven-year economic development incentives for EMC Corporation (5-0), a Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant reclaimed-water agreement with Cary and Wake County (5-0), a Falls Lake Water Quality Resolution (5-0), and an $8.26 million Shepard Middle School construction contract (5-0). The centerpiece dispute involved 71 public speakers on the 751 South / Jordan Lake Critical Area boundary adjustments (Plan Amendment A09-00004 and Zoning Map Change Z09-00009, ~835 acres), where despite a 12-0 Planning Commission denial recommendation and a contested invalidation of the Haw River Assembly protest petition, the Board approved both A09-00004 (3-2) and Z09-00009 (3-2) (Ayes: Joe W. Bowser, Brenda A. Howerton, Michael D. Page; Nays: Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, who cited Jordan Lake drinking-water protection and procedural flaws). Later on pulled consent Item 5B, the Board voted 4-1 to appropriate $133,192 from Community Health Trust Fund reserves for Bahama Volunteer Fire Department paramedic services (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton, Becky M. Heron, Michael D. Page; Nay: Joe W. Bowser, who objected to spending trust fund principal).

agenda_items.title: Minutes Approval and Consent Agenda (Uncontested Items A, D, E, F, H, J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the September 14 regular session minutes (5-0). Six consent items (5B, 5C, 5G, 5I, 5K, and 5L) were pulled to the end of the meeting, and the remaining uncontested consent items (A, D, E, F, H, and J) passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentives for EMC Corporation ($1.2M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a public hearing featuring business, school, and community speakers (including Victoria Peterson, Dr. Lavonia Allison, and Donald Hughes raising local hiring and clawback accountability), the Board approved $1.2 million in incentives over seven years—including $200,000 for Durham resident workforce training—for EMC's $280 million expansion and 292 jobs.

agenda_items.title: Joint Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan Amendment A09-00004 (Jordan Lake Critical Area / 751 South)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Steve Medlin, Keith Luck, Joe Carley) outlined Plan Amendment A09-00004 adjusting Jordan Lake normal pool, watershed overlays, and Urban Growth Area/tier boundaries across ~835 acres based on a NC DWQ-accepted Hunter survey, noting the Planning Commission voted 12-0 against approval and staff ruled a Haw River Assembly protest petition invalid despite a notification letter error. After hearing 71 speakers, a 3-2 majority adopted A09-00004 while Vice Chair Reckhow and Commissioner Heron dissented over water quality and process integrity.

agenda_items.title: Joint Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z09-00009 (Jordan Lake Critical Area Boundaries)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Immediately following A09-00004, the Board voted on companion Zoning Map Change Z09-00009 aligning zoning watershed overlays with the adjusted Jordan Lake normal-pool boundary. The same 3-2 coalition approved the rezoning over objections from Reckhow and Heron.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5B: Budget Ordinance Amendment 10BCC000022 ($133,192 Bahama VFD Paramedics)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $133,192 appropriation from Community Health Trust Fund / fund balance to support Bahama Volunteer Fire Department paramedic services. Commissioner Bowser opposed dipping into the Community Health Trust Fund while the remaining four commissioners approved the funding.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5C: Budget Ordinance Amendment 10BCC000023 (Reduce Trust Fund Transfer)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After staff clarified that Amendment 10BCC000023 reduced a planned transfer from the Community Health Trust Fund to the General Fund (preserving trust balance), Commissioner Bowser moved approval and the item passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 5G & 5I: Triangle WWTP Reclaimed Water ILA and Phase 3 Engineering ($72,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a unanimous motion extending the meeting past 12:30 AM to 1:15 AM, the Board approved an interlocal agreement with the Town of Cary and Wake County for Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant reclaimed water and an engineering consultant amendment up to $72,000 for Phase 3 permitting.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5K: Falls Lake Water Quality Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly reviewed and adopted the Falls Lake Water Quality Resolution.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5L: DPS Shepard Middle School Construction Contract ($8,255,600)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion on local workforce and MWBE participation with Durham Public Schools representatives, the Board approved the $8,255,600 Bar Construction contract for Shepard Middle School renovations.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved $1.2M incentive package tied to $280M capital investment, 292 jobs, and $200k Durham resident training.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Jordan Lake Critical Area Boundary Adjustments (A09-00004 & Z09-00009 / 751 South)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners divided 3-2 over shifting Jordan Lake watershed protection boundaries across ~835 acres in southern Durham County based on an applicant-funded survey accepted by NC DWQ, despite unanimous Planning Commission denial and an invalidated protest petition.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve A09-00004 and Z09-00009 using the NC Division of Water Quality-accepted survey rather than outdated 1980s USGS quad maps, expanding economic tax base while reserving site-level development scrutiny.
side_a_arguments: Under the Unified Development Ordinance, landowners bear the cost of engineering surveys, and NC DWQ accepted the Hunter survey as accurate.
Accurate boundary delineation supports southern Durham economic development and tax base growth, while any major project must return to the Board for site plan/rezoning approval.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject the boundary shifts until an independent county-funded survey validates the mapping, adhering to the Planning Commission (12-0) and EAB recommendations to safeguard Jordan Lake drinking water.
side_b_arguments: Jordan Lake is an impaired drinking-water source serving 10 million gallons per day to Durham residents.
The Planning Commission (12-0) and Environmental Affairs Board urged an independent survey following the 1999 Ellerbe Creek precedent, and erroneous staff protest-petition notice tainted the process.
disagreements.resolution: Both Plan Amendment A09-00004 and Zoning Map Change Z09-00009 passed 3-2.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Use of Community Health Trust Fund Reserves for Bahama VFD Paramedics (Item 5B)
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Bowser dissented 4-1 against appropriating $133,192 from the Community Health Trust Fund to support Bahama Volunteer Fire Department paramedic services.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve $133,192 from the Community Health Trust Fund to fund emergency paramedic coverage in northern Durham.
side_a_arguments: Paramedic response in Bahama directly serves county public health needs consistent with trust fund usage.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose spending down principal reserves in the Community Health Trust Fund.
side_b_arguments: Repeated appropriations erode the Community Health Trust Fund corpus rather than preserving principal.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all five commissioners present, the Board approved all agenda items unanimously 5-0, highlighted by major stimulus housing funds, school construction contracts, and a $70 million debt refunding order. Ceremonial presentations introduced new DSS Director Geraldine 'Jerry' Robinson, recognized Alliance of AIDS Services-Carolina and Tax Administrator Kim Simpson, celebrated the Durham Bulls' 2009 AAA National Championship, and proclaimed Big Sweep and Domestic Violence Awareness Months. On pulled consent Items 9I and 9J (renovation and roofing contracts at Neal and Carrington Middle Schools), commissioners and public advocates engaged in lengthy debate over low Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) utilization (7.9%-8.8%) and joint City/County/DPS MWBE enforcement before approving both contracts 5-0 with reservations.

agenda_items.title: Minutes Approval, Introductions, Recognitions, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the August 24 and September 8 minutes (5-0), welcomed new DSS Director Geraldine Robinson, presented the Community Circle Award to Alliance of AIDS Services-Carolina, honored Tax Administrator Kim Simpson for a remote tax kiosk productivity award, recognized the Durham Bulls' 2009 AAA National Championship, and proclaimed October as Big Sweep Month and Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Uncontested Items 9A-C, E, G-H, K-N)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Items 9D, 9F, 9I, and 9J were pulled for separate discussion. The Board unanimously approved the remaining consent agenda items.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 9D: Bahama VFD Tanker Truck Replacement ($320,000 Fund Balance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed purchasing a replacement fire tanker for Bahama VFD using $320,000 in fire district fund balance before 2010 emissions rules raised vehicle costs by $11,000. The Board approved the expenditure unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 9F: ARRA Homelessness Prevention and Rapid Rehousing Grant ($789,101)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS presented a $789,101 American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) Homelessness Prevention and Rapid Rehousing grant funding a provisional social worker position and a subcontract with Housing for New Hope. Public speakers and commissioners questioned subcontracting oversight and equitable access before approving the grant 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 9I & 9J: DPS Neal Middle School and Carrington Middle School Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On pulled items for Neal Middle School (Riggs-Harrell Builders, 7.9% MWBE) and Carrington Middle School roof replacement ($875,900, AAR of NC, 8.8% MWBE), Commissioner Bowser, Dr. Lavonia Allison, and Victoria Peterson criticized single-prime bidding and urged a unified City-County-DPS MWBE office. Bowser moved approval of Neal Middle School with reservations, and both contracts passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $70 Million Refunding General Obligation Bond Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff held the required public hearing on a bond order authorizing up to $70 million in refunding bonds for Series 2000 and 2002 general obligation debt projected to capture over 6% debt service savings. No speakers opposed the bond order.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board completed board and commission appointments and adjourned into closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development location incentives.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 24 and September 8, 2009 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes unanimously.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved pre-2010 emissions tanker order saving $11,000.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 9F: ARRA Homelessness Prevention and Rapid Rehousing Grant ($789,101)
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted ARRA stimulus homelessness grant with Housing for New Hope subcontract.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 9I: DPS Neal Middle School Renovation Contract (Riggs-Harrell Builders)
votes.discussion_detail: Moved with reservations by Bowser regarding 7.9% MWBE participation and single-prime contracting.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 9J: DPS Carrington Middle School Roof Replacement ($875,900, AAR of NC)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved roof replacement contract featuring 8.8% MWBE participation.

votes.item_title: $70 Million Refunding General Obligation Bond Order (Series 2000 & 2002)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted GO refunding bond order following public hearing.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for economic development business attraction.
