meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all five commissioners present, the Board passed every action item unanimously 5-0. Commissioners proclaimed Family Day and Minority Enterprise Development Week, during which Commissioner Bowser criticized a 2% MWBE participation rate on the Human Services Complex single-prime contract. On consent agenda pulls, the Board approved a 10-month contract for 12 DPS school social workers (5-0) while pressing for seven delayed Child and Family Support Team contracts and postponed the Durham Chamber of Commerce contract to September 28. Following public hearings, the Board approved Zoning Map Change Z07-41 (5622 Grandale Drive, 16-lot subdivision) with a 6-foot buffer fence condition (5-0), renamed five South Austin Avenue / Hopson Road street segments (5-0), continued the Jordan Lake Critical Area Plan Amendment hearing to October 12 (5-0), and authorized refunding up to $70 million in Series 2000 and 2002 General Obligation bonds for an estimated $3.4 million in savings (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Family Day / Minority Enterprise Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Bowser disputed a News & Observer characterization of his RDU airport sales-tax sharing remarks, and the Board approved the August 3 work session and August 10 regular session minutes (5-0). Commissioners proclaimed September 28 as Family Day and October 5-9 as Minority Enterprise Development Week, sparking criticism from Bowser over low 2% MWBE subcontracting on the Human Services Complex.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Uncontested Items 7A, B, D-H, K-S)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consent Item 7I was removed completely and Item 7J (Durham Chamber of Commerce $142,200 contract) was postponed until September 28 due to the Chamber representative's absence, while Item 7C was pulled for discussion. All other consent items passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7C: Durham Public Schools Social Worker Services Contract (12 Positions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS and Board members reviewed the 10-month contract funding 12 school social workers in Durham Public Schools. Vice Chair Reckhow, Commissioner Heron, and Chair Page pressed staff on seven delayed Child and Family Support Team (CFST) school nurse and social worker contracts before approving Item 7C unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z07-41 (5622 Grandale Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented revised development plans for 5622 Grandale Drive (7.87 acres rezoned from RR to RS-10 for 16 single-family lots) after the applicant added a committed element to install a 6-foot solid treated wood privacy fence buffering the neighboring McLam and Kilpatrick parcels. The rezoning passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Renaming (South Austin Avenue / Hopson Road Segments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented street renaming of five segments near Research Triangle Park (renaming South Austin Avenue and portions of Hopson Road to Louis Stephens Drive, Solutions Drive, Experiment Drive, and Strategic Drive). With no public opposition, the Board approved the renamings 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Continuance: Jordan Lake Critical Area Plan Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After opening the Jordan Lake Critical Area Comprehensive Plan Amendment public hearing, the Board voted unanimously to continue the hearing to October 12, 2009 to align with companion zoning review.

agenda_items.title: Authorization to Refund Series 2000 & 2002 General Obligation Bonds (Up to $70M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick presented a bond refunding resolution authorizing refunding up to $70 million of Series 2000 and 2002 General Obligation bonds, projected to achieve ~5.5% ($3.4 million) present-value savings.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Economic Development & Southern Durham Development Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session regarding economic development incentives and Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County (09 CVS 4125).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes with a typographical correction.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved 10-month school social worker contract while urging completion of pending CFST contracts.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved rezoning for 16 residential lots with added committed element for a 6-ft solid wood fence along neighboring property lines.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved renaming five roadway segments in the RTP vicinity.

votes.discussion_detail: Continued public hearing to October 12, 2009.

votes.discussion_detail: Authorized GO bond refunding projected to save ~$3.4M (~5.5%).

meetings.executive_summary: With all five commissioners present, the Board administered the oath of office to new County Attorney Lowell Siler, honored Parkwood VFD Assistant Chief Andy Barringer and late former Mayor Chester L. Jenkins, and recorded two 4-1 split votes. On pulled consent Item 7G, the Board voted 4-1 to award annual Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant chemical contracts renewable by the County Manager for up to five years (Ayes: Becky M. Heron, Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, Michael D. Page; Nay: Joe W. Bowser, who opposed delegating five-year renewal authority away from annual Board and MWBE review). On Item 8, following debate over neighborhood adjacency and Durham Public Schools site selection for New Middle School B in northern Durham/Treyburn, the Board voted 4-1 to defer the rezoning (Ayes: Brenda A. Unanimous 5-0 votes approved two RDU Airport FAA grants (7E, 7F), the 300 E. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Multi-Year Renewal Authority on Triangle WWTP Chemical Contracts (Item 7G)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over giving the County Manager authority to renew wastewater treatment plant chemical contracts annually for up to five years without annual Board bidding or approval.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve one-year chemical contracts with up to five annual manager renewals for operational stability and volume pricing.
side_a_arguments: Re-bidding specialized bulk wastewater chemicals annually is labor-intensive for staff and vendors and risks losing favorable multi-year pricing.
Staff retains authority to re-bid at any time for non-performance, and the methanol award already achieved 31.3% MBE participation via MACE Chemical.
disagreements.side_b_position: Limit delegation to two or three years rather than five years so the Board annually reviews vendor pricing and minority/women business participation.
side_b_arguments: Five-year open-ended renewal authority insulates large contracts from competitive re-bidding and obscures annual MWBE oversight.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Indefinite Deferral of New Middle School B Rezoning (Northern Durham / Treyburn)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners voted 4-1 to grant DPS's deferral request on New Middle School B so school officials could assemble site-plan data and negotiate with Treyburn-area neighbors, while Commissioner Bowser opposed deferral.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defer the rezoning without a fixed return date to encourage creative compromise between DPS and neighborhood residents.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners need enrollment data and combined site-plan/TSUP details before rejecting a school site.
Deferral preserves dialogue so DPS and residents can address traffic, busing, and neighborhood concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against deferment because the donated land parcel sits directly behind existing homes and cannot realistically win neighborhood consent.
side_b_arguments: Deferring the rezoning wastes time because neighbors will demand costly conditions on a site located too close to their backyards.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred 4-1.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all five commissioners present, the Board approved all formal votes unanimously 5-0. Following public testimony from healthcare advocates presenting 2,000 petition cards, commissioners adopted a resolution endorsing federal healthcare reform principles and added a chair cover letter and NCACC delegation resolution (5-0). The Board also recognized sustainability manager Tobin Freid and Library Director Skip Auld for national awards. On consent Item 8A (a five-year fitness center lease in the Durham Convention Center), commissioners expressed shock upon learning renovations had already been built and opened without BOCC approval and reached consensus to defer the lease to the August work session. Finally, after sharp debate and testimony from 12 public speakers including Rev. Pebbles Lucas over DSS's termination of the Families First faith-based Work First contract, the Board voted 5-0 to direct an Internal Audit of the program's 1998-2008 deliverables and FY 2009-10 funding.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence for Former Mayor Chester L. Jenkins, Agenda Adjustments, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page led a moment of silence following funeral services held earlier that day for former Durham Mayor Chester L. Jenkins, noted removal of Item 8N and addition of Item 8O from closed session, and oversaw approval of June 1 and June 8 minutes with a correction from Vice Chair Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Federal Health Care Reform Principles
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Reckhow introduced a resolution highlighting 50,500 uninsured Durham adults and safety-net hospital strain, followed by public testimony from John Parker, Donald Hughes, Dr. Lavonia Allison, and Rev. Melvin Whitley delivering 2,000 signature cards backing a public option and urging Congress not to recess in August. The Board adopted the resolution unanimously with a chair cover letter and NCACC convention submission.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions: Best of the Best Commute Program and Library Director Skip Auld
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid presented the Smart Commuter 'Best of the Best' award, reporting that employee alternative commuting reached ~10% internally (supported by the $10 pre-tax GoPass) and 23% countywide among major employers. Commissioners then recognized Library Director Skip Auld for earning a 2009 Urban Libraries Council leadership grant.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 8B-M, O) and Consensus Deferral of Item 8A (Convention Center Fitness Lease)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners approved Consent Items 8B through 8O (excluding eliminated Item 8N and pulled Item 8A, including $229,000 DSS Director salary approval for Geraldine Robinson) by a 5-0 vote. On pulled Item 8A, Vice Chair Reckhow and Commissioner Heron questioned how a fitness center in the Durham Convention Center had already been built out and opened after City Council action without County Commission approval; County Manager Ruffin apologized and the Board deferred Item 8A by consensus to the August work session.

agenda_items.title: DSS Work First Families First Contract Update and Internal Audit Directive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Bowser challenged DSS's cancellation of the Durham Congregations in Action (DCIA) Families First contract, arguing TANF federal funds were not reduced and background performance numbers conflicted with DSS testimony. DSS Vice Chair Newman Aguiar and staff cited missed deliverables (6 vs. 15 family matches) and an $85,831 line-item reduction, while 12 speakers including Rev. Pebbles Lucas defended the program's record; the Board voted 5-0 to order an Internal Audit covering 1998-2008 outcomes and FY 2009-10 funding.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners welcomed incoming DSS Director Geraldine Robinson, announced ballot appointments to nine county boards (deferring one Library Board seat lacking three votes), and entered a lengthy closed session on Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County and initial appointment conditions before adjourning at 11:58 PM with no action taken.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved with Vice Chair Reckhow's correction regarding stimulus funds discussion on page 16 of June 8 budget work session minutes.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted healthcare reform resolution to forward with a Chair cover letter to the NC Congressional Delegation, White House, and NCACC convention (with Reckhow as voting delegate).

votes.item_title: Motion Directing Internal Audit of DSS Families First Faith-Based Program (1998-2008 & FY 2009-10)
votes.discussion_detail: Directed County Manager to task the Internal Auditor with auditing 1998-2008 program results, deliverables, and funding through FY 2009-10 with participation from DCIA, Rev. Lucas, and DSS.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6); reconvened and adjourned at 11:58 PM with no action taken.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 22, 2009 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) adopted the FY 2009-2010 County budget without a property tax increase, with commissioners urging residents to contact state legislators regarding state-level budget cuts affecting local health and social services. The Board also unanimously (5-0) approved modifications to the County's 2004 interest rate swap to extend its maturity to May 1, 2031, following questioning by Commissioner Joe W. Bowser on bond maturities, BMA-to-LIBOR volatility, and tax-law risks. In ceremonial business, the Board recognized five 2009 NACo awards earned by the Durham County Public Library and the Department of Social Services, and issued proclamations for Durham College Day (June 27) and North Carolina Central University's 100th anniversary Charter Day (June 30). Commissioners also unanimously (5-0) approved the May 26 and May 28 minutes, appointed members to local boards including eight top vote-getters to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, and entered closed session (5-0) to consider the performance of a public officer before adjourning with no action taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page called the June 22, 2009 regular session to order following a closed session and led the Pledge of Allegiance. He announced that the July 22 regular session had been rescheduled to July 20, 2009 at 7:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 26 and May 28, 2009 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the May 26, 2009 regular session and the May 28, 2009 budget work session. Commissioner Becky M. Heron moved approval and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Five 2009 NACo Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Durham County's receipt of five 2009 National Association of Counties (NACo) awards across the Durham County Public Library and the Department of Social Services. Recognized library programs included Gen Text Book Club, Get Ready Let's Read, Poetry for Everyone, and Write On, while DSS was honored for the Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP), the state's first child welfare kinship care program.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Durham College Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Joe W. Bowser introduced and Chair Michael D. Page read a proclamation declaring Saturday, June 27, 2009 as Durham College Day to commemorate the 62nd anniversary of the school's founding by Dr. Lucinda McCaller Harris (later Durham Business College and Durham College). Paul Harrison accepted the proclamation on behalf of the alumni association.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: North Carolina Central University Charter Day Centennial
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page proclaimed Tuesday, June 30, 2009 as North Carolina Central University Charter Day, marking the 100th anniversary of the incorporation of the National Religious Training School and Chautauqua for the Colored Race. NCCU Chancellor Charlie Nelms and Centennial Planning Committee co-chair Bill Evans thanked the Board and invited residents to centennial events.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of the FY 2009-2010 County Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following prior budget deliberations (partly truncated in the transcript digest), commissioners emphasized avoiding a tax rate increase during the economic downturn and urged citizens to contact state legislators regarding state cost-shifts in health and social services. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser moved and Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded adoption of the FY 2009-2010 budget.

agenda_items.title: Modifications to the 2004 Interest Rate Swap
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director George Quick presented a recommendation, developed with financial advisor DEC Associates and a special swap advisor, to amend the County's 2004 interest rate swap by extending its maturity to May 1, 2031, noting more than $4 million in cumulative savings over 58 months and $1.2 million received in FY 2009. Commissioners questioned bond maturities, BMA-to-LIBOR rate volatility, and tax-law risks affecting the 65 percent spread before unanimously approving the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Auto Dealership Revenue Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During ballot distribution, Commissioner Joe W. Bowser asked staff to estimate tax revenue losses from closed auto dealerships including Johnson Auto Dealership and Michael Jordan Lincoln Mercury. The Clerk announced appointments across several boards, and because votes were split for the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, the Board voted unanimously to appoint the top eight vote-getters.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider the performance of a public officer. Upon returning to open session at 02:35:37, the Chair reported that no action was taken and adjourned the meeting at 9:35 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Budget Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 11, 2009 budget wrap-up work session, the Board of County Commissioners reviewed the County Manager's final FY 2009-2010 add-delete list and grant adjustments ahead of the June 22 adoption vote, taking no formal votes. Staff detailed technical adjustments in the court budget, potential state cost-shifts for a Chapel Hill Boulevard probation and parole office lease, General Services position reorganization, reductions in joint City-County departments (GIS, Emergency Communications, and Planning) from City personnel changes, and a $20,000 local appropriation to preserve Summer Youth Program slots for returning youth ineligible under federal stimulus rules. Commissioners also reviewed accounting transfers for the employee benefits plan and expressed disagreement over the Board's own travel budget: Chair Michael D. Page and Commissioner Becky M. Heron favored capping individual commissioner travel allocations (such as $3,000 per member within a $15,000 total) to set an example during departmental cuts, whereas Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and newly elected Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued that $3,000 was insufficient for NACo/NCACC leadership duties and commissioner training and favored $4,000 per member or preserving travel flexibility.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Attendance Wait
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page delayed starting the 9:00 a.m. work session briefly until Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and Commissioner Joe W. Bowser arrived so staff would not have to repeat explanations on social worker positions and Medicaid cost settlements.

agenda_items.title: FY 2009-2010 Budget Add-Delete List and Summer Youth Program Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff reviewed added expenditures, offsetting reductions, and grant-related adjustments, including a $340 court lease correction, potential state offloading of a Chapel Hill Boulevard probation/parole lease, removal of a DA's office ADA salary increase, and General Services reorganization preserving a solid waste tech slot by cutting a vacant maintenance tech slot. Staff also proposed $20,000 in local funding so returning youth excluded by federal stimulus income and eligibility criteria could continue in the eight-week Summer Youth Program, alongside offsets from City of Durham personnel cuts in GIS, Emergency Communications, and Planning.

agenda_items.title: Employee Benefits Plan Accounting Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In response to written questions from Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, staff explained that consolidating flex benefits into a single transfer explained the apparent 2.4 to 2.5 percent increase and agreed to Reckhow's suggestion to rename the fund from 'cafeteria fund' to 'benefits plan.' Staff confirmed the final budget ordinance would come forward for adoption on June 22.

agenda_items.title: Board of County Commissioners Travel Budget Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager noted that the Board's travel budget previously covered only three traveling commissioners but now five commissioners travel, recommending $4,000 per member if individual caps were instituted rather than Commissioner Becky M. Heron's $3,000-per-member ($15,000 total) proposal. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued that conferences yield valuable grant intelligence and training for new commissioners, while Heron and Chair Michael D. Page maintained that commissioners needed to set an example on spending restraint.

agenda_items.title: Mental Health Caseload Risks and School Backpack Flyers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff cautioned that an uptick of two to three mental health cases per week could strain staffing and require tapping mental health funds later in the year. A commissioner also displayed a multi-color flyer sent home in elementary school backpacks as an example of avoidable printing expense, before the session adjourned just before 11:00 a.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Budget Worksession
disagreements.issue: Board of County Commissioners Travel Budget Allocation and Individual Caps
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed during the budget wrap-up session over whether to cap individual commissioner travel at $3,000 each within a $15,000 pool or allocate $4,000 per member ($20,000) to support national/state conference participation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support a higher travel allocation ($4,000 per commissioner or flexible pool) to cover state and national conferences, committee leadership duties, and new-commissioner training.
side_a_arguments: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow serves as a chair/co-chair on national and state steering committees and needs $4,000 to attend legislative and summer conferences.
Conference attendance has directly produced valuable federal stimulus grant leads (such as COPS and JAG offsets) that benefit the County budget.
Newly elected commissioners need out-of-county training and peer learning opportunities.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict the Board's travel budget (e.g., $15,000 total / $3,000 per commissioner cap) to set an example of fiscal restraint.
side_b_arguments: Departments and agencies were asked to absorb 6 to 10 percent budget cuts and curtail travel.
Commissioners must set a visible example of spending restraint rather than expanding their own $20,000 travel budget.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken during the budget work session; item carried forward toward the June 22 budget ordinance.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Budget Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 9, 2009 follow-up budget work session with Durham Public Schools (DPS), commissioners pressed school officials on how federal stimulus funds and the discontinuation of the $2 million Reading Recovery program affected DPS's local budget request. Although no formal votes were taken, the Board reached clear consensus to hold the line at the County Manager's recommended DPS funding level—a $2.9 million reduction compared to DPS's request for a $1.4 million increase—citing insufficient transparency, unconvincing justification for 26 new teaching positions, and DPS's refusal to answer earlier written budget questions. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow advocated re-instituting a formal Memorandum of Understanding with DPS requiring regular performance reporting, and commissioners discussed staff projections of a 5-cent property tax rate equivalent needed in FY 2011 for Capital Improvement Plan debt service, planning a fall retreat to evaluate county program reductions rather than relying solely on tax increases.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Q&A with Durham Public Schools on FY 2009-2010 Budget and Reading Recovery
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the follow-up budget session with DPS officials, asking whether the district could meet the County halfway on its request. Commissioners questioned DPS on ending the $2 million-per-year Reading Recovery program after 13 years without measurable literacy gains and pressed where those freed local dollars would go if literacy coaches were funded via federal stimulus, while DPS cited non-supplant rules, heating/cooling costs for a new school, and a $20 million state cut.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Deliberation on DPS Funding Consensus, MOU Proposal, and FY 2011 CIP Tax Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After DPS representatives departed, commissioners expressed consensus to maintain the County Manager's recommended school allocation rather than increase funding, noting the $4.3 million gap largely funded 26 new teaching positions while lacking transparency and candor. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow proposed reviving a 1990s-style Memorandum of Understanding with DPS for regular financial and performance reporting, and Chair Michael D. Page directed the Manager to inform DPS of the Board's firm position while commissioners discussed holding a fall retreat to address a projected 5-cent CIP debt-service gap in FY 2011.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its June 8, 2009 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved the May 4 and May 11 minutes, recognized high school senior Alan Marcos Faircloth as a NACo Nationwide scholarship winner, and issued a June 2009 Hunger Awareness Month proclamation highlighting a 120 percent surge in County food stamp recipients since 2001. The Board also adopted a resolution opposing Section 10.26 of North Carolina Senate Bill 202 (the Public Health Improvement Plan), warning against unfunded state restructuring of local public health systems without local government input. Following public hearings with no speakers, commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved two Unified Development Ordinance text amendments: Technical Changes 5 (TC09-03) and Outdoor Recreation standards (TC09-01) requested by the Triangle Sports Social Club.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the June 8, 2009 regular session, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and announced that applications were open until July 27, 2009 for the fall term of the nine-week Durham Neighborhood College co-sponsored by the City and County.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 4 and May 11, 2009 Minutes and Scott King Road MOA Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the minutes from the May 4, 2009 work session and May 11, 2009 regular session on a motion by Commissioner Becky M. Heron, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton. A commissioner also confirmed with the County Manager that the Memorandum of Agreement with Durham Public Schools regarding the Scott King Road property remained on staff's work list.

agenda_items.title: Recognition: NACo Nationwide Scholarship Winner Alan Marcos Faircloth
agenda_items.discussion_summary: David Turner of Nationwide Retirement Solutions and Human Resources Director Marqueta Welton presented graduating high school senior Alan Marcos Faircloth with a NACo Nationwide college scholarship based on his essay on national retirement savings policy.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: June 2009 Hunger Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a proclamation declaring June 2009 as Hunger Awareness Month, citing Durham County's 15.6 percent poverty rate, food bank distributions exceeding 1.12 million pounds annually, and a 120 percent increase in DSS food stamp recipients from 12,837 in 2001 to 27,747 in April 2009.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing Public Health Improvement Plan in Senate Bill 202
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read a resolution opposing Section 10.26 of Senate Bill 202, objecting that the proposed Public Health Improvement Plan lacked input from local officials and public health professionals, imposed an unreasonable timeline, duplicated an existing task force, and redistributed insufficient state funds while counties shoulder rising local mental health obligations.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment Technical Changes 5 (TC09-03)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented TC09-03, making minor technical clarifications across the Unified Development Ordinance, including consistent use of 'townhouse' rather than 'townhome.' Commissioners asked about citizen notification tracking via the Land Development Office system and enforcement of illegal real estate signs around Southpoint before opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment Outdoor Recreation (TC09-01)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented TC09-01, requested by the Triangle Sports Social Club, replacing the requirement for direct access from a major or minor thoroughfare with tailored setback and minor special use permit standards to protect residential neighborhoods. After questions regarding a proposed Rim Road soccer complex, the Board opened and closed the public hearing with no speakers and unanimously approved the amendment.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Budget Worksession
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 28, 2009 joint budget work session with the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education, school board leaders presented their FY 2009-2010 budget request and objected to the 'elephant in the room' characterization made during the County Manager's May 26 budget presentation. DPS officials stated that their local increase request—covering 26 teaching positions, 18 teaching assistants, Encore support, and instructional supplies—was driven by roughly $20 million in state budget cuts rather than local expansion, noting that central office salaries were frozen and health insurance costs were rising. Commissioners, led by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, questioned why federal stimulus funds (IDEA 6B and Title I) could not backfill local cuts and pressed for clearer accounting of 30 new Exceptional Children positions, while also criticizing partial and late written responses from DPS. No formal votes were taken, and the boards agreed to schedule a follow-up session.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools FY 2009-2010 Budget Presentation and State Cut Impacts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Board of Education representatives, including Steve Martin, invoked N.C.G.S. 115C-36 and 115C-426(e) to defend their funding request for 32,000 students, half of whom are underserved. School leaders pushed back against perceived disparagement of the district in the County Manager's May 26 presentation, explaining that state cuts of $20 million drove their request for 26 teaching positions and 18 teaching assistants while central office contract raises were frozen.

agenda_items.title: Federal Stimulus Funding Restrictions, Budget Transparency, and Scheduling Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and commissioners questioned why federal stimulus funding was not backfilling the $2.8 million local reduction and queried 30 new Exceptional Children positions under Title VI. DPS finance staff explained that federal supplement-not-supplant rules barred shifting laid-off staff onto IDEA and Title I stimulus funds, prompting plans for 30 EC positions and 44 Title I academic coaches over two years, while commissioners requested fuller, timely written answers ahead of a follow-up meeting tentatively eyed for June 9.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 26, 2009 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners opened by reading an updated public charge on decorum and excusing Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton (3-0, prior to Commissioner Joe W. Bowser's arrival and Howerton's later arrival) following the passing of her mother. The Board recognized Durham County EMS paramedics for their heroic response to a fatal Russell Road house fire, honored Willis P. Witcher for nine years leading the Durham Library Foundation, and presented the Commissioners' Community Circle Award to Durham CrimeStoppers. The County Manager then presented his FY 2009-2010 recommended budget, highlighting an $18 million current-year revenue deficit and announcing a June 8 public hearing. With all five commissioners present later in the meeting, the Board unanimously (5-0) approved the 19-item Consent Agenda (including an $88.07 million capital project amendment and Gates Foundation library grants), authorized an ARRA transit grant application to NCDOT (5-0), received an H1N1 influenza briefing from Public Health Director Gayle Harris, and excused Commissioner Howerton from upcoming budget sessions (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Excusal of Commissioner Howerton, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page read an updated public charge requiring respectful conduct by commissioners and citizens, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and noted the passing of Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's mother, leading to an initial excusal vote (3-0). He also announced a June 8, 2009 public hearing on the FY 2009-2010 recommended budget.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 27, 2009 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With four commissioners present prior to Commissioner Howerton's later arrival, the Board approved the April 27, 2009 regular session minutes on a motion by Commissioner Becky M. Heron and second by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow.

agenda_items.title: Recognition: Durham County EMS Paramedics (Russell Road Structure Fire)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Liam Needham joined the Board in presenting certificates of appreciation to Durham County EMS employees for their heroic actions during a tragic structure fire on Russell Road in northern Durham County.

agenda_items.title: Recognition: Willis P. Witcher, Durham Library Foundation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board adopted a resolution honoring Willis P. Witcher for nine years as founding president of the Durham Library Foundation, during which the foundation raised $3 million including a $1.5 million National Endowment for the Humanities challenge grant, and noted the creation of the Willis P. Witcher Opportunity Fund as Ann Craver assumed the presidency.

agenda_items.title: Commissioners' Community Circle Award: Durham CrimeStoppers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page presented the Commissioners' Community Circle Award to Durham CrimeStoppers in recognition of its community public safety contributions.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of County Manager's Recommended FY 2009-2010 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented his ninth budget to Durham County, calling it the most difficult of his 31-year career amid the economic downturn. He reported that the current-year deficit announced at $14.2 million in January had grown past $18 million due to falling sales and property tax collections (remaining budget details truncated in digest).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-T, excluding M and O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With all five commissioners now seated, the Board approved the Consent Agenda (with Item M scratched and Item O intentionally blank), encompassing a $29,250 Gates Foundation library grant, a $189,067 federal grant for Lincoln Community Health Center, an $88,072,096 capital project amendment, Cane Creek open space grant agreements, Creekside Elementary NCDOT encroachments, a Lakeview School gym addition, Southwest Regional Library easements, and FY 2010 Planning/Inspections fees. A commissioner praised County departments for securing external grants during the budget crunch.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Cooperative Extension ARRA 2009 Transit Grant Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers and Transportation Access Coordinator Johnny Ford requested authorization to apply by June 30 for NCDOT ARRA stimulus capital funds to purchase vans and fund one mobility manager position. Resident Victoria Peterson asked how many local residents would be employed, and staff clarified the NCDOT capital grant was restricted to transportation infrastructure rather than general employment.

agenda_items.title: Briefing on Novel H1N1 Influenza Outbreak and Mitigation Plans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Gayle Harris briefed the Board on the Novel H1N1 ('swine flu') outbreak first identified in April, advising residents on hand hygiene, staying home when ill, and potential social distancing measures at upcoming graduations and public events.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton for Upcoming Budget and Work Sessions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following condolences to the County Attorney on a family loss, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton requested formal excusal from the upcoming Thursday budget session and Monday work session due to her mother's passing. The Board approved the excusal unanimously and adjourned at 8:15 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 11, 2009 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners approved the April minutes (4-0) and the 15-item Consent Agenda (5-0), which included an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham launching shared Government TV on Channel 8 and a $110,000 contingency transfer for the Durham Convention Center's operating deficit. On the meeting's major action item, the Board unanimously (5-0) adopted a substitute motion by Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow authorizing Durham Public Schools to purchase southern Durham parcels for $2,710,610 for a single future school—rather than two—and directing staff to negotiate an interlocal agreement deleting condition bullet two and broadening stakeholder design participation under bullet eight, though one commissioner noted on the record that the Board lacked legal authority to restrict DPS to one school. Commissioners also conducted board and commission appointments amid public comment from Victoria Peterson regarding Workforce Development Board residency and oversight, entered closed session (5-0), and returned to unanimously (5-0) approve three agricultural conservation easement options on the Carrington Family, Ellis, and Coats farms.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Announcements (Durham Government TV Channel 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and announced that as of May 4, the City and County began sharing Time Warner Cable Channel 8 for Durham Government TV while local community programming moved to Channel 18. He also announced the County Manager would present the FY 2009-2010 budget on May 26, and Commissioner Becky M. Heron announced the Saturday Walk for the Animals.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 6 and April 13, 2009 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With four commissioners present at the start of the meeting, the Board approved the minutes from the April 6, 2009 work session and April 13, 2009 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At a commissioner's request, Chair Michael D. Page read summary titles of Consent Agenda Items A through O while noting they could be displayed on screen. Items included HUD HOME/ESG submissions, animal ordinance amendments, the Durham Government TV interlocal agreement, a DPS Lakewood YMCA contract, an RDU Airport Authority grant, DSS and Cooperative Extension grant amendments, a $110,000 Convention Center deficit transfer from BOCC contingency, annual advisory board reports, and BOCC Rules of Procedure.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Real Property Acquisition in Southern Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Assistant Superintendent for Operational Services Mr. Osteen presented the proposed $2,710,610 purchase of southern Durham parcels (below the $3,177,000 appraisal), noting DPS agreed to build one school rather than two. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 13, 2009 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners divided 3-2 over the legal process for correcting the Jordan Lake 216-foot normal pool boundary and watershed overlay map affecting over 300 parcels tied to the 751 South project. Commissioner Joe W. Bowser moved to accept a February 4, 2009 state Division of Water Quality letter and a January 6, 2006 Planning Department interpretation as an administrative map correction without holding a public hearing, arguing the UDO allows administrative corrections; however, the Board adopted Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow's substitute motion (seconded by Commissioner Becky M. Heron) directing staff to process the map amendments through statutory and UDO public hearing procedures by a 3-2 vote, with Ayes from Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, and Brenda A. Howerton, and Nays from Joe W. Bowser and Michael D. Page. Earlier in the meeting, Commissioner Bowser disputed a Herald-Sun characterization that he was 'in the camp of the developers' on the 751 project, and the Board approved uncontested March minutes (5-0) after pulling two sets for corrections. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Jordan Lake 216 MSL Normal Pool Line / Watershed Overlay Map Amendment Process (Public Hearing vs. Administrative Correction)
disagreements.summary: The Board split 3-2 over whether updating the Jordan Lake 216-foot normal pool watershed overlay boundary affecting over 300 parcels required statutory and UDO public hearing map-amendment procedures or could be executed administratively without a public hearing.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require full statutory and Unified Development Ordinance map-amendment procedures, including public hearings, as recommended by the County Manager, County Attorney, and Planning Director.
side_a_arguments: Over 300 parcels are affected, so UDO Section 4.1.1.3A (single split-parcel reconsideration) does not apply.
State law and the UDO require public hearings for zoning/overlay map changes rather than administrative adjustments.
Following established legal procedure protects the integrity of the process and follows the advice of the County Attorney, Manager, and Planning Director.
disagreements.side_b_position: Treat the 216 MSL boundary update as an administrative map correction based on the February 4, 2009 Division of Water Quality letter and January 6, 2006 Planning Department interpretation without holding a public hearing.
side_b_arguments: The ordinance contains a provision for correcting mapping errors administratively rather than treating the update as a rezoning move.

A previous late-night 11:00 p.m. vote after closed session sent maps to Raleigh without a public hearing, and resolving the waterline dispute now lets the developer submit a rezoning/development plan for formal review.
Licensed surveyors should not be impugned, and prolonged delay harms economic and employment prospects.
disagreements.resolution: Substitute motion passed 3-2 (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, Brenda A. Howerton; Nays: Joe W. Bowser, Michael D. Page).

meetings.executive_summary: At its March 23, 2009 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners announced its March 24 FY 2009-2010 budget town hall at White Rock Baptist Church, discussed adding northern and southern Durham budget hearings, and unanimously (5-0) approved the February 16 and February 23 minutes. The Board presented the March Anchor Award to Engineering Department real estate specialist Jane Korest for her open space and farmland preservation work and issued proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month (April) and Earth Month (April). meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 23, 2009 work-only special session, the Board of County Commissioners met to address the Jordan Lake watershed protection overlay boundary line without public comment. City-County Planning Director Steve Medlin reviewed the history from 1994 USGS quadrangle mapping through a 2005–2006 property owner survey on NC 751 and the state Division of Water Quality's February 2009 approval of Durham's submitted survey data as better information. The County Attorney advised that legally adopting the revised watershed boundaries requires formal Unified Development Ordinance amendment procedures—Planning Commission review, property-owner notice, public hearing, and Board vote—rather than an administrative map correction. Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Ellen W. Reckhow differed over whether the update should be treated as a simple correction or a formal zoning map change, and the Board reached consensus to schedule a public hearing, peer review panel, and UNC Institute of Government opinion review for April 13, 2009 before moving to enter closed session with no formal policy votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary Line History and DWQ Review Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the work-only special session on the Jordan Lake watershed boundary line. City-County Planning Director Steve Medlin traced Durham's 1985 and 1994 watershed overlay mapping using 10-foot USGS quadrangle maps, a 2005 field survey request under UDO Section 4.11.3 for property west of NC 751, and the 2006 administrative zoning map revision despite UDO Section 3.5 limits on non-board map changes. He reported that the state Division of Water Quality (DWQ) approved Durham's submitted survey data in February 2009 as better information, allowing Durham to adopt revised boundaries through statutory and UDO processes while noting potential impacts on Orange County, Chatham County, Chapel Hill, and Cary.

agenda_items.title: Board Deliberation: Map Correction vs. Zoning Amendment and April 13 Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated whether implementing the DWQ-approved Jordan Lake boundary constitutes an administrative map correction or a formal zoning and comprehensive plan amendment, with Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Ellen W. Reckhow taking opposing views on correction versus change. The County Attorney advised—citing a prior Attorney General's opinion—that changing watershed overlay boundaries without Planning Commission review, neighbor notice, and a public hearing would expose subsequent rezonings to legal defeat. Commissioners also discussed funding an additional 8-to-10-week survey from contingency funds, and Chair Michael D. disagreements.issue: Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary: Administrative Map Correction vs. Formal Zoning Amendment
disagreements.summary: Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Ellen W. Reckhow took opposing positions on whether implementing the state-approved Jordan Lake normal-pool boundary survey should be handled as an administrative map correction or as a formal zoning map and comprehensive plan amendment. The transcript explicitly notes Bowser and Reckhow on opposite sides of the correction-versus-change debate without specifying which member championed each procedural path, while the County Attorney and Commissioner Becky M. Heron warned against skipping statutory public hearing procedures and risking litigation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Treat the revised Jordan Lake watershed delineation as a map correction to existing boundaries based on updated survey data.
side_a_arguments: Updated field survey data approved by DWQ reflects more accurate physical elevations than 1994 USGS quadrangle maps.
Staff could simply update the maps to reflect the corrected boundary without a protracted rezoning process.
disagreements.side_b_position: Treat the revision as a formal zoning and comprehensive plan amendment requiring Planning Commission review, property-owner notice, public hearing, and Board vote, alongside peer review and consideration of a broader survey.
side_b_arguments: Under UDO Section 3.5, North Carolina statutes, and the County Attorney's legal opinion, changing watershed overlay boundaries is a zoning change rather than a scrivener's error.
Bypassing public hearing and notice procedures creates major litigation risk from affected residents if subsequent rezonings are challenged in court.
An independent peer review, UNC Institute of Government review, and potential 8-to-10-week comprehensive survey provide stronger legal and technical footing.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Chair Michael D. Page directed staff to schedule a public hearing, a correction-versus-change discussion, and a peer review session for April 13, 2009, and to check survey pricing.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 12, 2009 afternoon special session—a continuation of the March 2 work session—staff presented a scaled-back $790 million 2010–2019 Capital Improvement Program (CIP) reflecting board feedback and deteriorating economic conditions. Major revisions included cutting EMS facility site costs from $5.8 million to $3.1 million, replacing a $154.2 million downtown detention center expansion with a $75 million satellite facility, removing a proposed $245 million 2015 school bond referendum while keeping a $132.3 million Durham Public Schools bond in 2011, and doubling 2011 open space and farmland funding to $20 million. Commissioners also reviewed Article 40/42 sales tax shifts, Fund 125 balances, the extended 40-year Durham Regional Hospital lease, potential state cuts to reentry and after-school prevention programs such as Encore, and Commissioner Becky M. Heron's objection to late Friday agenda revisions. No formal substantive votes or split votes occurred during the work session.

agenda_items.title: Revisions to Manager's Recommended 2010–2019 Capital Improvement Program (CIP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a revised $790 million 10-year CIP with project narratives and operational cost estimates. Key changes reduced two confidential EMS site projects from $5.8 million to $3.1 million, replaced a $154.2 million downtown detention expansion with a $75 million satellite detention center, deferred a second $245 million school bond from 2015 pending an updated DPS long-range facilities plan while keeping $132.3 million for schools in 2011, and raised 2011 open space and farmland bonds to $20 million. Staff and commissioners also reviewed Article 42 point-of-sale sales tax gains (~$1.5 million), $1.5 million in Fund 125 capital reserves, avoiding a $17 million Human Services parking deck via transit passes, and the $10 million commitment under Duke's rolling 40-year Durham Regional Hospital lease.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 23, 2009 special work session, the Board welcomed visitors from Durham, England and received a Capital Improvement Plan update from Durham Public Schools Superintendent Carl Harris, who reported that 2003 bond projects were 80% paid or obligated within budget and 18 of 25 projects from the $193.4 million 2007 bond had started with strong contractor bidding competition. Commissioners pressed school officials on their expanded $780 million 10-year capital request, vacant land accounting, inner-city school utilization, high school and Creekside Elementary overcrowding, and potential interest-free federal stimulus funds, while Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow warned that continuing $482 million per decade in school bonds could threaten Durham County's AAA credit rating. The Board also reviewed single-entrance ADA accessibility for Main Library renovations and heard from its financial advisor comparing Durham's $1.1 billion 10-year CIP against peer AAA North Carolina counties, concluding that Durham's capital program size and timing—and rapid school budget growth outpacing county revenues—must be scaled back ahead of Monday's follow-up discussion. No formal votes were taken during this session.

Reckhow cautioned that $482 million in school bonds from 2001–2011 could endanger the County's AAA bond rating.

agenda_items.title: Financial Advisor Peer AAA County Analysis and School Funding Growth Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County's financial advisor compared Durham's credit profile and $1.1 billion 2010–2019 CIP against Wake, Mecklenburg, Guilford, and Forsyth counties, advising that while Durham has a sound economy (~$115,000 per capita appraised value), the size and timing of its capital plan need scaling back. Subsequent discussion highlighted that Durham Public Schools' budget grew 7.29% in 2007 and 6.78% ($6.2 million) in 2008—more than double the County's 4.51% and 3.11% revenue growth—underscoring the need to tell DPS to scale back its capital plan and establish a sustainable funding formula.

disagreements.issue: County Hiring Freeze Enforcement on Senior Administrative Vacancies vs. Frontline Positions
disagreements.summary: Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Becky M. Heron differed on how strictly to freeze outgoing Assistant Director positions in Public Health and Social Services versus waiting for spring sales tax data and department harm assessments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Do not refill outgoing Assistant Director vacancies in Public Health and Social Services until the budget improves, stop freezing frontline roles while filling top positions, and require monthly exception reports.
side_a_arguments: Senior administrative replacements strain an already tight county budget.
It is unfair to freeze lower-level frontline workers who deliver services while refilling upper-management positions.
Commissioners should receive a monthly report of all positions approved to bypass the hiring freeze.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold off on replacements for 3–4 months until March sales tax revenues and the July 1 budget are clearer, maintaining the Public Health freeze while allowing Social Services and department heads to bring back positions if delays cause major departmental harm.
side_b_arguments: Only 3–4 months remain in the fiscal year before the July 1 budget takes effect.

If Social Services faces a delay in filling its Director post, leaving the Assistant Director or facility roles unfilled could harm operations, so department heads should be able to justify critical exceptions.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the Board discussed the manager's slowed hiring numbers and Bowser's request for monthly hiring-freeze exception reporting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 12, 2009 regular session, the Board unanimously voted 5-0 to excuse Chair Michael D. Page from the January 26 meeting, added an agenda item on opposing Sunday hunting, unanimously approved (5-0) the November 24 and December 8, 2008 minutes, recognized employees Leon Wright and Jacob Cash for law enforcement support, and heard a Community Health Coalition hypertension resolution presentation. Commissioners unanimously voted 5-0 to approve Consent Items A, D, F, G, I, J, K, and L while pulling Items B, C, E, H, and M. Following a middle-portion gap in the transcript digest, the Board reviewed mid-year FY 2008–2009 budget cuts—including 3% reductions to county contracts and nonprofits ($28,415) and a proposed 100% ($550,000) reduction to new Open Space and Farmland Protection capital funding—drawing strong public pushback from farmland, open space, and homeless shelter advocates. Commissioners unanimously voted 5-0 to extend the meeting until 11:30 PM and engaged in a policy debate in which Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton sought to direct a newly freed $75,000 Eno River open space sum toward homeless shelter support while an opposing view argued the funds belonged to Open Space and defended the 24/7 Animal Protection Society operation.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Chair Page, Sunday Hunting Agenda Addition, and MLK Program Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the meeting and the Board voted 5-0 to excuse him from the January 26, 2009 meeting due to travel. By consensus, the Board added Item 14 at Commissioner Becky M. Heron's request to discuss opposing a Wildlife Resources Commission regulatory proposal permitting Sunday hunting, citing church opposition and safety risks to families in woods and parks, and announced the Wednesday Martin Luther King Jr. City-County employee program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (November 24 and December 8, 2008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered the minutes from the November 24, 2008 and December 8, 2008 regular sessions. Commissioners approved both sets of minutes unanimously without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Employee Beyond-the-Call-of-Duty Recognition (Leon Wright and Jacob Cash)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page recognized county employees Leon Wright and Jacob Cash for actions beyond the call of duty on behalf of law enforcement. Both employees received certificates of appreciation, display and monetary bonus checks, and Service Anchor to Excellence plaques.

agenda_items.title: Community Health Coalition Hypertension Call to Action Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Lane Hotbrothers, Chair of the Community Health Coalition, joined by Dr. Howard Bitz and Ms. Bice, presented on the Call to Action resolution addressing hypertension as a silent killer. She urged workplace environments that support blood pressure monitoring, healthy eating, exercise, and medication compliance.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A, D, F, G, I, J, K, and L Approved; B, C, E, H, M Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To streamline the meeting, Chair Michael D. Page skipped reading individual consent titles unless pulled. Community members pulled Items B, C, H, and M and a commissioner pulled Item E, after which the Board voted 5-0 to approve the remaining consent items A, D, F, G, I, J, K, and L.

agenda_items.title: Mid-Year FY 2008–2009 Budget Reductions: Open Space/Farmland, Nonprofits, and $75,000 Eno River Reallocation Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a mid-transcript gap, staff outlined 3% mid-year cuts to county contracts (Downtown Durham, Greater Durham Chamber, Durham Economic Resource Center) and nonprofits ($28,415), alongside a proposed 100% ($550,000) reduction to new Open Space and Farmland Protection capital funding. Speakers from the Farmland Protection Board, open space advocates, Operation Breakthrough, and Urban Ministries warned of permanent watershed farmland loss and 242 homeless residents sleeping in the cold, while Victoria Peterson questioned nonprofit oversight. Following a 5-0 vote to extend the meeting to 11:30 PM, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton advocated directing $75,000 freed from an Eno River open space exchange toward homeless shelter support, while an opposing speaker countered that the $75,000 belonged to Open Space and defended the 24/7 Animal Protection Society budget before the transcript ended.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (extend meeting); No final budget vote captured

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Mid-Year Reallocation of $75,000 Eno River Open Space Funds and Nonprofit vs. Animal Shelter / Open Space Cuts
disagreements.summary: Following public appeals from Open Space, Farmland Protection, and Urban Ministries homeless shelter advocates regarding mid-year FY 2008–2009 budget cuts, board members debated whether $75,000 freed from a past Eno River open space exchange should go to homeless shelter support or remain in Open Space, as well as the fairness of 3% nonprofit cuts alongside $611,562 in Animal Protection Society funding.
disagreements.side_a_position: Direct the $75,000 Eno River open space refund toward homeless shelter support and prioritize human shelter needs over animal shelter funding.
side_a_arguments: Cutting Urban Ministries by 3% could leave 242 homeless individuals sleeping out in the cold.
Human homelessness needs should take priority over $611,562 in funding for the Animal Protection Society.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the $75,000 in Open Space/Farmland Protection where it originated and recognize the County's ongoing investments in both Urban Ministries and 24/7 animal shelter operations.
side_b_arguments: The $75,000 originally came from Open Space funds and rightly belongs to Open Space and Farmland Protection, which already faced a 100% ($550,000) mid-year cut to new capital funds.
The County has already poured substantial capital funds into building and renovating Urban Ministries facilities, while the animal shelter operates 24/7 including weekends and nights.
disagreements.resolution: No final vote on the mid-year budget reductions or the $75,000 reallocation was captured before the transcript ended at 04:07:55.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 8, 2008 Regular Session—the first regular meeting following the December 1 swearing-in and presided over by new Chair Michael D. Page—the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved all actions unanimously by 5-0 voice votes, with no split or contested votes. Commissioners offered post-election remarks, thanked newly named Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow for her six years as Chair, and urged a thorough January line-item budget review ahead of the annual retreat. The Board approved a $50,000 budget ordinance amendment recognizing half of a $100,000 Herndon Foundation donation via the Durham Library Foundation for public art at South Regional Library, adopted a resolution honoring the late photojournalist and longtime county meeting videographer James Edward Fields Sr., and passed the 17-item consent agenda (10A through 10Q) including a $3.3 million capital project amendment and $3.75 million construction contract with Resolute Building Company for the Southwest Regional Branch Library and a $500,000 One NC pass-through grant for Quintiles Transnational Corp. After Vice Chair Reckhow pulled Item 10N to urge expediting the sale of two Lowe's Grove parcels to reduce COPS debt issuance for libraries, the Board approved Item 10N 5-0 and received a briefing on the 2035 Long Range Transportation Plan from Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO staff.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Michael D. Page opened the December 8, 2008 Regular Session, noted a modified agenda action form for Item 10Q, and added a brief presentation from the Eno River Association following announcements. The Board then approved the minutes of the November 10, 2008 Regular Session and December 1, 2008 Work Session by a 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Eno River Association Calendar Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Jacobs of the Eno River Association presented the organization's new calendar to the Board. Chair Page thanked Jacobs for the association's work and praised the bird imagery featured on the calendar cover.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Post-Swearing-In Remarks and Recognition of Vice Chair Reckhow (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following their December 1 swearing-in, commissioners offered remarks on the new term. Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow encouraged a thorough January line-item departmental budget review before the upcoming retreat to identify potential savings amid tight revenues, while Chair Page pledged high integrity and led applause honoring Reckhow for her prior six years as Chair.

agenda_items.title: Herndon Foundation Recognition and Library Public Art Budget Amendment (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Library Director Skip Auld and Durham Library Foundation President Judge Willis Whichard recognized Herndon Foundation trustee Bob Bailey (alongside trustees Gus Godwin and Jack Walker) for a $100,000 donation to the Durham County Library. The Board unanimously approved a budget ordinance amendment transferring $50,000 (half of the grant) into the county budget to fund a public art installation at the new South Regional Library.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Honoring the Life of James Edward Fields Sr. (Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Page read a resolution honoring photojournalist and community access producer James Edward Fields Sr. ('Uncle Bubba Productions'), who passed away on November 24, 2008 after videotaping Board of Commissioners meetings and county events for over 23 years. Fields's son attended to accept the resolution, and speakers offered tributes in the truncated middle segment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 10A through 10M, 10O through 10Q)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved 16 consent items (pulling Item 10N for separate discussion), including Cooperative Extension grant amendments, a $30,000 Triangle United Way RBA contract, $272,006 in DSS at-risk case management funds, a $500,000 One NC pass-through grant to Quintiles Transnational Corp., the 2009 BOCC meeting schedule, resetting the Register of Deeds salary at $112,000, a $387,800 MHAworks design contract for the Criminal Justice Resource Center Phase 2 renovation, and a $3,300,000 capital amendment and $3,747,104 base construction contract with Resolute Building Company for the Southwest Regional Branch Library.

agenda_items.title: Reimbursement Resolution for Library and Civic Center Projects (Item 10N)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Ellen W. Reckhow pulled Item 10N (reimbursement resolution for South Regional Library, Southwest Library, and Civic Center projects) to urge expediting the recently approved sale of two Lowe's Grove parcels—expected to yield $1.5 million to $2 million—so proceeds can offset library COPS debt issuance since library bonds originally funded the land. The Board approved Item 10N 5-0.

agenda_items.title: 2035 Long Range Transportation Plan Options Briefing (Item 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Henry, City of Durham transportation planner and staff to the Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO, briefed the Board on the draft 2035 Long Range Transportation Plan. He explained federal fiscal-constraint requirements and reviewed major highway proposals—including widening the Durham Freeway, building the East End Connector, upgrading US-70 to a freeway toward Wake County, and widening I-85—while noting state enabling legislation would be required for new local transportation revenues.

votes.notes: Mover's name was garbled in the ASR transcript ('commission of hours'); passed by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Added a brief presentation by Robin Jacobs of the Eno River Association to the agenda following announcements.

votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('motion passes 5 0').
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted and received the November 10, 2008 Regular Session and December 1, 2008 Work Session minutes.

votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('Vote passes five to zero').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the budget ordinance amendment transferring $50,000 from the Herndon Foundation's $100,000 library gift via the Durham Library Foundation for South Regional Library public art.

votes.notes: Passed 5-0 by voice vote ('Motion carries five to zero'). The seconder was misstated in the transcript audio/ASR as duplicating the mover.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the reimbursement resolution after Vice Chair Reckhow noted that proceeds ($1.5M-$2M) from selling two Lowe's Grove parcels should be expedited to reduce library COPS debt.
